ENC-C10-B.desc: Nurses at a roadside fundraiser demonstrate the 2025 law’s projected Medicaid cuts with an adjustable display bed. They ask your crew to add testimony or move it. A volunteer shortens the mattress while keeping the pillow labelled “patient choice” impressively plump.
ENC-C10-B.choice_0: Add testimony to the nurses’ record
ENC-C10-B.log_0: You add your experience to the nurses’ record. The volunteer asks whether you prefer your feet or head outside the model’s coverage.
ENC-C10-B.log_1: You haul the bed until your arms ache. Everyone laughs when the pillow slides off. Patient choice has left the building first.

ENC-C10-C.name: Please declare your aircraft
ENC-C10-C.desc: Workers protesting their employer’s no-tip rule have built a cardboard jet after the Pentagon accepted Qatar’s plane. They flag your crew down for testimony or a hand pushing it. The wings are made from rejected gift declarations. One used to be about a biscuit.
ENC-C10-C.log_0: You record the employer’s rule and the workers’ account. The biscuit declaration includes its approximate value. Nobody has filled in cruising altitude.
ENC-C10-C.log_1: You push until your shoulder aches and the crowd cheers. A tip jar rolls down the runway in business class.

ENC-C11-A.name: The cost of the plug
ENC-C11-A.desc: Your crew stops at a public briefing on the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap. A researcher has brought itemized costs, chairs, and an unplugged freezer to explain what “overhead” pays for. The demonstration ice is providing a floor-level impact assessment.
ENC-C11-A.log_0: You verify the figures with a headache. The researcher adds electricity to the example. The ice has already submitted its objection.
ENC-C11-A.log_1: You sit and ease your sore legs. The researcher quietly plugs in a fan. Overhead immediately improves conditions for the taxpayer.
ENC-C11-A.log_2: You save the dated estimate and its proposal status. The researcher sets the papers above the puddle. That shelf is overhead too.

ENC-C11-B.name: The passport objection
ENC-C11-B.desc: At an airport print kiosk, an attendant’s demonstration distinguishes REAL ID from other acceptable identification. TSA’s $45 ConfirmID option is for travelers lacking acceptable ID, not everyone without REAL ID. A passport keeps interrupting the expensive version of the story.
ENC-C11-B.log_0: You check the examples through tired eyes and earn trust. The passport succeeds without being promoted into a state driver’s license.
ENC-C11-B.log_1: You sit and recover while the attendant explains accepted IDs. The chair conducts no additional verification of its occupant.
ENC-C11-B.log_2: You save the official distinction accurately. The attendant sets the passport beside the fee notice, giving the expensive misunderstanding a proper rival.

ENC-C11-C.name: Plug in your refund
ENC-C11-C.desc: The IRS is phasing out paper refund checks under Trump’s order, with limited exceptions. At a diner, a cook compares payment leaflets beside a phone charging from the last socket. “My refund used to arrive with its own power supply. None.” She offers you the other chair.
ENC-C11-C.log_0: You check the instructions until your head hurts. Her bank details are correct. Finding her federal refund still requires borrowing electricity from the pie warmer.
ENC-C11-C.choice_1: Sit while she compares the leaflets
ENC-C11-C.log_1: You sit and rest your legs while her phone charges. She checks the plug twice. Her federal refund has become a small appliance.
ENC-C11-C.choice_2: Save the order and useful locations
ENC-C11-C.log_2: You save the order, exceptions and nearby help locations. She adds the diner’s socket to the map. Apparently this is a Treasury branch now.

ENC-C12-A.name: Additional greatness
ENC-C12-A.desc: Trump said he got Coca-Cola to use cane sugar. The company announced an additional option, keeping its existing lineup. At a roadside cafe, the owner declares the whole soda shelf presidentially reformulated. His clerk points to the old bottles. They appear to have missed the inauguration.
ENC-C12-A.choice_0: Challenge the claim with the announcement
ENC-C12-A.log_0: You read “additional” from the company announcement until your head aches. The owner moves a new bottle in front of an old one. Reform complete.
ENC-C12-A.log_1: You repeat the claim and stop arguing. The clerk reads the old bottle’s corn-syrup ingredient. Apparently the original recipe didn’t receive the presidential memo.
ENC-C12-A.log_2: You rest outside and enjoy the quiet. Through the window, the owner poses with one new bottle blocking the shelf. National reform has a very precise camera angle.

ENC-C12-B.name: Serving suggestion
ENC-C12-B.desc: The FCC made broadband companies display prices, speeds, and data allowances. At a truck-stop Wi-Fi desk, an attendant puts the provider’s label beside a coffee tin and invites your comparison. Both list contents. Only one currently delivers a hot product.
ENC-C12-B.choice_0: Compare the terms with the attendant
ENC-C12-B.log_0: You untangle the introductory rate and earn trust, mentally tired. The cheap price has a shorter shelf life than the coffee.
ENC-C12-B.choice_1: Agree the label guarantees fast service
ENC-C12-B.log_1: The simple answer comforts you but costs credibility. The attendant points out that listing speed does not manufacture it.
ENC-C12-B.log_2: You rest and feel better. The coatroom supplies exactly the silence advertised, with no introductory period.

ENC-C12-C.name: Total, plus the rest
ENC-C12-C.desc: The FTC now requires mandatory lodging fees in the upfront price. At a roadside motel, the owner shows you his “honest” quote: $79 for the room, plus a mandatory $40 service charge. He has made the word honest enormous. The total is still hiding.
ENC-C12-C.choice_0: Explain the quote to the lobby
ENC-C12-C.log_0: You explain that the required upfront total is $119. Your head aches. The owner asks whether the FTC will accept $79 in a more sincere font.
ENC-C12-C.choice_1: Repeat that the room is only $79
ENC-C12-C.log_1: You praise the price and stop arguing. He announces that an independent traveler has verified it. Your endorsement is the first thing he hasn’t charged extra for.
ENC-C12-C.log_2: You rest in the van. It has no resort fee. It apologizes for the missing resort.

ENC-C13-A.name: Airport-ready feet
ENC-C13-A.desc: TSA ended routine shoes-off screening in July 2025. At a roadside shoe shop, a cobbler is labeling every pair “Airport Ready.” He offers $8 to check the size tags, or the announcement to read. His entire stock has achieved federal reform without moving a sole.
ENC-C13-A.log_0: He compares the old routine with the announcement. You learn the change and laugh. Washington has finally approved keeping the shoe around the foot.
ENC-C13-A.choice_1: Use your paper; record the change
ENC-C13-A.log_1: You use some paper to record the rule and its screening exceptions. No special shoe is required. You underline that before the cobbler invents a surcharge.
ENC-C13-A.log_2: You check the sizes, settle the labels and collect $8. The cobbler unveils his airport-ready slippers. Their security upgrade appears to be remaining slippers.

ENC-C13-B.name: A very exclusive lunch
ENC-C13-B.desc: After Trump’s Signal scandal, a catering depot offers your crew $8 to check a practice delivery list. The depot is holding a public demonstration of its new recipient checks. The boss has three forms for a sandwich. A defence secretary apparently needed fewer.
ENC-C13-B.log_0: You learn the checking process, laughing when the dispatcher verifies the pickle’s recipient. Nobody can accuse lunch of operating without oversight.
ENC-C13-B.choice_1: Use your paper; record the checks
ENC-C13-B.log_1: You spend some supplies recording the demonstration. Every sandwich reaches its intended recipient. The dispatcher is available for national emergencies after lunch.
ENC-C13-B.log_2: You earn $8 and clear up the list. The unknown recipient is removed before receiving anything more explosive than mustard.

ENC-C13-C.name: A larger territory than the bread
ENC-C13-C.desc: The FTC dropped its appeals defending a nationwide noncompete rule. At a bakery, a clerk compares the boss’s proposed job restriction with the delivery map and offers $8 to check address markers. The bread travels a modest distance. The boss’s ambitions for former workers go farther.
ENC-C13-C.choice_0: Hear how the proposed restriction works
ENC-C13-C.log_0: You learn the distinction and enjoy the clerk’s comparison. The bakery’s market area is apparently smaller than its desired authority over people.
ENC-C13-C.choice_1: Use your paper; document the two maps
ENC-C13-C.log_1: You record the proposed restriction and surviving legal limits accurately. The clerk keeps the delivery route separate from the boss’s territorial aspirations.
ENC-C13-C.log_2: You earn $8 and enjoy sorting out the map. The bread’s route becomes clear without inventing a legal claim over everyone nearby.

ENC-C14-A.name: Break-room government
ENC-C14-A.desc: Your hot, aching crew stops beside a travelling roofers’ protest against Florida’s ban on local heat mandates. Volunteers have shade and towels but need water. Their display shows a politician praising freedom from regulation beneath an umbrella held by somebody else.
ENC-C14-A.log_0: You use some water and recover in the shade. The volunteer wrings out a towel. Individual responsibility has soaked the bucket.
ENC-C14-A.log_1: You record the Florida rule and the roofers’ account. The display’s politician has a permanent parasol; everyone else has a shift rota.
ENC-C14-A.log_2: You leave some water for the workers. A roofer pours it into the cooler without first checking whether the county approved compassion.

ENC-C14-B.name: Count the fingers
ENC-C14-B.desc: A volunteer first-aider from Nebraska tends a roadside repair fair. Her state’s paid-sick-time mandate starts at eleven employees; her garage has ten. She offers basic care using your supplies. The boss likes a workforce he can count without taking off a shoe.
ENC-C14-B.choice_0: Use your supplies for basic first aid
ENC-C14-B.log_0: You provide supplies and recover. The first-aider treats your ache without asking whether enough coworkers are standing beside you.
ENC-C14-B.log_1: You record the state threshold accurately. The first-aider counts ten coworkers on her fingers, then points at the conspicuously missing eleventh.
ENC-C14-B.choice_2: Leave supplies at the first-aid table
ENC-C14-B.log_2: You leave some supplies. She adds them to the kit without demanding that the kit first acquire a larger workforce.

ENC-C14-C.name: The reverse button
ENC-C14-C.desc: At a game café, an attendant reads the FTC’s 2025 Fortnite refund announcement for unwanted purchases. She offers your tired crew a quiet booth and accepts refreshment donations. Buying the costume took one button; undoing it required Washington.
ENC-C14-C.choice_0: Use your food; take a proper break
ENC-C14-C.log_0: You eat and recover in the booth. The attendant points out that resting still works without buying a decorative chair.
ENC-C14-C.log_1: You record the unwanted-purchase case accurately. The attendant approves: imaginary armor should at least require real permission to buy.
ENC-C14-C.choice_2: Leave some food for the break table
ENC-C14-C.log_2: You leave some food. The attendant keeps it beside the controllers, where taking a biscuit requires a deliberate human movement.

ENC-C15-A.name: Bread without a secretary
ENC-C15-A.desc: At a roadside food swap, a baker explains California’s ban on consumer-facing sell-by dates for covered new products. She offers fresh bread and welcomes shared lunch. Her old labels advised the store manager. The person buying the food was expected to overhear.
ENC-C15-A.log_0: You record which dates concern quality and which concern safety. The baker retires a label that spent its whole career talking to management.
ENC-C15-A.choice_1: Take some fresh food for the road
ENC-C15-A.log_1: You accept the fresh food. For once, its information is intended for the person who will actually eat it.
ENC-C15-A.choice_2: Share some food; join the lunch
ENC-C15-A.log_2: You share food and enjoy lunch. The baker turns the old store-facing label around so it can finally join a conversation with customers.

ENC-C15-B.name: Multiple-choice patriotism
ENC-C15-B.desc: A PTA picnic is discussing a local board’s response to Trump’s anti-indoctrination order. Parents welcome your crew and your D.C. story. The board’s sample history quiz gives four answers: proud, very proud, extremely proud, and see the principal.
ENC-C15-B.log_0: You record the parents’ examples and laugh at the quiz. A history teacher writes the date in the margin. It wasn’t an option.
ENC-C15-B.choice_1: Accept some food for the road
ENC-C15-B.log_1: You take some food. The volunteer asks whether you enjoyed it. For the first time today, “could use salt” is an acceptable answer.
ENC-C15-B.choice_2: Share some food with the parents
ENC-C15-B.log_2: You share some food and join the table. Someone quizzes the potato salad on national greatness. It declines to commit without a spoon.

ENC-C15-C.name: Food for the footnotes
ENC-C15-C.desc: A library supper is checking the nonexistent citations from the first MAHA report. Volunteers welcome your crew’s D.C. account and offer food for the road. The librarian has left empty chairs for the imaginary authors. They’ve shown more restraint at the buffet than anyone.
ENC-C15-C.log_0: You save the corrected account and enjoy the librarian’s presentation. She thanks the absent authors. Their contribution takes exactly as long as expected.
ENC-C15-C.choice_1: Take some food for the road
ENC-C15-C.log_1: You collect some food. The librarian cancels the imaginary authors’ reservations. At last, the missing research produces something you can use.
ENC-C15-C.choice_2: Share some food at the supper
ENC-C15-C.log_2: You share some food and join the laughter. Someone sets a place for the peer reviewer. It’s an untouched pair of glasses.

ENC-C16-A.name: The bin was not consulted
ENC-C16-A.desc: After the SEC’s Keurig recyclability case, a café worker is checking the claims on old display material before clearing a cupboard. Materials are welcome; hauling boxes earns food. The corporate report approved the pod’s journey. The recycling company had other plans.
ENC-C16-A.log_0: Your supplies earn the worker’s endorsement. The replacement display leaves room for the inconvenient detail of what local collectors actually accept.
ENC-C16-A.choice_1: Haul the boxes for some food
ENC-C16-A.log_1: You earn food and sore shoulders. The old sales display reaches its proper destination without relying on the claims printed on it.

ENC-C16-B.name: A fresh coat of America
ENC-C16-B.desc: A boat club following Trump’s Gulf renaming needs supplies or hands to move its new visitor signs. They flag down your van and offer some food for lifting. The volunteer has painted the word “America” over a rust hole. Daylight is still getting through.
ENC-C16-B.log_0: You donate some supplies; the club records your help. The volunteer patches the hole. America finally stops whistling in the wind.
ENC-C16-B.choice_1: Move the signs for some food
ENC-C16-B.log_1: You earn some food and aching arms moving the signs. The old name underneath is doing most of the structural work.

ENC-C16-C.name: Special custody for phones
ENC-C16-C.desc: Virginia’s bell-to-bell school-phone guidance has inspired a library supply drive. A volunteer welcomes donated materials or offers food for hauling books before her demonstration. Phones get individual soft pouches. The dictionaries are sharing a wheelbarrow with a squeaky wheel.
ENC-C16-C.choice_0: Donate materials to the supply drive
ENC-C16-C.log_0: Your contribution earns the volunteer’s endorsement. She pads the book cart too, briefly extending the dignity already available to every phone.
ENC-C16-C.choice_1: Haul the books for some food
ENC-C16-C.log_1: You earn food and sore shoulders. The dictionaries arrive together without individual pouches, somehow retaining all their distracting information.

ENC-C17-A.name: The bread has appointments
ENC-C17-A.desc: A grocer shows you California’s new law separating food quality dates from safety dates. Her picnic table welcomes travelers and donated supplies. A loaf carries three old date phrases. Apparently bread used to need a personal secretary.
ENC-C17-A.choice_0: Donate some supplies to the picnic
ENC-C17-A.log_0: Your contribution earns a grateful endorsement. The grocer adds a simple description: food, available now, no appointment necessary.
ENC-C17-A.log_1: You settle into the quiet shade. The loaf may have a complicated schedule; for once, you do not.

ENC-C17-B.name: A house, actual size
ENC-C17-B.desc: Trump ordered limits on federal support for big investors buying single-family homes, with definitions still to come. At a neighborhood open-house picnic, a cleaner offers a quiet seat and accepts food donations. The house is smaller than the bidder’s corporate family.
ENC-C17-B.choice_0: Donate some food to the picnic
ENC-C17-B.log_0: Your food earns the neighbors’ endorsement. A tray fits through the doorway without requiring anyone to define a large institutional sandwich.
ENC-C17-B.log_1: You sit and clear your head. For ten minutes, the kitchen serves a person who has no acquisition strategy.

ENC-C17-C.name: Already paid to know
ENC-C17-C.desc: At a library rest stop, a volunteer opens a newly accessible NIH-funded manuscript. Since July 2025, covered new manuscripts no longer wait through a publication embargo. Supplies help maintain the reading nook. Taxpayers financed the research; the second entrance fee has finally disappeared.
ENC-C17-C.choice_0: Donate supplies to the reading nook
ENC-C17-C.log_0: Your supplies earn the volunteer’s endorsement. Someone can now read publicly funded work while sitting on a chair supplied by the public.
ENC-C17-C.log_1: You read and clear your head. The paper opens without asking whether your curiosity has a premium subscription.

ENC-C18-A.name: The approved stairs
ENC-C18-A.desc: Parents invite your crew to a fourth-floor meeting about their board’s response to Trump’s anti-indoctrination order. The lift is broken. The proposed lesson teaches that complaining weakens the nation. The staircase offers several opportunities to test the curriculum.
ENC-C18-A.log_0: You climb and argue the sourced case, legs and head aching. The board asks for a more positive account of the stairs.
ENC-C18-A.choice_1: Walk with parents to their picnic
ENC-C18-A.log_1: You take the hilly route, legs sore but spirits lifted. A parent marks the broken lift absent. It receives full credit for patriotism.
ENC-C18-A.log_2: You leave with a quieter head and no testimony to offer. The board’s attendance sheet has discovered another supporter of the current arrangement.

ENC-C18-B.name: One biscuit, four flights
ENC-C18-B.desc: Hotel workers invite your stopped crew to an upstairs meeting about their employer’s ban on guest gifts. They’re comparing a confiscated biscuit with the Pentagon’s Qatari jet. The lift is reserved for management. The biscuit has been allowed to use it as evidence.
ENC-C18-B.log_0: You climb and record the gift rule, legs and head aching. The biscuit arrives by lift in a sealed management envelope.
ENC-C18-B.choice_1: Walk with workers to their picnic
ENC-C18-B.log_1: You hike to the workers’ picnic, sore but laughing. Someone offers you a biscuit. It completes the journey without diplomatic clearance.
ENC-C18-B.log_2: You leave with a quieter head but no worker account. The gift comparison continues upstairs. The biscuit is apparently an excellent witness.

ENC-C18-C.name: Publicly excluded
ENC-C18-C.desc: At a roadside hall, residents invite your crew to a standing-room meeting about officials sharing Yemen strike details in Signal. Public questions must be handwritten, checked, and submitted upstairs. A volunteer has already lost the pencil. It has better access than the audience.
ENC-C18-C.log_0: You stand and argue through the procedure, feet and head aching. Your question reaches the table. They announce it needs a second copy.
ENC-C18-C.choice_1: Walk with residents around the lake
ENC-C18-C.log_1: You walk the long lakeside path, legs sore but spirits lifted. A resident reads the question to a duck. It acknowledges receipt immediately.
ENC-C18-C.log_2: You leave with a clearer head and no public question recorded. The blank submission tray is praised for its responsible handling of information.

ENC-D01-A.name: The lunch threat
ENC-D01-A.desc: At a diner, a trans driver reads May 2026’s counterterrorism strategy targeting violent groups described as “radically pro-transgender.” On TV, a pundit drops “violent.” The driver closes his lunch cooler. “There goes my weapons inspection.”
ENC-D01-A.choice_0: Use paper; save the actual wording
ENC-D01-A.log_0: You use some paper to save the wording, head pounding. The driver opens lunch slowly. Apparently mayonnaise now needs witnesses.
ENC-D01-A.log_1: The simple version clears your head and gets the facts wrong. The driver’s lunch has somehow become a summit.
ENC-D01-A.choice_2: Say all trans people were designated
ENC-D01-A.log_2: He says no: the strategy does not designate all trans people. The pundit has already booked a second expert on sandwiches.

ENC-D01-B.name: White, rye, or counsel
ENC-D01-B.desc: At a Pentagon-adjacent sandwich counter, a reporter shows March 2026’s revised press rules after a court struck parts down. The memo says asking questions isn’t criminal. The cashier asks white or rye. Three people check whether he’s credentialed.
ENC-D01-B.choice_0: Use paper; save the actual memo
ENC-D01-B.log_0: You use paper to save the memo, head pounding. The cashier repeats the bread options slowly, as though negotiating access to a submarine.
ENC-D01-B.choice_1: Accept that the dispute is settled
ENC-D01-B.log_1: You relax at the reassurance. The reporter corrects you: revised rules don’t settle every dispute. The sandwich still awaits clearance.
ENC-D01-B.log_2: The reporter corrects you: the memo expressly says asking questions isn’t criminal. The cashier courageously reveals the existence of mustard.

ENC-D01-C.name: Your call is medically important
ENC-D01-C.desc: At a diner, an off-duty nurse asks your crew to document her hospital's response to CMS withdrawing emergency-abortion guidance: a legal hotline. She's testing it over breakfast. The waitress brings the phone its own menu. It's been here longer than anyone.
ENC-D01-C.choice_0: Use your paper; document the delay
ENC-D01-C.log_0: You use some supplies to save the timed account, head aching. The waitress clears breakfast around the phone. It has qualified for lunch.
ENC-D01-C.log_1: The recorded reassurance settles your head until the nurse explains it approves nothing. The waitress asks whether the recording wants its usual.
ENC-D01-C.choice_2: Say federal law requires this hotline
ENC-D01-C.log_2: The nurse corrects you: the hospital invented the hotline. The waitress takes back its menu. House guests aren't federal officials.

ENC-D02-A.name: The house is still at large
ENC-D02-A.desc: Outside a courthouse, a volunteer asks your crew to help carry returned belongings. Her client was arrested after a miscarriage; the charges were dropped. Police kept the woman's house keys as evidence. Apparently her front door was an accessory.
ENC-D02-A.choice_0: Use some water; rest in shade
ENC-D02-A.log_0: You drink some water and recover in the shade. The volunteer checks the returned keys. The house is still at large.
ENC-D02-A.log_1: You scrape your arms carrying the box. The volunteer checks its contents twice. An apology wasn't among the items police returned.
ENC-D02-A.choice_2: Share water; record the property delay
ENC-D02-A.log_2: You share some water and record the arrest, dismissal and property delay. The volunteer turns the key. The door declines to resist release.

ENC-D02-B.name: The roof remains eligible
ENC-D02-B.desc: A school gym’s equipment sale draws you inside. The coach explains Trump’s sports order uses federal funding to exclude trans girls from girls’ teams. A leak drips onto the basketballs. Washington located the girl. Nobody located a roofer.
ENC-D02-B.choice_0: Use food and water; take a break
ENC-D02-B.log_0: You use some food and water for a break, recovering. The coach moves a bucket. The roof remains eligible for every team.
ENC-D02-B.choice_1: Shift equipment away from the leak
ENC-D02-B.log_1: You strain yourself shifting equipment out of the leak. The coach adds another bucket. It passes eligibility without a hearing.
ENC-D02-B.log_2: You give paper and tape for a notice quoting the actual order. Above it, the leak continues its undefeated season.

ENC-D02-C.name: An active workplace
ENC-D02-C.desc: At a nursing-home rummage sale, an aide points to federal staffing minimums repealed in February 2026. Older requirements remain. The administrator is selling extra chairs. His plan for keeping everybody on their feet is proceeding beautifully.
ENC-D02-C.log_0: You use food and water to rest and recover. The aide sits briefly. The chair demonstrates a suspiciously affordable retention strategy.
ENC-D02-C.log_1: You strain yourself moving chairs. The administrator calls this proof fewer seats encourage activity. The aide offers him the heaviest one.
ENC-D02-C.log_2: You give paper and tape for an accurate notice. The aide adds the older requirements. The administrator’s uncluttered wall becomes less efficient.

ENC-D03-A.name: Tell the airbags
ENC-D03-A.desc: At a rest stop, a trans Kansas driver shows the replacement license the state required. Same driver. Same car. Different sex marker. He asks whether he needs to notify the airbags.
ENC-D03-A.choice_0: Use paper; save the law’s scope
ENC-D03-A.log_0: You use paper to save the law’s actual scope. He puts the new card away. The camera still remembers who it photographed.
ENC-D03-A.log_1: You share lunch and laugh. His car unlocks without consulting his birth certificate. Even the door recognizes him.
ENC-D03-A.log_2: You clear your head on a quiet bench. He adjusts the driver’s seat. It still has the same opinion of his legs.

ENC-D03-B.name: The toaster has a floor
ENC-D03-B.desc: At a thrift store, a visiting disabled worker shows July 2025’s abandoned federal phaseout of subminimum-wage certificates. His employer uses one where state law permits. Here, the donated toaster enjoys a firm minimum price.
ENC-D03-B.choice_0: Use paper; save the federal rule
ENC-D03-B.log_0: You use paper to save the federal rule. He turns the toaster over. Even secondhand appliances receive a proper valuation.
ENC-D03-B.log_1: You share lunch and laugh. He checks the toaster’s warranty. Lasting thirty days apparently earns more confidence than working every weekday.
ENC-D03-B.log_2: You take a quiet break. The cashier refuses a lower offer for the toaster. Some labor-saving devices must never be undervalued.

ENC-D03-C.name: Roadworthy, pending counsel
ENC-D03-C.desc: At a motel breakfast, adult volunteers review Idaho's restrictions on concealed abortion assistance to unemancipated minors. They ask your crew to record the public facts for D.C. Their car passed its inspection. The route needs a lawyer. The lawyer doesn't do roadside assistance.
ENC-D03-C.choice_0: Use your paper; record the limits
ENC-D03-C.log_0: You use some supplies to save the minor-specific limits. The driver files the car's clean inspection beside the questions keeping it parked.
ENC-D03-C.choice_1: Share food with the planning volunteers
ENC-D03-C.log_1: You share some food and enjoy lunch together. The lawyer unrolls the route papers. The driver puts the bread basket on them. Lunch proceeds.
ENC-D03-C.choice_2: Read quietly on the motel porch
ENC-D03-C.log_2: You clear your head on the porch. The car wears a cheerful roadworthy sticker. Its driver is still inside, qualifying the journey.

ENC-D04-A.name: Small government, large pants
ENC-D04-A.desc: At an outdoor shop, a trans hunting-club treasurer shows you ATF’s proposed birth-sex rule for its forms. The owner wants Washington out of his gun cabinet. He is considerably more flexible about somebody else’s pants.
ENC-D04-A.log_0: You check the proposal’s limits. The owner hides his sales ledger when you glance at it. Certain personal details are sacred.
ENC-D04-A.log_1: You save the notice, head aching. The owner locks his office. His small-government tour has reached its border.
ENC-D04-A.log_2: The treasurer corrects you: this proposal does not ban all trans gun owners. The owner still pats his cabinet protectively.

ENC-D04-B.name: Housing, with a lock
ENC-D04-B.desc: At a camping shop, an outreach worker reads Trump’s July 2025 order promoting broader civil commitment through legal and funding changes. It isn’t automatic confinement. The display tent has three bedrooms. Her clients keep getting offered plans with locks.
ENC-D04-B.choice_0: Read what the order actually directs
ENC-D04-B.log_0: You check the order’s limits. The worker measures the display tent. It remains the most detailed housing proposal in the room.
ENC-D04-B.log_1: You save the order, head aching. The salesman demonstrates a zipper from the inside. Choosing when to leave appears to be a feature.
ENC-D04-B.choice_2: Call it automatic confinement for everyone
ENC-D04-B.log_2: The worker corrects you: legal processes and criteria still matter. The government’s sweeping announcement came with much smaller print.

ENC-D04-C.name: The purpose of a sandwich
ENC-D04-C.desc: A Texas volunteer at a roadside café asks your crew to check SB33: public abortion-travel assistance includes food. The café owner is preparing a city-convention catering bid. He holds up one sandwich. Apparently he needs to know where it plans to go after lunch.
ENC-D04-C.log_0: You verify the limits. The owner puts the sandwich beside his catering forms. It qualifies for public money by staying vague about its itinerary.
ENC-D04-C.log_1: You save the provision, head aching. The owner cuts the sandwich diagonally. It has changed direction without resolving its funding status.
ENC-D04-C.choice_2: Post that private food donations are banned
ENC-D04-C.log_2: The volunteer corrects you: SB33 targets public assistance. The owner removes your claim from the table before it frightens the bread.

ENC-D05-A.name: A lifetime warranty
ENC-D05-A.desc: A visiting Louisiana nurse asks your crew to time a cabinet lock at a hardware store. State controls now secure misoprostol, also used to stop bleeding. The salesman offers a lifetime warranty. She would settle for getting it open before closing.
ENC-D05-A.choice_0: Check the rule and reported delays
ENC-D05-A.log_0: You verify the rule and reported delays, head aching. The salesman offers another key. The nurse asks whether it comes with another afternoon.
ENC-D05-A.log_1: You clear your head by the garden supplies. The salesman demonstrates a watering can. Its contents escape without finding a supervisor.
ENC-D05-A.choice_2: Say the medicine is completely banned
ENC-D05-A.log_2: The simple story settles your head until she corrects it: valid prescribing remains lawful. The salesman resumes wrestling with the lawful cabinet.

ENC-D05-B.name: The phone plan stays
ENC-D05-B.desc: At a pharmacy café, a parent reads the Medicaid and CHIP youth transition-care exclusions due October 13, 2026. Some existing hormone care gets up to six extra months. Her teenager keeps growing. The phone plan renews automatically.
ENC-D05-B.choice_0: Read the dates and funding limits
ENC-D05-B.log_0: You check the dates and exceptions, head aching. The phone company has committed to her longer than the benefits department.
ENC-D05-B.log_1: You clear your head by the window. Her phone renews with a cheerful ping. Apparently continuity is available as an add-on.
ENC-D05-B.choice_2: Use the headline; take a break
ENC-D05-B.log_2: The short version feels manageable until she corrects it: funding exclusions, not a ban on all care. Your certainty expires first.

ENC-D05-C.name: Still part of the family
ENC-D05-C.desc: A retired municipal worker at a diner shows June 2025’s Supreme Court ruling limiting disabled retirees’ employment-discrimination claims. Other protections remain. His old workplace still calls him family. Benefits would like to know whether he’s currently employed by this family.
ENC-D05-C.log_0: You read the job-holding limits, head aching. His retirement photograph has room for everybody except the person calculating the benefits.
ENC-D05-C.log_1: You take a quiet break. He folds the workplace-family brochure into a coaster. It finally supports something.
ENC-D05-C.log_2: You trust the warm brochure and relax. He corrects your legal summary. The family reunion has an eligibility date.

ENC-D06-A.name: The federal wardrobe case
ENC-D06-A.desc: At a post office, a woman explains how June 2026’s court order restored her trans sister’s care and clothing in federal prison. She needs a stamp. Her sister needed a federal judge to get dressed.
ENC-D06-A.choice_0: Read and save the public ruling
ENC-D06-A.log_0: You save the ruling, head aching. Her sister’s care needed a judge. The postage merely wants money.
ENC-D06-A.choice_1: Give paper for the public order
ENC-D06-A.log_1: You give paper for the public order; her sister’s details stay private. The wardrobe dispute has grown another stack of stationery.
ENC-D06-A.log_2: You clear your head outside. She seals the envelope. Ordinary glue remains one of the few accommodations requiring no litigation.

ENC-D06-B.name: A cleaner angle
ENC-D06-B.desc: At a hardware counter, a power-plant neighbor reads EPA’s February 2026 repeal of stronger mercury and toxic-metal rules. Older limits survive. The salesman makes a dirty demonstration filter look cleaner by turning it around. Government innovation travels fast.
ENC-D06-B.choice_0: Read and save the remaining limits
ENC-D06-B.log_0: You save the remaining limits and repealed requirements, head aching. The salesman turns the filter back. The dirt declines to renegotiate.
ENC-D06-B.choice_1: Use paper for an accurate notice
ENC-D06-B.log_1: You use paper for an accurate notice. The neighbor draws the filter’s dirty side. The salesman calls it an unfair angle.
ENC-D06-B.log_2: You clear your head outside. Through the window, the same filter is enjoying a second immaculate face.

ENC-D06-C.name: The complimentary lullaby
ENC-D06-C.desc: At a rest stop, an Alabama couple asks your crew to check the embryo ruling and later IVF-clinic immunity law. Their own insurance excludes IVF. The agent on speaker calls children priceless. He has priced everything required to have one.
ENC-D06-C.choice_0: Check and save the legal distinction
ENC-D06-C.log_0: You save the ruling and immunity limits, head aching. The agent congratulates them on the embryos' status. They ask where to redeem it.
ENC-D06-C.choice_1: Use your paper; copy the limits
ENC-D06-C.log_1: You use some supplies to copy the limits. They fold the agent's smiling-baby brochure over the exclusions. The baby is sitting on the bill.
ENC-D06-C.choice_2: Leave the call for some quiet
ENC-D06-C.log_2: You clear your head away from the call. The hold music plays a lullaby. The couple has been receiving it for free.

ENC-D07-A.name: Rewards for coming back empty
ENC-D07-A.desc: A traveler at a rest stop asks your crew to check Arizona's emergency-contraception refusal rule. The pharmacy returned her prescription, as required. It also offered a loyalty card. She holds them side by side. They are building a lasting relationship with the paper.
ENC-D07-A.choice_0: Check and save the actual rule
ENC-D07-A.log_0: You save the refusal-and-return rule, clearing the confusion. She folds the loyalty card around the prescription. It finally supports contraception.
ENC-D07-A.log_1: She corrects you: the law permits specified refusals. She hasn't come this far to collect another person saying no.
ENC-D07-A.choice_2: Use your paper; copy the limits
ENC-D07-A.log_2: You use some supplies to copy the limits. She tucks them into the loyalty-card sleeve. The free gift finally contains useful information.

ENC-D07-B.name: The invisible emergency
ENC-D07-B.desc: At a copy shop, a trans mechanic reads Social Security’s June 2026 rule: its sex field can only be changed to reflect sex at birth. It isn’t printed on the card. Washington has discovered his most urgent component: invisible paperwork.
ENC-D07-B.log_0: You save the rule and clear up the confusion. He holds the card to the light. Still no sex field. Tremendous progress.
ENC-D07-B.log_1: He corrects you and covers the personal details. The blank space remains flawless. The federal government has defended it at considerable length.
ENC-D07-B.choice_2: Use paper for the public rule
ENC-D07-B.log_2: You use your paper for the public rule. He puts it beside the card. The invisible field now requires visible luggage.

ENC-D07-C.name: The website gets an extension
ENC-D07-C.desc: At a library printer, a low-vision resident reads DOJ’s April 2026 extension of government-web accessibility deadlines into 2027 and 2028. Existing access duties remain. Her appointment confirmation is due today. The website has successfully requested an accommodation.
ENC-D07-C.log_0: You save the deadlines and clear up the confusion. Her appointment still needs confirming. Only the website has been excused from showing up.
ENC-D07-C.choice_1: Assume all access duties are suspended
ENC-D07-C.log_1: She corrects you: existing access duties remain. The government gave its website more time, not permission to stop being a government.
ENC-D07-C.choice_2: Use paper for a large-type copy
ENC-D07-C.log_2: You use paper for a large-type public notice. She checks the dates. Enlarging the words proves considerably faster than enlarging the deadline.

ENC-D08-A.name: Two functioning arms
ENC-D08-A.desc: At a pregnancy center's open house, a nurse asks your crew to check its ads against Massachusetts's warnings about misleading centers. The manager offers a 'medical volunteer' badge for carrying a sandwich board. The qualifications are two functioning arms. The center offers no abortion referrals.
ENC-D08-A.choice_0: Use your paper; check the services
ENC-D08-A.log_0: You use some supplies to check the missing services, head pounding. The manager offers a lab coat. Apparently it covers the gaps.
ENC-D08-A.choice_1: Carry the sign; endorse the center
ENC-D08-A.log_1: You scrape your shin and relax into the pitch. The nurse corrects your endorsement: no abortion referrals. Your badge doesn't cover that either.
ENC-D08-A.log_2: You leave with a quieter head and no checked account. The manager hangs your unused badge on the sandwich board. Staffing restored.

ENC-D08-B.name: Family first, calendar later
ENC-D08-B.desc: At a union-hall table sale, a worker shows May 2025’s ruling removing certain abortion accommodations from the federal pregnancy-workplace rule. Medical-treatment exceptions remain. A manager selling “FAMILY FIRST” mugs promises unlimited time off, provided time stops first.
ENC-D08-B.choice_0: Use paper; check the actual limits
ENC-D08-B.log_0: You save the actual limits using paper, drained. The manager removes the clock batteries. His generous leave policy is nearly operational.
ENC-D08-B.log_1: The simple promise clears your head. You strain yourself stacking tables, then learn the manager’s unlimited leave exists only on mugs.
ENC-D08-B.choice_2: Skip the details; take a break
ENC-D08-B.log_2: You relax, then repeat that every pregnancy protection vanished. The worker corrects you. The mug is still the least complicated witness.

ENC-D08-C.name: Same water, happier label
ENC-D08-C.desc: At a water-filter shop, a utility worker reads EPA’s May 2026 proposals to drop some PFAS limits and extend certain deadlines. Nothing is final. The salesman presents two identical demonstration samples. One has a much more optimistic label.
ENC-D08-C.choice_0: Use paper; check the actual proposals
ENC-D08-C.log_0: You use paper to save the proposals, drained. The salesman swaps the labels. The samples achieve an immediate regulatory breakthrough.
ENC-D08-C.choice_1: Trust him; help carry display boxes
ENC-D08-C.log_1: His assurance clears your head. You strain yourself carrying boxes before the worker corrects his claims. The optimism weighs more than advertised.
ENC-D08-C.choice_2: Take the headline; take a break
ENC-D08-C.log_2: You relax, then describe the proposals as final. The worker corrects you. The salesman has already printed the victory stickers.

ENC-D09-A.name: Reserved for the return trip
ENC-D09-A.desc: Your crew stops at a hospital's public meeting about losing maternity services. A volunteer shows the national maternity-care desert report. The county commissioner unveils reserved parking for new mothers. From those spaces, it's a long drive to somewhere they can become one.
ENC-D09-A.choice_0: Check the closure and remaining services
ENC-D09-A.log_0: You check the closure and remaining services, head aching. The commissioner measures the parking bay. The route to a delivery ward won't fit.
ENC-D09-A.choice_1: Take a quiet look at the garden
ENC-D09-A.log_1: You clear your head in the garden. The commissioner tests the parking ribbon again. It is the only local delivery he has scheduled.
ENC-D09-A.log_2: You nap and miss the community account. The commissioner posts his parking photograph, cropped just above the shuttered maternity windows.

ENC-D09-B.name: The cheaper repair
ENC-D09-B.desc: At a phone-repair counter, a youth volunteer revises referral cards: the specialized LGBTQ+ option within 988 closed July 17, 2025; the general line remains. Washington called it ending separate services. The clerk calls removing buttons a cheaper repair.
ENC-D09-B.choice_0: Check the agency and operator notices
ENC-D09-B.log_0: You check both notices, head aching. The clerk points at a phone missing a button. It also serves everyone equally now.
ENC-D09-B.log_1: You clear your head outside. The clerk is still waiting to hear how fewer specialists became a larger welcome.
ENC-D09-B.log_2: You nap, then repeat that 988 closed. The volunteer corrects you. Your shortcut has disconnected the service that remains.

ENC-D09-C.name: A longer planning horizon
ENC-D09-C.desc: At a rest-area picnic table, a Women’s Health Initiative participant shows April 2025’s funding cancellation and May’s reversal. The study continued. She’s kept appointments for decades. Her bagged salad has a longer planning horizon than Washington.
ENC-D09-C.log_0: You check the timeline, head aching. She puts the cancellation under her salad container. It has finally helped preserve something.
ENC-D09-C.log_1: You clear your head on a quiet bench. She checks next year’s appointment. The salad is the only thing legitimately expiring.
ENC-D09-C.log_2: You nap and repeat that the study closed. She corrects you. Your obituary arrived before her next appointment reminder.

ENC-D10-A.name: Freedom at whisper volume
ENC-D10-A.desc: While you price copies, a trans warehouse worker reads EEOC’s January 2026 decision rescinding harassment guidance. Discrimination law survives. A supervisor asks whether he can say anything now. The clerk switches on the security microphone.
ENC-D10-A.choice_0: Use paper; save the agency statement
ENC-D10-A.log_0: You use paper to save the agency’s statement. The supervisor lowers his voice. Remarkable how quickly clarification improves working conditions.
ENC-D10-A.log_1: You wait by the door and clear your head. The supervisor tests a whisper. His new freedom requires very little volume.
ENC-D10-A.log_2: The worker corrects you: the law remains. The supervisor asks if the camera records sound. His confidence needs terms and conditions.

ENC-D10-B.name: The crayon checkpoint
ENC-D10-B.desc: At a school-supply sale, a Head Start volunteer shows the September 2025 injunction stopping Washington’s attempted immigration restrictions on the program. The policy remains unenforced. A box of crayons has survived its promotion to border-control equipment.
ENC-D10-B.choice_0: Use paper; save the court notice
ENC-D10-B.log_0: You use paper to save the injunction. The volunteer opens the crayon box. Every color got in without a background check.
ENC-D10-B.log_1: You clear your head outside. The volunteer returns to sorting crayons. Her original job has survived another attempt to make it something else.
ENC-D10-B.choice_2: Trust the headline about new checks
ENC-D10-B.log_2: The volunteer corrects you: the injunction blocks the Head Start restriction. The crayons have already returned to their previous profession.

ENC-D10-C.name: The wrong door needs a lock
ENC-D10-C.desc: After reports of police using Flock to follow ex-partners, a hardware shop advertises extra door locks. A customer offers the public investigation report. The salesman recommends another deadbolt. She asks whether it fits a police database.
ENC-D10-C.choice_0: Share food; check the public report
ENC-D10-C.log_0: You share food and preserve the findings. The shop has seventeen locks for a door and none for authorized curiosity.
ENC-D10-C.choice_1: Take a break by the key rack
ENC-D10-C.log_1: Your head clears by the key rack. Every ordinary key has teeth; the safeguards in the brochure appear to be decorative.
ENC-D10-C.log_2: You endorse the brochure. She turns it over: a warranty for the camera, nothing for the person underneath.

ENC-D11-A.name: The atlas answers first
ENC-D11-A.desc: At a rest stop, a Minnesota legal volunteer offers directions while reading March 2026’s Whipple order requiring private legal calls and transfer safeguards. Her atlas finds every town. Finding a detained client took a federal judge.
ENC-D11-A.log_0: Her direct route recovers time and clears your head. The atlas locates you without requiring three phone calls and a court order.
ENC-D11-A.log_1: The gentler route regains some time and lifts the mood. She waves goodbye. Nobody needs permission to tell you where you are.

ENC-D11-B.name: Directions, not a statement
ENC-D11-B.desc: At a truck-stop counter, a camera promoter calls Texas’s abortion-related Flock search a welfare check. The cashier keeps the released investigation summary beside the road maps. She separates them: one tells you where to go; the other demands an explanation.
ENC-D11-B.choice_0: Use the cashier’s direct road map
ENC-D11-B.log_0: You follow her public-road directions and make up miles, head clearer. She gets the van moving without asking for a statement.
ENC-D11-B.log_1: You regain some road, spirits lifted. The cashier declines the promoter’s help finding everybody’s reason for leaving.

ENC-D11-C.name: Over one counter
ENC-D11-C.desc: At a highway pharmacy, a clerk offers detour directions while recalling Biden’s January 2025 withdrawal of proposed prescription-free contraceptive coverage. Existing rules remained. The medicine was already on the shelf. The insurance card wanted it to visit a doctor.
ENC-D11-C.log_0: The direct detour regains time and clears your head. The clerk’s map has a startling innovation: only one place marked destination.
ENC-D11-C.log_1: You regain some time and laugh at her directions: “Past the doctor, past the insurer, then actually go somewhere.”

ENC-D12-A.name: Attendance, with free delivery
ENC-D12-A.desc: At a courthouse coffee cart, a visiting California volunteer offers detour directions. June 2026’s judgment struck down the immigration-court arrest policy; appeals continue. The system invited people to attend hearings, then discovered attendance came with free delivery.
ENC-D12-A.choice_0: Use paper for the road shortcut
ENC-D12-A.log_0: Your copied shortcut uses some paper and recovers time. The volunteer separates it from the court notice. Directions should honor their invitations.
ENC-D12-A.choice_1: Check the ruling; take side streets
ENC-D12-A.log_1: You confirm the ruling’s limits and recover some time on side streets. The volunteer appreciates a route that discloses its destination.

ENC-D12-B.name: Destination included
ENC-D12-B.desc: At a bus-station café, a travel-aid volunteer offers directions while reading March 2026’s stay of a third-country deportation ruling. A chance to contest the destination remains disputed. At the ticket desk, that privilege comes with the cheap seats.
ENC-D12-B.choice_0: Use paper for the quick road route
ENC-D12-B.log_0: You copy the quick road route using some paper and regain time. The volunteer circles the destination. Your itinerary has advanced civil rights.
ENC-D12-B.choice_1: Check the status; take the slower shortcut
ENC-D12-B.log_1: You verify the ruling’s status and take the slower shortcut. The volunteer confirms where you’re going. No one calls this radical.

ENC-D12-C.name: The screen is the easy repair
ENC-D12-C.desc: At a phone-repair kiosk, a customer asks about deleting fertility data already shared. The technician points to the FTC’s Premom settlement, tips glitter into a desk fan, and hands her a dustpan. “Now ask for it back.”
ENC-D12-C.choice_0: Share food; take his direct directions
ENC-D12-C.log_0: You share food and take his direct road directions. He can repair the screen; the audience assembled behind it is another department.
ENC-D12-C.log_1: You regain some road and credibility. The technician can replace a cracked screen faster than an advertiser can forget a useful secret.

ENC-D13-A.name: Smaller dots, same clinic
ENC-D13-A.desc: The FTC banned X-Mode’s sale of sensitive location data. At a roadside café, a promoter insists location dots are anonymous. The waitress points to the clinic across the street. He offers to make the dots smaller.
ENC-D13-A.log_0: You regain road. Her directions point to the highway; the promoter’s map keeps trying to explain why everyone stopped beside the clinic.
ENC-D13-A.choice_1: Wait for the signed exit lane
ENC-D13-A.log_1: You regain some road and clear your head. She folds the promoter’s map until his pitch is the smallest dot in town.

ENC-D13-B.name: The tolerant detour sign
ENC-D13-B.desc: At a Beltway road closure, a reporter recalls 2025’s White House restrictions on AP over “Gulf of Mexico.” Access was still disputed that November. The detour sign is more tolerant: it lets you disagree with the arrows.
ENC-D13-B.log_0: The reporter’s directions recover time. The road accepts your destination without testing whether you’ve used the president’s preferred name for the water.
ENC-D13-B.log_1: You regain some time and clear your head. The reporter waves goodbye. No test of your publication’s ocean vocabulary.

ENC-D13-C.name: Turn the page
ENC-D13-C.desc: At a Beltway service station, a visiting Alabama plumber offers directions and recalls DOJ ending Lowndes County’s sewage settlement in April 2025 as an anti-DEI move. His wrench turns both ways. Washington prefers turning the page.
ENC-D13-C.log_0: His shortcut gets you moving. He points to the turn, then the wrench. One problem can actually be fixed today.
ENC-D13-C.log_1: You regain some time and clear your head. He caps a clean pipe fitting. Still waiting on the government’s matching part.

ENC-S01-A.name: Uniformly absent
ENC-S01-A.desc: At a park stop after DOGE firings, volunteers offer your crew some food and ask for help sorting abandoned service-desk stock. A rack holds uniforms for staff who aren’t coming back. It has more name badges than the welcome desk.
ENC-S01-A.log_0: You haul stock until your shoulders and head ache. The ranger finds another uniform. It is immediately qualified to staff the empty desk.
ENC-S01-A.log_1: You record the staffing account and laugh at the ranger’s coat-hanger demonstration. The hangers achieve perfect attendance while declining every visitor request.
ENC-S01-A.choice_2: Take some food for the road
ENC-S01-A.log_2: You take some food from the visitors’ donation. It’s the only queue today with somebody working at both ends.

ENC-S01-B.name: The spare part's chair
ENC-S01-B.desc: A garage hit by Trump’s tariffs welcomes your crew to its volunteer repair day and shared lunch. The owner needs help sorting old parts. A new imported component sits alone on a clean chair. Nobody wanted to leave that much money standing up.
ENC-S01-B.log_0: You scrape your knuckles and get a headache sorting parts. The owner finds a matching component. The expensive chair has acquired a roommate.
ENC-S01-B.log_1: You record the changed bill and enjoy the owner’s demonstration. He offers the component a seatbelt for its eventual trip across the workshop.
ENC-S01-B.log_2: You collect some food. The owner moves the component off its chair so lunch can use the only seating not yet priced as an investment.

ENC-S01-C.name: The second opening ceremony
ENC-S01-C.desc: A veterans’ hall is holding a supper about Trump’s “Department of War” secondary title. They welcome your crew and need help sorting old ceremonial stock. The same ribbon is scheduled to open both departments. It’s beginning to look concerned about the scissors.
ENC-S01-C.log_0: You haul boxes until your back and head ache. The volunteer finds the original scissors. The new era can now be opened with used equipment.
ENC-S01-C.log_1: You record the actual announcement and enjoy the volunteers’ rehearsal. They cut an imaginary ribbon twice. The imaginary department remains the same size.
ENC-S01-C.log_2: You take some food. The volunteer labels the leftovers strategic reserves. The sandwiches appear comfortable with their secondary title.

ENC-S02-A.name: Lunch for the slogan
ENC-S02-A.desc: At a roadside tariff fair, an importer needs supplies for his public cost display. Across the aisle, a promoter offers your crew some food to repeat “China paid.” The importer has his American bank statement. The promoter has better sandwiches.
ENC-S02-A.choice_0: Donate supplies to the cost display
ENC-S02-A.log_0: You donate some supplies; the importer records your help. The American payment finally gets a display board as large as the foreign-payer slogan.
ENC-S02-A.choice_1: Take the food; repeat the slogan
ENC-S02-A.log_1: You collect some food and repeat the slogan. The importer corrects you with his payment record. The sandwich has purchased a very small spokesperson.
ENC-S02-A.choice_2: Use your paper; record the payment
ENC-S02-A.log_2: You use some supplies to document the actual payment. The importer points to his name. It has remained American throughout the promotion.

ENC-S02-B.name: Complimentary certainty
ENC-S02-B.desc: At a library health-information fair, volunteers need supplies to display the corrected MAHA citations. A wellness promoter offers your stopped crew some food for praising the original report as error-free. The volunteers have the corrections. The promoter has covered them with the biscuit tray.
ENC-S02-B.choice_0: Donate supplies for the correction display
ENC-S02-B.log_0: You donate some supplies; volunteers record your help. The correction board rises above the biscuits. Evidence is finally operating at eye level.
ENC-S02-B.choice_1: Take the food; call it error-free
ENC-S02-B.log_1: You take some food and praise the original report. The librarian corrects you. The promoter moves another biscuit over the missing study.
ENC-S02-B.choice_2: Use your paper; save the corrections
ENC-S02-B.log_2: You use some supplies to save the original and corrected citations. The librarian moves the biscuit tray. The references immediately become easier to find.

ENC-S02-C.name: Independent sandwiches
ENC-S02-C.desc: A civic picnic explains unlimited super-PAC contributions and the different limits on direct candidate gifts. Volunteers need supplies for their examples. A sponsor offers your crew some food to say there are no limits at all. His example is currently talking with its mouth full.
ENC-S02-C.log_0: You donate some supplies, and volunteers record your help. The two sets of rules finally get separate folders. The sponsor requests a third sandwich.
ENC-S02-C.choice_1: Take the food; repeat no limits
ENC-S02-C.log_1: You collect some food and repeat the wrong rule. A volunteer corrects it. The sponsor has confused unlimited independent spending with unlimited agreement.
ENC-S02-C.choice_2: Use your paper; record the distinction
ENC-S02-C.log_2: You use some supplies to record the rules accurately. The volunteer separates the folders. The sandwiches continue attempting a merger.

ENC-S03-A.name: A shift to prove the shift
ENC-S03-A.desc: Your tired crew stops at a workshop preparing for Medicaid work checks due from 2027. A cleaner is filling in a practice form during her unpaid break. The form asks why she isn’t working. Volunteers offer a table for your own food and welcome help.
ENC-S03-A.log_0: You read until your head aches. The cleaner lists her unpaid break as time spent explaining her unpaid break. The form requests detail.
ENC-S03-A.choice_1: Use some food; take a break
ENC-S03-A.log_1: You use some food and recover at the table. The cleaner turns the form face down. It cannot question chewing from that position.
ENC-S03-A.log_2: You donate some supplies, and volunteers add your help to their account. The cleaner finally gets a spare pen that doesn’t belong to another job.

ENC-S03-B.name: The disappearing overhead chair
ENC-S03-B.desc: Your road-weary crew stops at a research teach-in about the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap. A scientist explains which costs keep a laboratory running. Her demonstration chair has a cushion marked “discovery” and no legs. Volunteers offer ordinary seating and need supplies.
ENC-S03-B.log_0: You read until your head aches. The scientist lists the chair legs as overhead. The discovery cushion begins its research on the floor.
ENC-S03-B.log_1: You use some water and ease your aches in an ordinary chair. Its unglamorous legs quietly complete the assignment.
ENC-S03-B.log_2: You donate some supplies, and volunteers record your help. The scientist puts a box under the cushion. Overhead returns disguised as a donation.

ENC-S03-C.name: The gift that needs a chair
ENC-S03-C.desc: Your aching crew stops at a temp-work briefing. The recruiter’s gift policy requires workers to document a free coffee while a news display covers the Pentagon’s Qatari jet. The coffee has its own folder. Applicants are still standing. A volunteer welcomes supply donations.
ENC-S03-C.log_0: You read until your head aches. The form asks how the coffee could influence you. Remaining conscious seems like a dangerous admission.
ENC-S03-C.log_1: You use some food and recover on the outside bench. Your lunch comes from your own bag. The recruiter cannot find its foreign sponsor.
ENC-S03-C.choice_2: Donate supplies to the worker desk
ENC-S03-C.log_2: You donate some supplies, and the worker volunteer records your help. The coffee’s folder gets a divider. Aircraft acceptance remains outside her stationery budget.

ENC-S04-A.name: The safe place to stop
ENC-S04-A.desc: After Trump officials’ Signal scandal, a roadside freight desk has put its public rest-area directions through a privacy briefing. Your tired crew is welcome to wait. The dispatcher knows a quiet corner. The briefing presenter has accidentally sent the directions to the biscuit supplier.
ENC-S04-A.log_0: You read until your head aches. The biscuit supplier knows where you can rest. The people operating the rest area await a secure reply.
ENC-S04-A.log_1: You use some food and rest with a clearer head. The dispatcher closes the briefing window. The outdoor bench requires no recipient list.
ENC-S04-A.choice_2: Ask the dispatcher about the quiet corner
ENC-S04-A.log_2: The dispatcher becomes a local contact and shows you a place to rest. She writes her number down without adding a journalist.

ENC-S04-B.name: Rest assured by the brochure
ENC-S04-B.desc: After DOGE park firings, your tired crew reaches a campground with an unanswered service phone. A volunteer host welcomes you to rest and explain your trip. The recorded greeting promises personal attention. The host has heard it often enough to consider it a character reference.
ENC-S04-B.log_0: You read the changes until your head aches. The phone promises someone will be right with you. It has become the park’s longest-serving optimist.
ENC-S04-B.choice_1: Use some food; rest by the van
ENC-S04-B.log_1: You use some food and rest with a clearer head. The greeting continues inside. Outside, the host actually knows where the bench is.
ENC-S04-B.log_2: The host becomes a local contact and finds you a resting place. She answers your question before the recording finishes promising an answer.

ENC-S04-C.name: The name is not a bed
ENC-S04-C.desc: Following Trump’s Gulf renaming, a marina has renamed its visitor area “America’s Great Rest.” Your tired crew stops beneath the new sign. The benches are stacked for painting. A dockhand offers the old shaded corner. It has survived without being named after the country.
ENC-S04-C.log_0: You read the directions until your head aches. Every route reaches America’s Great Rest. None explains how to sit on stacked benches.
ENC-S04-C.choice_1: Use some food; rest in shade
ENC-S04-C.log_1: You use some food and rest with a clearer head. The old corner has no ceremonial title, but it has successfully retained the shade.
ENC-S04-C.choice_2: Ask the dockhand for a resting place
ENC-S04-C.log_2: The dockhand becomes a local contact and shows you the old resting spot. His directions contain an actual bench and only one name.

ENC-S05-A.name: The adhesive boom
ENC-S05-A.desc: At a grocery hit by Trump’s tariffs, your crew can buy some food for $6 or earn $10 applying revised prices. The owner has run out of shelf space for the stickers. American manufacturing has begun with a very large order of glue.
ENC-S05-A.log_0: You pay $6 and collect some food. The cashier peels off the old price. It comes away more reluctantly than the patriotic flag.
ENC-S05-A.log_1: You earn $10 and a headache. By closing time, the shelf is mostly adhesive. The promised manufacturing boom has reached your thumb.
ENC-S05-A.log_2: You pass and leave dispirited. The affordability display has put its own prices out of reach.

ENC-S05-B.name: The complimentary evidence
ENC-S05-B.desc: A temp-work centre sells some food for $6 and offers your crew $10 to inventory gifts surrendered under its employer’s rule. Above the mint collection, a news screen reports the Pentagon’s Qatari jet. The recruiter has ordered a bigger evidence bag. For the mints.
ENC-S05-B.log_0: You pay $6 and collect some food. Buying it avoids a gift declaration. The receipt is your lunch’s diplomatic passport.
ENC-S05-B.log_1: You earn $10 and a headache listing the mints. One is marked “possible influence, peppermint.” Nobody asks whether it needs a runway.
ENC-S05-B.choice_2: Pass on the food and job
ENC-S05-B.log_2: You leave dispirited. The recruiter locks up a complimentary biscuit. The aircraft on the news remains complimentary.

ENC-S05-C.name: Secondary-title special
ENC-S05-C.desc: A surplus-market café celebrates Trump’s “Department of War” secondary title. It offers your crew some food for $6 or $10 to check the souvenir labels. The chili has been renamed “Operational Readiness.” The cook is still defending it from a fly.
ENC-S05-C.log_0: You pay $6 and collect some food. The cook deploys a lid. Operational readiness is now protected by an actual defence system.
ENC-S05-C.log_1: You earn $10 and a headache checking the secondary title. The cook asks whether the chili must retain a statutory name.
ENC-S05-C.log_2: You leave dispirited. The fly lands on Operational Readiness. The market announces no change in its strategic position.

ENC-S06-A.name: Actual-size science
ENC-S06-A.desc: A library fair is checking the nonexistent studies from the initial MAHA report. The organizer offers your crew $8 to correct the display cards. The original author table has empty chairs. The corrected version needs actual people, which is proving a serious catering complication.
ENC-S06-A.choice_0: Check and save the citation history
ENC-S06-A.log_0: You save the original and corrected references with a headache. The organizer cancels the imaginary seating plan. The room becomes smaller and more accurate.
ENC-S06-A.log_1: You earn $8 and enjoy crossing out the fictional study. It is the first government-inspired job here completed without needing an imaginary qualification.
ENC-S06-A.log_2: You leave dispirited. The empty author chair has acquired a ribbon. The organizer still needs somebody who exists to move it.

ENC-S06-B.name: Please redirect the sandwich
ENC-S06-B.desc: A print shop’s public display reconstructs the Trump officials’ Signal leak with a sandwich-order diagram. The owner offers your crew $8 to rearrange its arrows after the demonstration. The journalist’s plate is full. The cook is still waiting for permission to learn about lunch.
ENC-S06-B.choice_0: Check and save the reported timeline
ENC-S06-B.log_0: You save the checked timeline, head aching. The owner adds a label for the accidental recipient. It is larger than the label for security.
ENC-S06-B.log_1: You earn $8 and enjoy connecting the cook to the order. The sandwich completes its journey without appearing in an unexpected publication.
ENC-S06-B.log_2: You leave dispirited. The owner runs the demonstration again. The journalist receives another sandwich while the cook studies the empty order tray.

ENC-S06-C.name: Return postage required
ENC-S06-C.desc: Parents responding to Trump’s Education Department closure directive have set up a roadside letter stall. They offer your crew $8 to sort public requests by subject. The crate marked “power returned to parents” contains mostly envelopes needing stamps. Sovereignty has developed a postage problem.
ENC-S06-C.log_0: You save the actual directive and its legal limits, head aching. The parent removes a premature “closed” sticker. The crate still needs carrying.
ENC-S06-C.log_1: You earn $8 and enjoy the parents’ commentary. The request for less paperwork fills its own box. Everyone agrees to start there.
ENC-S06-C.log_2: You leave dispirited. A parent weighs the request for more local control. It has gone into the next postage bracket.

ENC-S07-A.name: The desk survived
ENC-S07-A.desc: After DOGE park firings, a campground association is moving the unused service desk into its volunteer tent. They offer your crew $12 for lifting, or welcome supplies. The coordinator calls the desk “excess bureaucracy.” It still has to go somewhere people can ask for toilet paper.
ENC-S07-A.log_0: You donate some supplies and gain a local contact. The coordinator finds your details easily; the desk’s staff directory has plenty of space.
ENC-S07-A.log_1: You earn $12 with aching arms. The coordinator empties the drawer of unused name badges. Smaller government becomes surprisingly easier to lift.
ENC-S07-A.log_2: You leave dispirited. The empty service desk remains outside the volunteer tent, continuing its successful transition out of public service.

ENC-S07-B.name: Premium domestic rust
ENC-S07-B.desc: Trump’s tariffs have sent a roadside machine shop hunting salvage. The owner offers your crew $12 to unload old steel, or welcomes useful supplies. He has price-tagged the rust. “It’s American rust. We’re protecting it now.”
ENC-S07-B.log_0: You donate some supplies and gain a local contact. The owner adds your name beside the repair phone. The rust gets no vote.
ENC-S07-B.log_1: You earn $12, sore but laughing as flakes fall off the steel. The owner sweeps them into a tin. “Domestic inventory.”
ENC-S07-B.log_2: You leave dispirited. The owner moves the rust behind the counter. Apparently protection requires somewhere safer to put the price tag.

ENC-S07-C.name: The useful tax leaflet
ENC-S07-C.desc: A pantry fundraiser preparing for the 2025 SNAP cuts offers your stopped crew $12 to move a donated empty freezer. Food donations are also welcome. The freezer has a bad wheel. A politician’s tax-cut leaflet is waiting for its first practical assignment.
ENC-S07-C.choice_0: Donate some food to the pantry
ENC-S07-C.log_0: You donate some food and gain a local contact. The cook writes down your details before filling the freezer. Your contribution actually has a destination.
ENC-S07-C.log_1: You earn $12 and sore arms. The cook wedges the tax-cut leaflet beneath the wheel. Its food policy finally stops something rolling backwards.
ENC-S07-C.log_2: You leave dispirited. The freezer rolls back across the room. The politician’s smiling face remains very positive about the direction of travel.

ENC-S08-A.name: The foldout electorate
ENC-S08-A.desc: A roadside café hosts a bookkeeper’s public guide to unlimited super-PAC money; some food costs $5. Your crew stops beside a sample donor ledger. The ordinary voter fits on a receipt. The billionaire requires a foldout that has reached the next table.
ENC-S08-A.choice_0: Check and save the spending rules
ENC-S08-A.log_0: You save the checked rules and examples, head aching. The bookkeeper folds the billionaire away. Several ordinary voters become visible underneath.
ENC-S08-A.log_1: You pay $5 and collect some food. The cook gives your order equal time on the grill. The ledger’s largest donor has not been consulted.
ENC-S08-A.log_2: You leave dispirited. The bookkeeper opens another foldout. The electorate is going to need a larger tablecloth.

ENC-S08-B.name: The coverage magnifier
ENC-S08-B.desc: A community health briefing at a roadside diner explains the 2025 Medicaid law; some food costs $5. Your crew stops at the source table. The eligibility changes are in small print. The politician’s promise of simplicity needs the entire window.
ENC-S08-B.choice_0: Check and save the law’s changes
ENC-S08-B.log_0: You save the checked changes and projections, head aching. The nurse moves the enormous simplicity poster so you can find the actual rules.
ENC-S08-B.log_1: You pay $5 and collect some food. The cook states exactly what is included. The nurse asks whether he is available to explain the bill.
ENC-S08-B.log_2: You leave dispirited. From outside, the simplicity promise is perfectly legible. The rules remain behind it, requiring better eyesight and an appointment.

ENC-S08-C.name: A war on small print
ENC-S08-C.desc: A roadside souvenir printer is explaining Trump’s “Department of War” secondary title beside a $5 food counter. Your crew stops at the source display. The word “War” fills a banner. The explanation of “secondary” has been squeezed onto the back of the stapler.
ENC-S08-C.choice_0: Check and save the naming order
ENC-S08-C.log_0: You save the actual order and statutory-name distinction, head aching. The printer turns over the stapler. The qualification has survived underneath the war effort.
ENC-S08-C.log_1: You pay $5 and collect some food. The cook leaves its name alone. Lunch reaches operational readiness when he finds the lid.
ENC-S08-C.choice_2: Pass on the display and food
ENC-S08-C.log_2: You leave dispirited. The large banner flaps over the source display. War has successfully occupied the part explaining what actually changed.

ENC-S09-A.name: Patriotically air-conditioned
ENC-S09-A.desc: Florida barred local heat-break rules. At a roadside trade fair, a contractor wants the same freedom here. He praises toughness from inside a refrigerated sales trailer. A worker points you toward shade; the trailer’s exhaust is blowing directly onto her.
ENC-S09-A.log_0: Food and shade restore you. The contractor shuts his trailer window to explain more comfortably why workers need fewer protections.
ENC-S09-A.log_1: His certainty calms you. You repeat it; the worker offers to swap places with his air conditioner. Your authority evaporates.
ENC-S09-A.log_2: You leave irritated. The contractor puts on a cardigan before recording another message about people becoming too sensitive to heat.

ENC-S09-B.name: The research was feeling shy
ENC-S09-B.desc: The MAHA report cited studies that did not exist. You stop at a wellness fair where a vendor says missing evidence proves how suppressed it is. A first-aid volunteer offers a shaded seat. The vendor’s certificate has been printed backwards for additional secrecy.
ENC-S09-B.log_0: You eat and recover in the shade. The volunteer reads the backwards certificate in a mirror; it remains impressively unqualified.
ENC-S09-B.choice_1: Agree the missing studies prove it
ENC-S09-B.log_1: The neat explanation settles your nerves. A visitor asks whether an empty bottle therefore contains the strongest possible medicine.
ENC-S09-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. The vendor covers the blank reference list, protecting the authorities from discovering absolutely nothing.

ENC-S09-C.name: Your speech needs a bigger wallet
ENC-S09-C.desc: Super PACs can take unlimited contributions. At a roadside political picnic, a donor’s giant fan cools the premium tables while volunteers sweat. The organizer says everyone’s voice is equal. A worker points out the quiet shade behind the speaker tower.
ENC-S09-C.log_0: You recover over food. Above you, the donor’s speech requires enough amplification to knock a paper plate off a democratic table.
ENC-S09-C.log_1: The reassurance helps until you repeat it near the premium microphone. Your equal voice disappears beneath the donor clearing his throat.
ENC-S09-C.log_2: You leave dispirited. A volunteer searches for the small-donor table and finds it being used to hold the large donor’s fan.

ENC-S10-A.name: The drain is unpatriotic
ENC-S10-A.desc: Trump ordered “Gulf of America” onto federal maps. At a flooded parking stop, the owner offers $7 to repaint his sign. The attendant asks for a drain. He hands her a flag.
ENC-S10-A.log_0: Seven dollars and a headache. The owner salutes the new gulf while you wring the old water out of your socks.
ENC-S10-A.log_1: Drivers trust your arrow. The attendant asks whether draining an American gulf now counts as surrendering territory.
ENC-S10-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. His flag falls into the puddle. He blames Mexico.

ENC-S10-B.name: The mountain’s forwarding address
ENC-S10-B.desc: Trump ordered Denali renamed Mount McKinley for federal use. At a souvenir stall, the printer offers $7 to replace labels on identical mountain photographs. A customer demands to see the new mountain before paying. The printer rotates the old photograph.
ENC-S10-B.log_0: Seven dollars and a headache. A customer asks whether McKinley is taller. The printer raises the shelf.
ENC-S10-B.log_1: You earn trust by comparing the labels with the order. The mountain has performed no work whatsoever on its rebrand.
ENC-S10-B.log_2: You leave without the cash. The customer asks whether the old mountain is discounted now that Washington has replaced it.

ENC-S10-C.name: Welcome to the other department
ENC-S10-C.desc: Trump authorized Department of War as a second title for Defense. A motel near a veterans’ event offers $7 to relabel its meeting room accordingly. The owner wants a grander entrance. The cleaner suggests opening the door instead of adding another name.
ENC-S10-C.log_0: Seven dollars and a headache. The owner holds two ribbon cuttings; both crowds enter the same room and collide.
ENC-S10-C.log_1: Guests trust your directions. The cleaner moves one arrow and achieves the evening’s only successful military maneuver.
ENC-S10-C.log_2: You leave disappointed. The owner asks whether the two departments will need separate beds or can continue occupying the same mattress.

ENC-S11-A.name: The raccoon has seniority
ENC-S11-A.desc: After DOGE’s park-staff cuts, you stop at a park-side shop. The clerk offers $9 to fold trail leaflets. Outside, a bin overflows beneath AMERICA THE BEAUTIFUL. A raccoon is wearing somebody’s entire picnic.
ENC-S11-A.log_0: You share food and exchange numbers, enjoying a laugh. She locks the door before the raccoon applies for management.
ENC-S11-A.log_1: Nine dollars and aching eyes. The clerk endorses your careful folding. Washington’s savings now require the gift shop’s wages.
ENC-S11-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. The raccoon climbs onto the information desk, becoming the first park employee to receive lunch.

ENC-S11-B.name: The library needs a patriotic eraser
ENC-S11-B.desc: Trump’s patriotic-education order reaches a community book sale. The organizer offers $9 to sort donated books. A campaigner wants every unpleasant chapter removed from the history section. The thickest book is beginning to resemble a coaster.
ENC-S11-B.log_0: You share food and exchange numbers, enjoying a laugh. The coaster-sized history book finally supports something real: a cup of tea.
ENC-S11-B.log_1: Nine dollars and aching eyes earn the organizer’s endorsement. The rejected history fills three shelves; the patriotic remainder fits beside the bookmarks.
ENC-S11-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. The champion requests larger type so the remaining history can still look like an education.

ENC-S11-C.name: Closing time for the closing department
ENC-S11-C.desc: Trump directed his education secretary to facilitate closing the department. A print shop offers $9 to fold school-help leaflets. A campaign flyer promises fewer bureaucrats. The help number reaches somebody who also needs the number.
ENC-S11-C.log_0: You share food and gain a contact, laughing at the phone tree. The printer suggests putting the education secretary on hold.
ENC-S11-C.log_1: Nine dollars and a headache earn the printer’s endorsement. The leaflet unfolds into more instructions for finding the simpler government.
ENC-S11-C.log_2: You leave dispirited. The flyer’s smiling parent has been on hold long enough for the pictured child to look employed.

ENC-S12-A.name: The ingredients in your wallet
ENC-S12-A.desc: USDA approved Nebraska’s ban on buying soda and energy drinks with SNAP benefits, effective January 2026. At a Nebraska grocer, you can move crates for $14 or sort shelf labels for some food. Cash still buys the identical bottles. The government’s taste test happens inside the card reader.
ENC-S12-A.log_0: You haul crates, earn $14 and stretch your sore back. The clerk pays cash. Suddenly every bottle you just moved is an acceptable purchase.
ENC-S12-A.log_1: You earn some food and a headache giving identical bottles different payment labels. The clerk checks the ingredients again. Still no mention of household income.
ENC-S12-A.log_2: You leave frustrated without earnings. The clerk turns a bottle over, looking for the part of the drink that changes when somebody pays cash.

ENC-S12-B.name: The baby’s money has a bedtime
ENC-S12-B.desc: Trump Accounts offer eligible newborns $1,000, locked away from childhood expenses. At a discount-store loading bay, a parent needs diapers today. The manager offers $14 for lifting boxes or food for checking labels. The baby’s investment statement has already needed changing.
ENC-S12-B.log_0: You earn $14 and sore muscles. The parent buys diapers; the baby immediately demonstrates why this cannot wait for compound interest.
ENC-S12-B.log_1: You earn food and a headache. The parent considers asking the baby’s portfolio to stay awake for the next feeding.
ENC-S12-B.log_2: You leave without earnings. The investor screams from the trolley, expressing a surprisingly immediate preference for spending.

ENC-S12-C.name: The straw receives immediate assistance
