ENC-S12-C.desc: Trump ordered federal agencies off paper straws. At a catering depot, the dispatcher offers $14 to move plastic-straw cartons or food for sorting them. A school’s cancelled food order is still on the desk. Lunch has lost funding; its drinking equipment has a national strategy.
ENC-S12-C.log_0: Fourteen dollars and sore shoulders. The dispatcher asks whether a hungry child could survive by chewing the national priority.
ENC-S12-C.log_1: You earn supplies and a headache. Your lunch arrives beside enough protected plastic to feed an extremely disappointed whale.
ENC-S12-C.log_2: You leave without earnings. The dispatcher places a straw beside the cancelled lunch order so at least something has received federal attention.

ENC-S13-A.name: China’s card declined
ENC-S13-A.desc: Trump says China pays the tariffs. At a roadside shop, your supplies cost $12. The cashier taps a Chinese flag against the card reader. Declined.
ENC-S13-A.log_0: Your payment works. “Congratulations,” she says. “You’re China now.”
ENC-S13-A.log_1: She circles the tariff. “China’s very generous with your money.”
ENC-S13-A.log_2: You leave empty-handed. The tariff has successfully protected the supplies from Americans.

ENC-S13-B.name: One cent, before expenses
ENC-S13-B.desc: The Mint stopped making circulating pennies after each cost 3.69 cents to produce. Old pennies still count as money. At a roadside shop, some food and water cost $12. The cashier taps her penny jar. “Washington finally found something it couldn’t afford to keep making cheap.”
ENC-S13-B.log_0: You pay $12 and collect some supplies. She straightens the penny jar. “Still worth a cent. Just retired from costing us nearly four.”
ENC-S13-B.log_1: You keep the $12 quote and the Mint’s cost figures through a long explanation. She asks you not to let the bread hear what a penny cost.
ENC-S13-B.log_2: You leave empty-handed and annoyed. She pats the penny jar. The smallest thing on the counter has a retirement plan. Your van still needs feeding.

ENC-S13-C.name: Lost and found a stadium
ENC-S13-C.desc: Ohio’s 2025 budget allocated $600 million in unclaimed funds to a Browns stadium. At an Ohio roadside shop, some food and water cost $12. The cashier keeps the report beside the lost-property box. “Anything in there shaped like a billionaire? Apparently they get collected first.”
ENC-S13-C.log_0: You buy some food and water. She points at the stadium report. “See? Even you managed to spend your own money.”
ENC-S13-C.log_1: You save the $12 quote and budget report through a long explanation. “They couldn’t find the money’s owners,” she says. “The stadium introduced itself immediately.”
ENC-S13-C.log_2: You leave empty-handed and frustrated. She calls after you: “Keep a hand on it. Ohio’s looking for a midfield logo.”

ENC-S14-A.name: A donation you can trip over
ENC-S14-A.desc: Super PACs accept unlimited contributions. You stop at an event depot offering $10 to carry a donor’s giant ceremonial cheque. Its accompanying poster says every citizen has a voice. The cheque is too wide to fit through the citizens’ entrance.
ENC-S14-A.choice_0: Save the terms and donor display
ENC-S14-A.log_0: You document the arrangement, head aching. The donor’s speech is officially independent; it still requires three people and a loading door.
ENC-S14-A.log_1: Ten dollars and sore muscles. The donor signs in one effortless stroke; you need to sit down after delivering his free speech.
ENC-S14-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. A worker removes the public entrance sign so the donor’s equal voice can scrape through sideways.

ENC-S14-B.name: Savings need volunteers
ENC-S14-B.desc: Republicans’ 2025 law reduced projected federal Medicaid spending. At a clinic fundraiser, a hire company offers $10 to move chairs. The display celebrates government savings beside a jar asking patients to fill the hole. Someone has helpfully supplied a very small jar.
ENC-S14-B.choice_0: Compare the law with the display
ENC-S14-B.log_0: You save the figures, head aching. The jar would need to become a bank before the savings started looking like healthcare.
ENC-S14-B.log_1: You earn $10 and aching muscles. The fundraiser adds another chair for people who will be asked to applaud needing a fundraiser.
ENC-S14-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. A patient drops coins into the jar; the sound is considerably smaller than the tax bill.

ENC-S14-C.name: The border has a gift shop
ENC-S14-C.desc: Trump’s Gold Card offers an expedited immigration route tied to a million-dollar gift. At a visa-agent open house, a contractor offers $10 to move gold display stands. The welcome mat is so thick the cleaner has to drag it in.
ENC-S14-C.choice_0: Read and save the program terms
ENC-S14-C.log_0: You preserve the terms through a headache. The welcome gets noticeably warmer once the applicant’s money is allowed to arrive first.
ENC-S14-C.log_1: Ten dollars and sore arms. You carry the golden gateway while earning enough to approach it with considerable imagination.
ENC-S14-C.log_2: You leave disappointed. The agent calls the entrance welcoming, then asks someone to check whether the welcome mat might attract ordinary shoes.

ENC-S15-A.name: Working on proof of working
ENC-S15-A.desc: Congress added Medicaid work requirements for 2027. At a community information table, a cleaner practices assembling proof of shifts between shifts. The sample form asks why she missed the workshop. Her payslip is still damp from the job that prevented her attending.
ENC-S15-A.log_0: You document the mismatch, mentally drained. The cleaner’s work prevented her proving she works. The sample answer box is admirably small.
ENC-S15-A.log_1: You share food and exchange numbers. She eats while sorting payslips, providing evidence that employment can interfere with both lunch and paperwork.
ENC-S15-A.log_2: You leave frustrated. She asks whether attending a workshop about proving work can itself count as work. Nobody has brought that form.

ENC-S15-B.name: The book’s missing workforce
ENC-S15-B.desc: Trump ordered changes to federal history displays. At a pop-up history discussion, a warehouse worker compares the proposed patriotic captions with old factory photographs. The cheerful new caption celebrates industrial greatness. Somebody has placed it directly over the people doing the work.
ENC-S15-B.log_0: You document the missing workers, eyes aching. The factory’s greatness becomes easier to explain once you peel the explanation off its employees.
ENC-S15-B.log_1: You share lunch and exchange numbers. He places a crumb on each hidden worker, briefly restoring history with a sandwich.
ENC-S15-B.log_2: You leave irritated. The organizer adjusts the caption so industrial greatness no longer has any visible need for lunch breaks.

ENC-S15-C.name: A lecture is not a meal
ENC-S15-C.desc: Republicans’ 2025 law tightened SNAP eligibility and cut spending. At a food-aid discussion, a night-shift worker compares the changes with a leaflet explaining personal responsibility. The leaflet’s author is pictured beside a banquet. The worker would like to qualify for whatever is behind him.
ENC-S15-C.choice_0: Check the changes with the worker
ENC-S15-C.log_0: You save a careful comparison, mentally tired. The leaflet has six photographs of responsibility and no instructions for eating any of them.
ENC-S15-C.log_1: You share lunch and gain a contact. The worker moves the author’s banquet photograph aside to make room for actual dinner.
ENC-S15-C.log_2: You leave frustrated. The worker folds the leaflet around a small snack, finally finding a useful relationship between the advice and food.

ENC-S16-A.name: Cabinet-level contact management
ENC-S16-A.desc: Trump’s team included a journalist in its Signal strike chat. At a café showing the news, the owner offers $8 to clear a tour bus’s tables. The cashier needs his PIN to refund mayonnaise.
ENC-S16-A.log_0: You confirm the report. The café’s new security procedure is asking who the people in the chat actually are.
ENC-S16-A.log_1: Eight dollars and a headache. You match forgotten phones to passengers. The café’s standards now exceed national security’s.
ENC-S16-A.log_2: You leave unpaid. The mayonnaise refund remains behind a stronger security procedure than the airstrikes.

ENC-S16-B.name: Refund-shaped paper
ENC-S16-B.desc: At a parcel counter, a clerk’s airline cancelled her flight. She declined replacement travel, so DOT’s rule requires an automatic refund. It sent a voucher instead. She offers $8 to sort return labels while she reads the rule. Her cash drawer refuses to recognize the voucher as a relative.
ENC-S16-B.choice_0: Read the refund rule with her
ENC-S16-B.log_0: You confirm that the refund must use her original payment method. “I paid with money,” she says. “Apparently that was an unusual choice.”
ENC-S16-B.log_1: You sort the labels, earn $8 and rest your aching eyes. The drawer produces cash on its first attempt. She wonders whether it has airline-management experience.
ENC-S16-B.log_2: You leave unpaid and annoyed. She folds the unwanted voucher into a paper plane. At last, something this airline sent her can take off.

ENC-S16-C.name: Independent balloons
ENC-S16-C.desc: Super PACs can receive unlimited contributions. At a party-supply shop, the owner offers $8 to sort balloons for an independent political event. One donor’s balloon fills the van-sized loading door. The small-donor balloons come in a bag labelled decorative filler.
ENC-S16-C.log_0: Your careful account earns trust. The giant balloon is officially independent, although every smaller balloon must move wherever it goes.
ENC-S16-C.log_1: Eight dollars and a headache. You separate the citizens by purchasing power while the event plan calls everyone part of one big conversation.
ENC-S16-C.log_2: You leave disappointed. The large donor’s balloon blocks the light, giving the small donors their first experience of being overshadowed literally.

ENC-S17-A.name: Freedom reaches the tuna
ENC-S17-A.desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation. At a truck stop, a celebratory display sprays the sandwich counter. The clerk offers $9 to brace it. Ordinary showers are free if you bring soap. The tuna has already exercised its freedom.
ENC-S17-A.choice_0: Use your soap; take a shower
ENC-S17-A.log_0: Clean at last. On your way out, a tuna sandwich makes a determined break for the drain.
ENC-S17-A.log_1: Nine dollars and aching arms. You hold freedom upright while the clerk evacuates the egg mayonnaise.
ENC-S17-A.log_2: You leave unwashed. The display has liberated half the lunch menu; the remaining sandwiches are gathering on higher ground.

ENC-S17-B.name: Florida’s refreshing example
ENC-S17-B.desc: Florida blocked local heat-break mandates. At a gym open house, a contractor promotes copying the law while workers assemble his enormous cooling fan. Nine dollars pays for moving its bases. Showers are free with your own soap; apparently water works better without a speech.
ENC-S17-B.log_0: You wash and clear your head. The contractor’s fan blows a worker’s break request under his refrigerated drinks table.
ENC-S17-B.log_1: Nine dollars and sore arms. You carry the equipment allowing the contractor to explain comfortably why cooling should remain optional.
ENC-S17-B.log_2: You leave irritated. The contractor complains that his free water is not cold enough while explaining why workers need fewer local protections.

ENC-S17-C.name: America has acquired your shower
ENC-S17-C.desc: Trump renamed the Gulf on federal maps. At a truck stop, the owner celebrates by renaming the free showers American Waters. He offers $9 to move a heavy map stand. You need your own soap. The water still comes from the same pipe.
ENC-S17-C.log_0: You wash and feel human again. The owner asks whether the American water felt different; you point at the unchanged dirt in the drain.
ENC-S17-C.log_1: Nine dollars and aching muscles. You move the national boundary three feet left so customers can reach the toilet.
ENC-S17-C.log_2: You leave unwashed and annoyed. The owner asks whether the shower queue looks more patriotic now that it has a coastline.

ENC-S18-A.name: Education, some assembly required
ENC-S18-A.desc: Trump directed the Education Department’s closure as far as law permits. At a school fundraiser, an organizer offers $11 to sort donated books. A volunteer is using the closure flyer to prop up a broken shelf. Finally, the policy is supporting education.
ENC-S18-A.log_0: Eleven dollars and aching eyes. You shelve the books; the closure flyer holds steady in its first successful teaching-support role.
ENC-S18-A.log_1: You share lunch and a laugh. She adds another closure flyer beneath the shelf, strengthening education through repeated calls to dismantle it.
ENC-S18-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. The shelf needs more support; the volunteer asks whether Washington has printed anything else about providing less.

ENC-S18-B.name: The owner fits; history doesn’t
ENC-S18-B.desc: Trump ordered federal history displays steered toward his version of national greatness. At a souvenir printer, $11 is offered for stocking postcard racks. A retired guide shows a proposed factory image: the owner fills the frame; the workforce has been cropped into the gift-shop floor.
ENC-S18-B.log_0: Eleven dollars and a headache. You arrange the owner’s face beside the cropping scraps containing everyone who made him wealthy.
ENC-S18-B.log_1: You share lunch and laugh at the edits. The guide reconstructs the workforce from scraps; the owner suddenly looks much less self-made.
ENC-S18-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. The printer enlarges the owner again, removing the last employee capable of explaining how the factory operated.

ENC-S18-C.name: Patriotism gets the big type
ENC-S18-C.desc: Trump’s school order promotes patriotic education. At a used-book stall, an organizer offers $11 to arrange the history section. A campaigner’s proposed guide prints the country’s achievements in huge letters and its mistakes so small the volunteer needs the stamp-collecting magnifier.
ENC-S18-C.log_0: Eleven dollars and tired eyes. You find the difficult history hiding beneath a photograph large enough to require its own table.
ENC-S18-C.log_1: You share lunch and laugh. She puts the magnifier over the omissions, making the proposed patriotic curriculum unexpectedly easier to see through.
ENC-S18-C.log_2: You leave disappointed. The campaigner asks whether the magnifier could be restricted to passages that make the country look bigger.

ENC-S19-A.name: Gold-standard stapling
ENC-S19-A.desc: The MAHA report cited nonexistent studies. A copy shop offers $15 to collate report booklets for a public discussion. The printer says missing pages are your fault, but missing science is apparently a formatting issue. He checks your staples more carefully than the references.
ENC-S19-A.log_0: Fifteen dollars, evidence, and a headache. Every page is now attached to something real, which puts the staples ahead of several citations.
ENC-S19-A.log_1: Your grand reading gets a laugh. You endorse a nonexistent paper; the printer asks whether your application to the commission is pending.
ENC-S19-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. The printer checks another staple, still the only part of the report willing to hold under light pressure.

ENC-S19-B.name: Overhead has started dripping
ENC-S19-B.desc: Trump’s NIH overhead-cap proposal put research running costs under pressure. At a university open day, a hire worker offers $15 to sort equipment tags. A researcher has put a bucket beneath a leak. The proposal’s cheerful summary keeps getting wet.
ENC-S19-B.log_0: Fifteen dollars and evidence cost a headache. The bucket becomes essential research equipment the moment the ceiling starts participating in the experiment.
ENC-S19-B.log_1: The crew laughs at your confident pitch. The researcher hands you the wet summary; you have omitted the part directly above your head.
ENC-S19-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. The bucket fills beneath a proposal that finds the room itself an awkward expense to associate with indoor research.

ENC-S19-C.name: The fine print has more money
ENC-S19-C.desc: Super PACs can accept unlimited contributions while candidate donations have separate limits. At an event printer, $15 is offered to sort disclosure inserts. The donor’s name gets a banner; the word independent has been squeezed behind the staple.
ENC-S19-C.log_0: Fifteen dollars and reliable evidence cost a headache. You unfold the small print until the donor’s independence becomes physically capable of occupying a room.
ENC-S19-C.log_1: Your donor impression gets laughs. You confuse the two contribution rules; the printer points out that the loophole requires better aim.
ENC-S19-C.log_2: You leave disappointed. The donor’s banner needs another pole; the disclosure remains small enough to disappear behind one finger.

ENC-S20-A.name: Federal savings, local shoulders
ENC-S20-A.desc: USDA cancelled local-food purchasing funds. At a co-op loading bay, an organizer offers food for packing donated groceries or $10 for sorting delivery slips. The cancelled order is easy to lift. Everything replacing it is in crates.
ENC-S20-A.log_0: You earn supplies and a sore back. The federal savings arrive in your shoulders, considerably heavier than they looked in the announcement.
ENC-S20-A.log_1: Ten dollars and a headache. Each address gets matched to food; Washington’s contribution remains a remarkably lightweight cancellation notice.
ENC-S20-A.log_2: You leave without earnings. The organizer folds the cancellation into a tiny square. Unfortunately, the crates refuse to become equally efficient.

ENC-S20-B.name: The cut comes with a serving suggestion
ENC-S20-B.desc: Republicans’ 2025 law cut SNAP spending and tightened eligibility. At a food-bank warehouse, packing groceries earns food; sorting address slips pays $10. A political leaflet calls the cuts an incentive. The volunteer holds it over a bowl to see what drops out.
ENC-S20-B.log_0: You earn supplies and aching muscles. The incentive produces nothing edible; the volunteer puts it under the bowl to protect the table.
ENC-S20-B.log_1: Ten dollars and a headache. You match hungry households with deliveries while the leaflet continues offering them a stronger character.
ENC-S20-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. The volunteer shakes the incentive one last time before returning to the groceries somebody actually supplied.

ENC-S20-C.name: A carton returns to public life
ENC-S20-C.desc: Congress and Trump let schools serve whole milk again in 2026. A dairy co-op is throwing a tiny welcome-back party for a carton. You can pack produce for some food or sort pickup slips for $10. The milk was always for sale. It just needed federal clearance for lunch.
ENC-S20-C.log_0: You earn some food and sore muscles boxing apples. Nobody in Congress has needed to take a position on their percentage of apple.
ENC-S20-C.log_1: You earn $10 and a headache. SCHOOL is now an allowed destination for the carton. Its contents haven’t changed; its congressional representation has improved.
ENC-S20-C.log_2: You leave frustrated, without wages or supplies. A member asks if you’ll stay for the carton’s victory speech. You’ve already heard enough from its elected representatives.

ENC-S21-A.name: The sea forgot its new name
ENC-S21-A.desc: Trump ordered federal maps to say Gulf of America. At a marine-supply counter, a customer demands an American refund because his old chart still says Mexico. The clerk has the order. The customer checks his shoes for foreign seawater.
ENC-S21-A.log_0: You save the actual naming change, head aching. The clerk explains that the water did not relocate; the customer looks personally betrayed by geography.
ENC-S21-A.log_1: The crew laughs until you invent a maritime border change. The clerk takes the chart away before your geography reaches the fish.
ENC-S21-A.log_2: You leave irritated. The customer wrings out a sock and asks whether the shop can exchange the water for the patriotic version.

ENC-S21-B.name: The second name needs a second mug
ENC-S21-B.desc: Trump authorized Department of War as a second name for Defense. At a surplus shop, a customer wants both departmental mugs because he supports both departments. The clerk has the order and one mug with a removable paper sleeve.
ENC-S21-B.choice_0: Read and save the actual order
ENC-S21-B.log_0: You preserve the secondary-title detail, head aching. The clerk slides the sleeve off, giving the customer a remarkably affordable tour of the bureaucracy.
ENC-S21-B.log_1: The crew laughs. You invent a rivalry between the two names; the customer starts asking which mug has the larger budget.
ENC-S21-B.log_2: You leave irritated. The customer buys confidence by pointing at both names while the clerk continues holding exactly one mug.

ENC-S21-C.name: Immigration, now with gift wrapping
ENC-S21-C.desc: Trump’s Gold Card ties expedited immigration to a million-dollar gift. You stop at a travel shop where the brochure sits beside cheap luggage. A clerk wraps it in tissue. Apparently the border opens more politely when it thinks it is receiving a present.
ENC-S21-C.log_0: You save the eligibility terms, head aching. A million dollars buys special attention; your travel budget qualifies for being pointed toward the exit.
ENC-S21-C.log_1: The crew laughs until you promise automatic citizenship. The clerk corrects you: even the expensive welcome still has terms.
ENC-S21-C.log_2: You leave irritated. The clerk smooths the tissue around a welcome priced well beyond the people currently carrying the luggage.

ENC-S22-A.name: The map has already won
ENC-S22-A.desc: Albuquerque reported a federal attempt to withdraw its Rail Trail grant. At a Beltway transport-book stall, a $6 route print still shows the promised path. The clerk keeps the withdrawal notice beside it. The funding has become harder to locate than the destination.
ENC-S22-A.log_0: You keep the six-dollar print as evidence. A dotted line remains the cheapest way to deliver infrastructure without anyone having to walk on it.
ENC-S22-A.choice_1: Compare the notice with the map
ENC-S22-A.log_1: You save a careful comparison, head aching. The clerk draws the uncertain funding in pencil, finally giving the path an accurate surface.
ENC-S22-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. The print reaches the destination beautifully; the people who might use the actual path have received a notice instead.

ENC-S22-B.name: A second name costs six dollars
ENC-S22-B.desc: Trump gave Defense the secondary title Department of War. At a military-souvenir stall, a $6 visitor guide marks two departments at the same address. The clerk has the order. A tourist is trying to schedule enough time to walk between them.
ENC-S22-B.log_0: You keep the six-dollar error as evidence. The tourist asks whether visiting both departments qualifies for a multi-site discount.
ENC-S22-B.choice_1: Compare the guide with the order
ENC-S22-B.log_1: You untangle the secondary name through a headache. The clerk erases the walking route, saving the tourist an ambitious circuit of the pavement.
ENC-S22-B.log_2: You leave irritated. The tourist sets two reminders for reaching the same building, providing the rebrand with its first doubling of effort.

ENC-S22-C.name: The difficult history is around the back
ENC-S22-C.desc: Trump ordered intervention in federal history displays. At a historical-site souvenir stall, a $6 guide offers a newly cheerful route past every grand house. The clerk has the earlier map. The servants’ entrance appears to have walked off without permission.
ENC-S22-C.log_0: You keep the six-dollar revision as evidence. The route enters every drawing room without once passing anyone who cleaned it.
ENC-S22-C.log_1: You preserve the missing entrance, head aching. The house’s self-made grandeur begins looking rather dependent on the path erased behind it.
ENC-S22-C.log_2: You leave disappointed. A cleaner takes the missing route, demonstrating an inconveniently practical relationship with the history being removed.

ENC-S23-A.name: Small government inspects your straw
ENC-S23-A.desc: Trump ordered federal agencies to stop using paper straws. At a burger stand, the owner films inspections of customers’ drinks as his own patriotic tribute. The cashier points out that customers are not federal agencies. He asks her to stop weakening the border.
ENC-S23-A.log_0: You share food and confirm her point. She eats while he carefully investigates whether the burger wrapper is conspiring with the straw.
ENC-S23-A.choice_1: Read and save the actual order
ENC-S23-A.log_1: You save the order through a headache. His federal jurisdiction shrinks until it no longer reaches the milkshake currently in front of him.
ENC-S23-A.log_2: You leave irritated. He demands another close-up of the straw, which has now received more oversight than the owner’s payroll.

ENC-S23-B.name: The working parent has insufficient time
ENC-S23-B.desc: Congress created Medicaid work rules beginning in 2027. At a preparation workshop, a working parent asks when to complete the paperwork between shifts. A campaign volunteer offers a pamphlet about initiative. The parent asks whether initiative can collect a child from school.
ENC-S23-B.log_0: You share food and back the question. The pamphlet lies beside the parent’s schedule, contributing no childcare whatsoever.
ENC-S23-B.log_1: You save the rollout details, head aching. The parent’s employment has already filled every hour the pamphlet calls available for getting organized.
ENC-S23-B.log_2: You leave annoyed. The parent folds the initiative pamphlet small enough to carry; fitting the actual requirements into the day remains harder.

ENC-S23-C.name: The photograph is insufficiently grateful
ENC-S23-C.desc: Trump’s Smithsonian directive called for his version of patriotic history. At a roadside history display, a promoter copies the idea by covering a strike photograph with a flag. The attendant asks where the workers went. He says they are now behind the country.
ENC-S23-C.log_0: You share food and confirm what was covered. The attendant lifts one corner of the flag; American workers reappear without harming America.
ENC-S23-C.log_1: You document the change, head aching. The promoter’s restored truth requires the photograph to remain mostly invisible.
ENC-S23-C.log_2: You leave frustrated. The promoter adds another flag after discovering the first one has failed to cover a worker’s raised hand.

ENC-S24-A.name: The shower has taken the hair
ENC-S24-A.desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation after years of complaining about water pressure. At a hardware launch, the demonstration blasts the wig off a presidential mannequin. The clerk offers $12 to mop; ordinary traveler showers cost $5. The wig is heading for plumbing reform.
ENC-S24-A.log_0: Twelve dollars and a sore back. You catch the wig on the mop, briefly becoming the best-groomed cleaner in the building.
ENC-S24-A.log_1: Five dollars buys a proper wash. The ordinary shower leaves your hair attached, an achievement the demonstration has chosen not to emphasize.
ENC-S24-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. The clerk puts the wet wig back on the mannequin, which now looks less certain about freedom.

ENC-S24-B.name: The gulf has reached reception
ENC-S24-B.desc: Trump put Gulf of America on federal maps. At a motel promotion, the owner gives a leaking lobby fountain the same name. He offers $12 to mop or a $5 shower token. The cleaner asks whether the expanding gulf now includes the carpet.
ENC-S24-B.log_0: You earn $12 and aching muscles. The owner calls your mop a territorial concession and asks you to stop shrinking America.
ENC-S24-B.log_1: You wash and clear your head. The shower’s water stays within its borders without anyone giving it a national identity.
ENC-S24-B.log_2: You leave annoyed. The owner shifts a tiny flag to the puddle’s edge, updating the map instead of calling the plumber.

ENC-S24-C.name: The welcome is dripping
ENC-S24-C.desc: Trump’s Gold Card offers an immigration route linked to a million-dollar gift. At a hotel’s promotional evening, a gold-colored ice gateway is melting over workers’ shoes. The attendant offers $12 to mop or a $5 shower. Wealthy arrivals enter through the dry side.
ENC-S24-C.log_0: Twelve dollars and aching muscles. You remove the wet border so the people buying special welcome never have to step in it.
ENC-S24-C.log_1: Five dollars buys a refreshing shower. Your welcome is smaller but has working drainage and no minimum donation.
ENC-S24-C.log_2: You leave irritated. The presenter asks someone to move the workers; their wet shoes are spoiling the photograph of a welcoming America.

ENC-S25-A.name: Same bombs, new letterhead
ENC-S25-A.desc: Trump gave the Defense Department “Department of War” as a second name. At a print shop, the printer offers $13 to sort new letterheads. He presents two invoices. “Same bombs. Twice the stationery.”
ENC-S25-A.log_0: You sort both names, save the invoices, and earn $13, head aching. The printer needs another cabinet for the expanded letterhead supply.
ENC-S25-A.log_1: You announce two armies by mistake. The crew laughs; the printer doubles his quote. You both briefly understand government contracting.
ENC-S25-A.log_2: You leave unpaid. The printer asks whether peace needs a separate invoice or whether nobody is ordering that.

ENC-S25-B.name: Evidence available in cardboard
ENC-S25-B.desc: The MAHA report cited nonexistent studies. At a conference printer, the owner offers $13 to sort poster components. A promotional design shows a tower of scientific evidence. The tower is cardboard, which at least exists.
ENC-S25-B.log_0: You earn $13 and preserve the errors, head aching. The cardboard passes its first evidence check by being physically present.
ENC-S25-B.log_1: The crew laughs at your solemn delivery. You praise an imaginary paper; the printer offers you a place inside the cardboard tower.
ENC-S25-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. The printer adds a stronger base, giving the scientific claim a kind of support it previously lacked.

ENC-S25-C.name: Original, in very large letters
ENC-S25-C.desc: The U.S. Copyright Office says prompting alone does not establish authorship of an AI output. An art-stall seller offers $13 to pair generated pictures with honest credit labels. He has made ORIGINAL larger than the picture. The lettering is doing most of the creative work.
ENC-S25-C.choice_0: Match the labels; save the guidance
ENC-S25-C.log_0: You earn $13 matching labels and save the guidance, head aching. The seller’s word original shrinks to match his actual contribution.
ENC-S25-C.choice_1: Give the computer an authorship award speech
ENC-S25-C.log_1: Your speech gets laughs and loses trust. The seller asks where the computer’s human author should stand for the presentation.
ENC-S25-C.log_2: You leave annoyed. The seller looks at the oversized lettering and considers doing some actual drawing before ordering a larger sign.

ENC-S26-A.name: The trail has become a notice
ENC-S26-A.desc: Albuquerque reported a federal attempt to withdraw Rail Trail money. At a Beltway supporters’ stall, the printer offers $9 to fold leaflets. A volunteer’s bicycle leans against the funding announcement. It is the only transport here receiving actual support from the paperwork.
ENC-S26-A.log_0: You share food and gain a contact. She moves the leaflet stack under her bicycle’s wobbly stand, getting one useful public service from it.
ENC-S26-A.log_1: Nine dollars and aching eyes earn an endorsement. You make the withdrawal notice compact enough for people to carry while walking.
ENC-S26-A.log_2: You leave disappointed. The volunteer rings her bicycle bell; the funding notice remains considerably less capable of moving people.

ENC-S26-B.name: Please silence the launch
ENC-S26-B.desc: Virginia ordered school divisions toward bell-to-bell phone policies. At a roadside school-supply drive, an organizer offers $9 to fold explanatory leaflets and welcomes lunch company. She keeps reaching for her phone to photograph the phone-free demonstration. The distraction has organizer privileges.
ENC-S26-B.choice_0: Share some food with the organizer
ENC-S26-B.log_0: You share lunch and exchange numbers. She puts the phone away long enough to discover that company is available without opening an app.
ENC-S26-B.log_1: You earn $9 and an endorsement through tired eyes. Each folded leaflet briefly blocks the organizer’s view of her own screen.
ENC-S26-B.log_2: You leave disappointed. She asks for one last photograph of everyone concentrating on something other than phones.

ENC-S26-C.name: The newborn cannot expense lunch
ENC-S26-C.desc: Trump Accounts offer eligible babies $1,000 unavailable for ordinary childhood spending. At a baby-supply charity sale, the organizer offers $9 to sort price tags. A parent holds an account notice beside diapers. The baby is attempting a hostile takeover of the receipt.
ENC-S26-C.choice_0: Share some food with the parent
ENC-S26-C.log_0: You share food and gain a contact. The parent eats while the baby crumples the notice into the nearest available financial product.
ENC-S26-C.log_1: Nine dollars and aching eyes earn the organizer’s endorsement. The diapers remain stubbornly priced for people who need them before retirement.
ENC-S26-C.log_2: You leave disappointed. The parent checks the notice again. The infant investor has expressed an immediate cash-flow problem directly into the stroller.

ENC-S27-A.name: The forty-two-cent department
ENC-S27-A.desc: Washington offered federal agencies Musk’s Grok AI for forty-two cents. A copy shop selling AI classes advertises that price for attendees and offers $6 to hang the banner. The class costs extra. So does being the wrong customer.
ENC-S27-A.choice_0: Save the offer and the proposed banner
ENC-S27-A.log_0: You save the agency-only terms despite the headache. The banner’s universal bargain shrinks to a very particular customer.
ENC-S27-A.log_1: You earn $6 and lose trust when readers discover the restriction. The owner has outsourced the expensive part: looking them in the eye.
ENC-S27-A.log_2: You leave annoyed. The owner checks whether folding the banner can conceal the part where his shop is not a federal agency.

ENC-S27-B.name: Five stars, no footsteps
ENC-S27-B.desc: The FTC prohibits fabricated consumer reviews. A motel owner offers $6 to hang a banner quoting guests his marketing service invented. The housekeeper has counted the occupied rooms. She would like to meet the delighted couple who apparently slept in the linen cupboard.
ENC-S27-B.choice_0: Save the review and room comparison
ENC-S27-B.log_0: You save the contradiction through tired eyes. The linen cupboard has excellent storage and an increasingly distinguished romantic history.
ENC-S27-B.log_1: You earn $6 and lose trust. A visitor asks for the famous suite; the housekeeper opens the cupboard and points at the towels.
ENC-S27-B.log_2: You leave irritated. The owner asks whether upgrading the cupboard’s pillows might make the review retroactively less imaginary.

ENC-S27-C.name: Approved by the printer
ENC-S27-C.desc: Trump floated fifty-year mortgages in 2025; that was a proposal, not an available nationwide program. A housing-leads seller offers $6 to hang WASHINGTON APPROVED FIFTY-YEAR LOANS. The only approval he can produce is the printer’s receipt.
ENC-S27-C.choice_0: Save the proposal and the seller’s claim
ENC-S27-C.log_0: You save both, head aching. The seller’s promised government program turns out to have been authorized by a man operating a laminator.
ENC-S27-C.log_1: You earn $6 and lose trust. A visitor asks where to apply; the seller offers another brochure instead of the program you advertised.
ENC-S27-C.log_2: You leave annoyed. The seller checks the laminator again, hoping its finished light might count as federal approval.

ENC-S28-A.name: The small briefcase strategy
ENC-S28-A.desc: Trump ordered limits on federally supported institutional home purchases, with definitions and implementation required. At an open-house cleanup, an agent has bought a smaller briefcase for corporate visitors. Sorting cards pays $12; a quiet break is available. The company itself refuses to fit inside.
ENC-S28-A.choice_0: Sort the cards; save the actual scope
ENC-S28-A.log_0: You sort cards for $12 and save the order, head aching. The agent’s briefcase has shrunk. His institutional investor has not.
ENC-S28-A.choice_1: Use your food; take a recovery break
ENC-S28-A.log_1: You eat and recover in the empty chair. The agent’s miniature briefcase remains incapable of making a corporation into a household.
ENC-S28-A.log_2: You leave irritated. The agent tries folding the corporate letterhead smaller, extending a remarkably ambitious interpretation of household size.

ENC-S28-B.name: Obsolete, with references
ENC-S28-B.desc: Duffy told Congress in 2025 that parts of air-traffic infrastructure still used floppy disks. At a surplus-electronics stall, sorting old media pays $12; a quiet break is available using your food. The seller has crossed obsolete off one basket. The price remains two dollars.
ENC-S28-B.choice_0: Sort the media; save the testimony
ENC-S28-B.log_0: You sort disks for $12 and save Duffy’s testimony, head aching. The oldest disk has outlasted the computer that promised to replace it.
ENC-S28-B.choice_1: Use your food; take a recovery break
ENC-S28-B.log_1: You eat and recover while the seller handles the fragile old media. Your break requires no compatibility adapter.
ENC-S28-B.log_2: You leave annoyed. The seller wraps a floppy disk carefully, newly aware that retirement can apparently be postponed by federal infrastructure.

ENC-S28-C.name: Fifty pages of affordability
ENC-S28-C.desc: Trump floated fifty-year mortgages in 2025. A roadside housing fair needs $12 worth of help assembling a sample payment calendar; its volunteer first-aider can also tend your aches using supplies you provide. The sample house has two rooms. The calendar needs three tables.
ENC-S28-C.log_0: You earn $12 and preserve the proposal, mentally exhausted. The pages keep arriving long after the little house runs out of rooms.
ENC-S28-C.choice_1: Use your supplies; see the first-aider
ENC-S28-C.log_1: Your supplies help you recover. The first-aider finishes a useful service without offering to spread it over fifty years.
ENC-S28-C.log_2: You leave frustrated. A volunteer asks for another table, the only immediately available expansion in the affordability proposal.

ENC-S29-A.name: The manuscript gets through
ENC-S29-A.desc: NIH’s July 2025 access policy makes covered new accepted manuscripts public without an embargo. At a library copy kiosk, matching versions pays $12. The author’s manuscript can be read free; the publisher’s glossy layout is a different product. The knowledge has escaped without its expensive jacket.
ENC-S29-A.log_0: You earn $12 and tired eyes. The plain manuscript contains the research despite arriving without the publisher’s carefully dressed cover.
ENC-S29-A.choice_1: Keep the public manuscript and publication details
ENC-S29-A.log_1: You save both records, eyes aching. The public copy opens immediately; the decorative cover no longer controls whether the ideas may enter.
ENC-S29-A.log_2: You leave the kiosk. The volunteer clips the plain pages together, supplying all the luxury binding needed to keep the research in order.

ENC-S29-B.name: The direct route is closed
ENC-S29-B.desc: Treasury suspended the IRS’s free Direct File tool for 2026; other free filing options remain. At a used-computer stall, a seller offers $12 to sort replacement labels for old tax-help kiosks. The machines still work. Only the part where government made itself convenient has broken.
ENC-S29-B.log_0: You earn $12 and a headache sorting “Direct File” from “Other filing options.” The computers pass every hardware test. The government needs a replacement part.
ENC-S29-B.choice_1: Preserve the old and new captions
ENC-S29-B.log_1: You save both captions and the IRS update, head aching. The seller keeps one old label: “File directly with us.” Apparently that was the experimental feature.
ENC-S29-B.log_2: You leave the job behind. He puts the empty kiosks on sale. “Taxes still mandatory,” he calls. “Helpful government sold separately.”

ENC-S29-C.name: Please sort the welcomes by income
ENC-S29-C.desc: Trump’s Gold Card ties an expedited immigration route to a million-dollar gift. At a promotional printer, the owner offers $12 to sort translated brochures. The gold editions say welcome on the cover. The ordinary immigration leaflet begins with several reasons to be nervous.
ENC-S29-C.log_0: You earn $12 and a headache. The same country greets readers in remarkably different tones depending on the price of the cover.
ENC-S29-C.choice_1: Keep the public brochures and terms
ENC-S29-C.log_1: You preserve the comparison, mentally tired. A large gift makes the border’s language lessons progress directly to hospitality.
ENC-S29-C.log_2: You leave the job behind. The printer adds another layer of gold, apparently the international symbol for this applicant will be treated as an asset.

ENC-S30-A.name: The campaign for a path needs a van
ENC-S30-A.desc: Albuquerque reported an attempted federal withdrawal of Rail Trail funds. At a coastal transport meeting, an organizer offers $15 to deliver campaign materials using your own packing supplies. A commuter has the correspondence. Once again, the working route belongs to somebody else.
ENC-S30-A.log_0: You spend supplies and earn $15. The posters promising movement reach the meeting because the van never waited for the funding announcement.
ENC-S30-A.choice_1: Compare the correspondence with the commuter
ENC-S30-A.log_1: You gain evidence and a contact, head aching. The promised path currently moves most efficiently when printed small enough for somebody to carry.
ENC-S30-A.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The organizer checks your van’s departure time with more urgency than the campaign’s map has ever received.

ENC-S30-B.name: The welcome cannot carry itself
ENC-S30-B.desc: Trump’s Gold Card offers expedited immigration linked to a million-dollar gift. At a coastal information event, $15 is offered to deliver welcome boxes using your supplies. A hotel worker has the public terms. The boxes are too heavy for the people being welcomed.
ENC-S30-B.log_0: You spend supplies and earn $15. The expensive welcome reaches its destination through people whose own welcome has never required a ribbon.
ENC-S30-B.choice_1: Read the terms with the worker
ENC-S30-B.log_1: You gain a contact and evidence, mentally tired. The brochure calls wealth a contribution; carrying the brochure’s furniture earns a much smaller word.
ENC-S30-B.log_2: You leave the offer behind. An organizer asks whether the welcome can be made lighter without reducing the impression of money.

ENC-S30-C.name: No wind, except for the banner
ENC-S30-C.desc: Trump paused new federal wind-project approvals. At an energy meeting, an organizer offers $15 to deliver display materials using your supplies. A technician has the order. The anti-wind banner keeps escaping across the car park, apparently unaware it should wait for a review.
ENC-S30-C.log_0: You spend supplies and earn $15. The banner needs extra fastening to keep its opposition to wind from being carried away by wind.
ENC-S30-C.choice_1: Read the order with the technician
ENC-S30-C.log_1: You gain a contact and evidence through a headache. The breeze supplies an unscheduled demonstration while the discussion of whether to permit it continues.
ENC-S30-C.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The organizer chases the banner, discovering that opposition to wind still requires an effective relationship with it.

ENC-S31-A.name: Paid by the century
ENC-S31-A.desc: Wisconsin’s court upheld Governor Evers’s deletion of budget characters extending school revenue-limit increases to 2425, not guaranteed appropriations. A roadside printer offers $14 to align comparison cards and welcomes shared lunch. He is reconsidering the phrase annual printing contract.
ENC-S31-A.choice_0: Align the cards; keep the comparison
ENC-S31-A.log_0: You earn $14 and save the comparison, eyes aching. A few missing characters have given the printer several centuries of extra calendar space.
ENC-S31-A.choice_1: Share some food; rest with the printer
ENC-S31-A.log_1: You share lunch, recover, and exchange numbers. He promises to repay the favor this century, a modest improvement on the school calendar.
ENC-S31-A.log_2: You leave the stall. The printer checks the date on his next invoice very carefully before letting anyone near the scissors.

ENC-S31-B.name: Purchasing should be the deliberate bit
ENC-S31-B.desc: The federal consumer watchdog refunded unwanted Fortnite purchases. At a used-console stall, a worker offers $14 to label demonstration controls and keep the comparison. You may share lunch and rest here. The pretend purchase button is huge. The pretend confirmation button is apparently shy.
ENC-S31-B.choice_0: Label the controls; save the comparison
ENC-S31-B.log_0: You earn $14 and tired eyes. The demonstration finally gives buying something as clear a label as moving a cartoon person left.
ENC-S31-B.choice_1: Share some food; take a break
ENC-S31-B.log_1: You share food, recover, and gain a contact. The worker asks before taking a second biscuit, demonstrating a complete purchasing philosophy.
ENC-S31-B.log_2: You leave the stall. The worker enlarges the confirmation label until an ordinary finger can finally see what it is agreeing to.

ENC-S31-C.name: The after-coffee instructions
ENC-S31-C.desc: The SEC fined Keurig over incomplete recyclability disclosures. At a coffee-equipment co-op, a worker offers $14 to match sample pods with local collection instructions, or a shared lunch break. Making coffee takes one button. Dealing with the company’s environmental claim has filled the other counter.
ENC-S31-C.choice_0: Match the instructions; save the comparison
ENC-S31-C.log_0: You earn $14 and tired eyes. The sorting guide finally includes the collectors’ answer, which the confident sales display had treated as optional.
ENC-S31-C.choice_1: Share some food; rest with the worker
ENC-S31-C.log_1: You share lunch, recover, and gain a contact. The worker pours ordinary water, briefly avoiding a product that needs a disposal seminar.
ENC-S31-C.log_2: You leave the co-op. The worker clears space beside the coffee machine for the instructions required after its simple part is over.

ENC-S32-A.name: The wind has not read the order
ENC-S32-A.desc: Trump paused new federal wind-project approvals. At a turbine-repair stall, a technician offers $10 to sort spare-part labels. He keeps the order under a paperweight. The breeze removes the paperweight’s supporting documents every time somebody praises the pause.
ENC-S32-A.log_0: Ten dollars and a headache. The technician retrieves another page from the hedge; wind continues producing results without waiting for the speech to finish.
ENC-S32-A.log_1: You gain evidence and a contact, mentally tired. He distinguishes paused approvals from moving air, a distinction the flying order demonstrates repeatedly.
ENC-S32-A.log_2: You leave the offer behind. A speaker asks someone to hold the paperwork still while he explains the advantages of stopping wind development.

ENC-S32-B.name: The unreliable panel is doing the work
ENC-S32-B.desc: Trump ordered strict enforcement of wind and solar tax-credit terminations, calling those sources unreliable. At a repair fair, a technician offers $10 to sort component labels. The anti-solar presentation is powered by the small solar panel nobody wants included in the photograph.
ENC-S32-B.log_0: Ten dollars and aching eyes. The panel powers another slide explaining its unreliability; the technician asks whether it should stop interrupting the argument.
ENC-S32-B.choice_1: Save the setup and technician’s account
ENC-S32-B.log_1: You gain evidence and a contact through a headache. The presentation’s most reliable participant is the one being accused on every slide.
ENC-S32-B.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The photographer moves the panel out of frame, successfully reducing visible solar dependence without reducing solar dependence.

ENC-S32-C.name: An actual choice
ENC-S32-C.desc: After a court restricted Google’s exclusive distribution deals, a computer refurbisher makes a demonstration keyboard with several search keys. Sorting spare keycaps pays $10; he also invites you to check the ruling. Previously, his display offered four choices of the same button.
ENC-S32-C.log_0: You earn $10 and tired eyes. The refurbished keyboard can finally suggest that a choice might lead somewhere different.
ENC-S32-C.choice_1: Record the ruling with the refurbisher
ENC-S32-C.log_1: You save the exclusivity distinction, mentally tired, and gain a contact. He keeps Google available; the demonstration needs competition, not a disappearance trick.
ENC-S32-C.log_2: You leave the stall. The refurbisher tests a second search key and enjoys its modest refusal to be the first one.

ENC-S33-A.name: The tank has run out of freedom
ENC-S33-A.desc: Trump ordered showerhead deregulation. At a desert service stop, a celebratory display is draining the tank. The plumber offers water for help shutting it off or $12 for the heavier work. The owner asks whether the empty tank is refusing to cooperate politically.
ENC-S33-A.choice_0: Help shut it off; take water
ENC-S33-A.log_0: You gain water and some peace of mind. The plumber demonstrates the off switch, a technology omitted from the freedom ceremony.
ENC-S33-A.log_1: Twelve dollars and sore muscles. You haul the equipment while the owner asks whether refilling the tank counts as government interference.
ENC-S33-A.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The display coughs; the owner checks the banner instead of the water level.

ENC-S33-B.name: A nationally protected blockage
ENC-S33-B.desc: Trump ordered federal agencies back to plastic straws. At a desert drinks promotion, the giant ceremonial straw blocks the refill station. The installer offers water for clearing the walkway or $12 to move its heavy base. The straw has secured access to all the drinks.
ENC-S33-B.log_0: You gain water and clear your head. Ordinary people can reach the tap once the national drinking priority moves out of their way.
ENC-S33-B.log_1: Twelve dollars and aching muscles. You carry the object designed to prove that drinking ought to require less effort.
ENC-S33-B.log_2: You leave the offer behind. The installer bends the giant straw sideways, achieving the national strategy’s first practical compromise with thirst.

ENC-S33-C.name: The inspection left a forwarding fee
ENC-S33-C.desc: Texas ended most noncommercial safety inspections but kept a $7.50 inspection-program replacement fee. At a Texas garage, the mechanic offers water for clearing access or $12 to shift barriers. The inspection bay is empty. Its fee has kept the appointment.
ENC-S33-C.log_0: You clear the approach, collect water, and enjoy a useful result. The empty inspection bay contributes no further inspection to the arrangement.
ENC-S33-C.log_1: You earn $12 and sore muscles. The barriers move on; the replacement fee has secured a more permanent position.
ENC-S33-C.log_2: You leave the garage. The mechanic checks the empty bay once more, just in case the fee has grown an inspector.

ENC-S34-A.name: A fee for the lack of money
ENC-S34-A.desc: Congress repealed the CFPB’s new overdraft rule for very large banks. At a roadside payroll kiosk, a clerk offers $16 to match account notices and invites a closer comparison. The charge is easiest to describe when the customer can least afford the description.
ENC-S34-A.log_0: You earn $16 and tired eyes. The account receives a charge for running short, then has to run shorter to cover it.
ENC-S34-A.choice_1: Compare the repeal with the old options
ENC-S34-A.log_1: You read until your eyes ache. Charging someone for having no money remains a remarkably confident business model.
ENC-S34-A.log_2: You leave the kiosk. Its empty coin dish remains the most accurate illustration of the customer account.

ENC-S34-B.name: Ten fewer ways to fold
ENC-S34-B.desc: Trump told agencies to identify ten rules to scrap for each new one. A hotel owner is copying him: one new towel rule has cost him ten folding instructions. He offers $16 to sort linen labels. His fitted sheet has captured one arm. Deregulation is reaching for the other.
ENC-S34-B.log_0: You earn $16 and rest your aching eyes. The sorted tags say FITTED. The owner asks whether you could repeal that part too.
ENC-S34-B.choice_1: Compare his claim with the old instructions
ENC-S34-B.log_1: You save his boast, the order and both instruction cards, head aching. One new rule removed ten useful steps. The sheet now contains less regulation and one whole owner.
ENC-S34-B.log_2: You leave the offer behind. He announces that he has eliminated red tape. The elastic captures his other arm.

ENC-S34-C.name: Tomorrow’s investor needs today’s invoice
ENC-S34-C.desc: Trump Accounts offer eligible newborns $1,000 unavailable for childhood bills. At a baby-goods warehouse, $16 is offered to sort delivery labels. A parent compares the account announcement with a diaper invoice. The baby has begun rejecting delayed gratification at full volume.
ENC-S34-C.log_0: Sixteen dollars and a headache. The diaper boxes leave today; the money meant to celebrate the baby’s future remains admirably patient.
ENC-S34-C.choice_1: Compare the account rules with the invoice
ENC-S34-C.log_1: You save the mismatch through aching eyes. The parent asks whether the diapers might accept a payment schedule based on adulthood.
ENC-S34-C.log_2: You leave the job behind. The baby grabs the announcement, becoming the first person here to extract immediate practical entertainment from it.

CARE-01-A.name: Alive With Goodness
CARE-01-A.desc: {name} tries raw milk from a “Make America Healthy Again” stall. The vendor calls it “alive with goodness.” Judging by the screaming from the toilet, the goodness has a knife.
CARE-01-A.continuing: {name} is still ill from the MAHA raw milk. The vendor has promoted the stomach cramps to a cleansing process.
CARE-01-A.log_0: {name} recovers with care. The vendor asks for a testimonial. You offer the bathroom key.

CARE-01-B.name: The Freedom Fridge
CARE-01-B.desc: {name} drinks raw milk at a MAHA stall opposing government food rules. They start vomiting. The vendor checks the fridge: unplugged, in protest.
CARE-01-B.continuing: {name} is still sick. The vendor says refrigeration is a slippery slope to federal control of cheese.
CARE-01-B.log_0: {name} recovers. The vendor plugs in the fridge and asks you to keep his surrender quiet.

CARE-01-C.name: A Second Opinion
CARE-01-C.desc: A MAHA vendor tells {name} raw milk builds immunity. Now they’re ill. He recommends a second bottle. Apparently the immune system needs a rematch.
CARE-01-C.continuing: {name} remains ill. The unopened second bottle sits in the van like a very small hostile nation.
CARE-01-C.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. You decline the rematch. The bottle keeps its undefeated record.

CARE-02-A.name: Executive Forecast
CARE-02-A.desc: During a paid unloading shift, {name} becomes dehydrated. The boss crossed out the heat warning with a Sharpie, but apparently, the sun doesn’t take corrections. #sharpiegate
CARE-02-A.continuing: {name} is still dehydrated. The Sharpie has made a full recovery and returned to management.
CARE-02-A.log_0: Care restores {name}. The sun continues operating outside the boss’s chain of command.

CARE-02-B.name: Local Control
CARE-02-B.desc: During an unloading shift, {name} becomes dehydrated. The boss praises Florida’s ban on local heat-break rules. “Government shouldn’t tell us what to do,” he says, blocking the water.
CARE-02-B.continuing: {name} remains dehydrated. The boss’s freedom to manage has developed an impressive thirst.
CARE-02-B.log_0: {name} recovers with care. For several revolutionary minutes, thirst gets a vote.

CARE-02-C.name: Drill, Baby, Drink
CARE-02-C.desc: {name} becomes dehydrated unloading a “Drill, baby, drill” rally stage. The organizer says heat is natural. So is the ice in his private cooler.
CARE-02-C.continuing: {name} is still dehydrated. The organizer has ordered more ice for his argument.
CARE-02-C.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. The organizer guards the cooler like the last remaining oil reserve.

CARE-03-A.name: Proof of Labor
CARE-03-A.desc: After a temp shift, {name} stays up proving those hours count under Congress’s benefits work rules. By dawn, the only unpaid work is proving they work.
CARE-03-A.continuing: {name} is exhausted from the benefits paperwork. Their shift is documented; the night spent proving it remains volunteer work.
CARE-03-A.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. You put the forms away before they develop a work requirement of their own.

CARE-03-B.name: Efficient Exhaustion
CARE-03-B.desc: {name} loses sleep helping a laid-off DOGE-cut worker assemble job applications. The government called them redundant. Every employer wants the same information entered again.
CARE-03-B.continuing: {name} is still exhausted. The last application has asked the worker to upload the résumé it just deleted.
CARE-03-B.log_0: Care restores {name}. For once, something has been saved without creating a new account.

CARE-03-C.name: The Merit Test
CARE-03-C.desc: {name} loses a night applying for a government contractor’s temp work. The firm denounces DEI. Its application asks whether the owner’s nephew referred them. He’s twelve.
CARE-03-C.continuing: {name} remains exhausted. The nephew’s referral box is still the shortest route through the merit system.
CARE-03-C.log_0: {name} recovers. The nephew is unavailable for comment; it’s a school night.

CARE-04-A.name: Drain the Sample Bucket
CARE-04-A.desc: {name} tries a MAHA tonic promising to “drain the swamp” from their body. They vomit into the sample bucket. The swamp has acquired a gift shop.
CARE-04-A.continuing: {name} is still sick from the tonic. The vendor says discomfort proves it works. Refunds apparently prove nothing.
CARE-04-A.log_0: {name} recovers with care. The vendor offers a loyalty card. You suggest a mop.

CARE-04-B.name: The Unelected Stomach
CARE-04-B.desc: {name} becomes sick after a MAHA supplement sample. The vendor blames unelected health experts. Nobody recalls voting for the powder, either.
CARE-04-B.continuing: {name} remains ill. The vendor has demanded an investigation into the stomach’s political affiliations.
CARE-04-B.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. Their stomach accepts the result without demanding a recount.

CARE-04-C.name: Personal Responsibility, Now in Mango
CARE-04-C.desc: {name} tries a MAHA cleanse sold as freedom from the FDA. Now they’re sick. The vendor celebrates personal responsibility by pointing at the customer.
CARE-04-C.continuing: {name} is still ill. The vendor’s cure for government overreach has reached the entire stomach.
CARE-04-C.log_0: {name} recovers. You ask the vendor to take some personal responsibility. He suddenly has a lawyer.

CARE-05-A.name: Patriotically Lost
CARE-05-A.desc: {name} loses sleep reconciling maps after Trump’s Gulf and mountain renaming. The van still needs the same turn. Geography has failed its loyalty test.
CARE-05-A.continuing: {name} is exhausted. Two maps disagree about the name of something that has not moved.
CARE-05-A.log_0: Care restores {name}. You follow the road, which has managed to stay in office.

CARE-05-B.name: The Mountain Formerly Known
CARE-05-B.desc: {name} stays up matching a renamed federal landmark to an older route guide. A mountain has two names. Somehow the human has to do the paperwork.
CARE-05-B.continuing: {name} is still exhausted. The mountain has declined to provide a preferred spelling.
CARE-05-B.log_0: {name} recovers. You agree to recognize the mountain by the enormous mountain underneath the name.

CARE-05-C.name: Rebranding Detour
CARE-05-C.desc: {name} loses sleep updating the route after another federal renaming announcement. The app celebrates American greatness by sending you past the same gas station twice.
CARE-05-C.continuing: {name} remains exhausted. The renamed destination is secure; the route to it is doing a victory lap.
CARE-05-C.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. You disable the celebratory update and keep the actual road.

CARE-06-A.name: A Very Small Trade War
CARE-06-A.desc: {name} spends all night disputing Trump’s tariff on a van part. By dawn, they’re waving a white napkin at the card reader. It asks for a tip.
CARE-06-A.continuing: {name} is exhausted from the tariff dispute. China has not sent a relief driver.
CARE-06-A.log_0: {name} recovers with care. You declare a ceasefire with the receipt printer.

CARE-06-B.name: America First in Line
CARE-06-B.desc: {name} loses sleep tracing a “foreign-paid” tariff through the repair quote. Every arrow leads back to your wallet. America first, apparently.
CARE-06-B.continuing: {name} remains exhausted. You have traced international trade to the lint in the van’s coin tray.
CARE-06-B.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. The coin tray is formally cleared of responsibility for China.

CARE-06-C.name: The Tariff Hotline
CARE-06-C.desc: {name} stays up calling about a tariff on the van’s replacement part. The hotline promises to connect them with whoever pays it. Their own phone starts ringing.
CARE-06-C.continuing: {name} is still exhausted. The hold music has survived three attempts to make China answer.
CARE-06-C.log_0: {name} recovers. You let the next call go to voicemail. International relations can leave a message.

CARE-07-A.name: Five Things Before Breakfast
CARE-07-A.desc: {name} loses sleep helping a DOGE-cut friend list their work for an efficiency review. They count five tasks. The person requesting the list has created a sixth.
CARE-07-A.continuing: {name} remains exhausted. The review has classified time spent answering the review as administrative waste.
CARE-07-A.log_0: Care restores {name}. You record one completed task: keeping an actual person functioning.

CARE-07-B.name: Secure Group Chat
CARE-07-B.desc: After a loading job, {name} spends the night sorting the boss’s endless group messages. He copied the Pentagon’s bombing-plan chat. Nobody is sure who invited the pizza delivery driver.
CARE-07-B.continuing: {name} is still exhausted. The delivery driver knows tomorrow’s rota and would prefer to know who ordered garlic bread.
CARE-07-B.log_0: {name} recovers. You mute the chat before the boss authorizes a second shift by emoji.

CARE-07-C.name: The Need-to-Know Shift
CARE-07-C.desc: {name} loses sleep after a temp boss copies the Signal bombing-plan scandal: rota, payroll, everyone’s phone number, one chat. He says it’s secure because the group has a padlock emoji.
CARE-07-C.continuing: {name} remains exhausted. The padlock emoji has not prevented the boss’s uncle from replying to all.
CARE-07-C.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. You remove the notifications. The emoji remains bravely on duty.

CARE-08-A.name: Self-Made, Staff Carried
CARE-08-A.desc: At a paid unloading job for a billionaire’s political fundraiser, {name} injures their back moving his memoir, I Did It All Myself. The donor steps over them to reach the podium.
CARE-08-A.continuing: {name} remains injured. The donor’s speech about self-reliance has required another pair of hands to turn the pages.
CARE-08-A.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. You leave the remaining memoirs to pull themselves up by their dust jackets.

CARE-08-B.name: The Donation Photo
CARE-08-B.desc: {name} strains their back moving food-pantry donations as the radio covers Congress’s SNAP cuts. A politician arrives to lift an empty box. Finally, a balanced workload.
CARE-08-B.continuing: {name} is still injured. The politician’s empty box has appeared in three photographs without requiring medical attention.
CARE-08-B.log_0: {name} recovers with care. The empty box is unavailable to help; it has a press conference.

CARE-08-C.name: The Smaller Delivery Service
CARE-08-C.desc: At a food pantry discussing Congress’s food-aid cuts, {name} helps haul sacks and strains their back. The volunteer calls it trickle-down. Nothing appears to be trickling; it’s all carrying.
CARE-08-C.continuing: {name} remains injured. The pantry still has sacks to move and no billionaire has dripped out of the ceiling.
CARE-08-C.log_0: Care helps {name} recover. The next sack can wait for the invisible hand.

REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.name: China Is Running Late
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.desc: The alternator fails. The replacement costs more after Trump’s tariffs. The mechanic on the radio asks who’s paying. You say China. She asks for a shorter joke.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.log_0: You fit the onboard spare. China is excused from this particular invoice.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.log_1: The shop fits the replacement. Your money crosses the counter with remarkable international confidence.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.log_2: You barter supplies for a used alternator and fit it. The food accepts responsibility for the tariff.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.log_3: You do the arranged work for a used alternator and repair. China’s shift looks exactly like your crew.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.roadside: The replacement arrives and is fitted. The driver asks for you by name, which settles who is paying.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-A.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.name: The One-Person Department
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.desc: The alternator quits. You’ve been asking one tired part to charge the battery and power everything, which is also DOGE’s staffing plan.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.log_0: You fit the spare. The new department head is immediately given all the old department’s work.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.log_1: The shop fits a replacement. Restoring capacity is briefly mistaken for waste.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.log_2: You trade supplies for a used alternator and fit it. The van reluctantly agrees to retain an experienced worker.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.log_3: You finish the arranged work and fit a used alternator. The crew handles the workload that the efficiency slogan declined.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.roadside: The replacement arrives and is fitted. The delivery driver is spared a presentation about doing more with less.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-B.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.name: Charging for Access
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.desc: The alternator dies. A political fundraiser on the radio offers dinner with a senator. You’d prefer access to twelve volts, but nobody has bought those a ballroom.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.log_0: You fit the spare. The van accepts a contribution within the engine compartment.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.log_1: The shop fits the replacement. Your payment secures access to electricity and absolutely no senator.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.log_2: You barter supplies for a used alternator and fit it. The food produces a more measurable return than a donor dinner.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.log_3: You complete the arranged work and fit the used part. Sweeping a garage buys more movement than meeting a senator.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.roadside: The replacement arrives and is fitted. The driver does not call the delivery a private audience.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-ALTERNATOR-C.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-BATTERY-A.name: Five Accomplishments, Zero Volts
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.desc: The battery dies. Inspired by DOGE, a crewmate asks it to list five accomplishments. It has powered every departure. Management asks what it did today.
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.log_0: The spare battery is fitted. Its first accomplishment is making the dashboard stop being a mirror.
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.log_1: The shop fits a replacement. You approve electricity without hiring a billionaire to investigate it.
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.log_2: You barter supplies for a used battery and fit it. Experience survives another efficiency initiative.
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.log_3: You finish the arranged work and fit a used battery. The four-hour productivity review includes actual productivity.
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.roadside: The replacement is delivered and fitted. The driver has accomplished something visible before sending an email.
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-BATTERY-A.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-BATTERY-B.name: Energy Dominance, Locally Unavailable
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.desc: The battery dies halfway through Trump’s “American energy dominance” speech. The slogan finishes on your phone. National abundance has terrible coverage.
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.log_0: The spare battery is fitted. The van achieves the radical policy objective of starting.
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.log_1: The shop fits the replacement. Energy dominance arrives with a bill in your name.
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.log_2: You trade supplies for a used battery and fit it. Nobody says “dominance.” The engine starts anyway.
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.log_3: The agreed work earns a used battery and repair. Your arms supply the energy policy.
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.roadside: The battery is delivered and fitted. The driver carries more usable energy than the entire speech.
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-BATTERY-B.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-BATTERY-C.name: The Qualified Candidate
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.desc: Your battery fails. The radio blames another problem on DEI. Under the hood, the positive and negative terminals have worked together for years. Neither will comment.
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.log_0: You fit the spare. Positive and negative resume their suspiciously inclusive arrangement.
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.log_1: The shop fits the replacement. Nobody asks the voltage for its political affiliations.
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.log_2: You barter supplies for a used battery and fit it. The van selects its candidate by starting.
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.log_3: You finish the arranged work and fit a used battery. Competence turns out to involve connecting things.
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.roadside: The replacement arrives and is fitted. The driver connects both terminals despite the radio’s concerns.
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-BATTERY-C.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.name: Drill, Baby, Nothing
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.desc: The fuel pump fails. Trump’s “Drill, baby, drill” plays on the radio. Finding more oil is an unusually loud answer to the wrong broken part.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.log_0: You fit the spare pump. Fuel reaches the engine without finding a new oilfield.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.log_1: The shop fits a replacement. Distribution briefly gets more attention than drilling.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.log_2: You barter supplies for a used pump and fit it. The tank’s existing reserves finally reach the public.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.log_3: You complete the arranged work and fit a used pump. Your arms solve a problem the drilling speech could not reach.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.roadside: The replacement arrives and is fitted. The driver repairs the route between the fuel you have and the engine that needs it.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-A.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.name: A Very Patriotic Obstruction
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.desc: The fuel pump fails. Trump’s tariff pitch says barriers protect American industry. The engine is currently protected from gasoline and has no follow-up questions.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.log_0: You fit the spare pump. Fuel negotiates passage into the engine.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.log_1: The shop fits a replacement. You pay for the pump, including the protection from cheaper pumps.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.log_2: You trade supplies for a used pump and fit it. Domestic leftovers reopen the fuel route.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.log_3: The agreed work earns a used pump and repair. The crew provides the labor; China remains unavailable for shifts.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.roadside: The pump is delivered and fitted. The barrier between you and your money also comes down.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-B.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.name: The Internal Group Chat
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.desc: The fuel pump stops sending fuel to the engine. After the leaked bombing-plan chat, you check the exhaust. Perhaps the important stuff went to the wrong recipient.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.log_0: You fit the spare pump. The engine is finally included in the distribution list.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.log_1: The shop fits a replacement. Fuel goes to the engine, an apparently elite level of operational security.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.log_2: You barter supplies for a used pump and fit it. The engine receives the briefing in a format it can burn.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.log_3: You complete the arranged work and fit a used pump. The van resumes keeping its combustion plans inside the engine.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.roadside: The replacement arrives and is fitted. The driver manages to deliver a sensitive object to its intended recipient.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-FUELPUMP-C.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-TIRE-A.name: Trickle-Down Tread
REPAIR-TIRE-A.desc: A tire bursts beside a billionaire-funded tax-cut billboard. You find the tread beneath “prosperity.” So that’s the part that trickles down.
REPAIR-TIRE-A.log_0: You fit the spare. Wealth has not redistributed itself, but weight has.
REPAIR-TIRE-A.log_1: The shop fits the replacement. The billionaire’s billboard remains strangely unwilling to co-sign.
REPAIR-TIRE-A.log_2: You barter supplies for a used tire and fit it. An exchange with two actual beneficiaries feels suspiciously radical.
REPAIR-TIRE-A.log_3: You finish the agreed work and fit a used tire. The self-made van required other people again.
REPAIR-TIRE-A.roadside: The replacement arrives and is fitted. The delivery driver brings rubber; trickle-down economics sent nothing.
REPAIR-TIRE-A.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-TIRE-A.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-TIRE-B.name: Protected From Tires
REPAIR-TIRE-B.desc: Your tire fails. A replacement quote includes Trump’s tariffs. You check the old tire for patriotism. It is still mostly hole.
REPAIR-TIRE-B.log_0: The spare is fitted. Its country of origin remains less important than its supply of tire.
REPAIR-TIRE-B.log_1: The shop fits the replacement. America is one tire richer and you are considerably poorer.
REPAIR-TIRE-B.log_2: You trade supplies for a used tire and fit it. The tire has already survived one economy.
REPAIR-TIRE-B.log_3: You finish the arranged work for a used tire and repair. Bringing manufacturing home apparently starts with sweeping the garage.
REPAIR-TIRE-B.roadside: The replacement is delivered and fitted. China does not accompany the driver with your change.
REPAIR-TIRE-B.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-TIRE-B.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

REPAIR-TIRE-C.name: A More Flattering Tire
REPAIR-TIRE-C.desc: The tire splits. On the radio, Trump wants museums to emphasize American greatness. You turn the good side outward. The van remains difficult to drive as an exhibit.
REPAIR-TIRE-C.log_0: You fit the spare. Correcting the problem works better than curating it.
REPAIR-TIRE-C.log_1: The shop fits a replacement. The old tire retires before writing its own museum label.
REPAIR-TIRE-C.log_2: You barter supplies for a used tire and fit it. Its difficult history includes several useful years of being round.
REPAIR-TIRE-C.log_3: You complete the arranged work and fit the used tire. The old one can finally focus on its legacy.
REPAIR-TIRE-C.roadside: A replacement arrives and is fitted. The delivery driver declines a tour of the good side.
REPAIR-TIRE-C.incomplete: The repair is not complete. The van remains broken.
REPAIR-TIRE-C.cashless: Radio contacts can arrange work in exchange for a used part and repair. No cash or spare is needed.

CROSS-01-A.name: American Enough
CROSS-01-A.desc: At the checkpoint, an officer demands an American-made van. You open the hood. He starts an international incident with the alternator.
CROSS-01-A.passage: He waves you through. The alternator is admitted on a temporary work visa.
CROSS-01-A.diversion: You take the detour. The alternator remains suspiciously good at its job.
CROSS-01-A.permit_receipt: Your permit clears the van. The alternator is included as a dependent. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-01-A.permit_tag: Your permit clears the van. The alternator is included as a dependent. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-01-A.bribe_success: The payment clears the barrier. Your money passes the nationality test.
CROSS-01-A.bribe_failure: He takes the payment and keeps the barrier down. Apparently tariffs work here too.
CROSS-01-A.refused_passage: The officer refuses passage. You take the detour, with the alleged foreign threat still charging the battery.

CROSS-01-B.name: Geographic Contraband
CROSS-01-B.desc: The checkpoint officer spots “Gulf of Mexico” on your map. Trump renamed it. The officer holds the map by one corner, like it might leak Mexicans.
CROSS-01-B.passage: He lets you pass after folding the offending Gulf out of sight. The ocean has been contained.
CROSS-01-B.diversion: You take the detour. Both names continue to contain the same water.
CROSS-01-B.permit_receipt: Your permit is accepted. Apparently the map has diplomatic immunity. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-01-B.permit_tag: Your permit is accepted. Apparently the map has diplomatic immunity. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-01-B.bribe_success: The payment gets you through. He becomes surprisingly relaxed about where things come from.
CROSS-01-B.bribe_failure: He takes the payment but refuses passage. You have purchased a very patriotic delay.
CROSS-01-B.refused_passage: He refuses passage. You detour around the checkpoint; the Gulf stays where it was.

CROSS-01-C.name: Where Was the Van Born?
CROSS-01-C.desc: The checkpoint officer announces Trump-style extreme vetting. He asks where the van was born. You point to the manufacturer’s plate. “Long-form certificate,” he says.
CROSS-01-C.passage: You are waved through. The van’s citizenship interview has not improved its suspension.
