CROSS-01-C.diversion: You detour. The van is now accused of taking jobs from American vans.
CROSS-01-C.permit_receipt: Your permit is accepted. The van is apparently a naturalized cargo space. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-01-C.permit_tag: Your permit is accepted. The van is apparently a naturalized cargo space. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-01-C.bribe_success: The payment opens the barrier. The van has qualified for the investor route.
CROSS-01-C.bribe_failure: The payment is taken; the barrier stays down. The van’s investment has become foreign aid.
CROSS-01-C.refused_passage: Passage is refused. You take the detour before he asks the spare tire for its grandparents.

CROSS-02C-A.name: The Department of Barrier
CROSS-02C-A.desc: The crossing office has copied Trump’s “Department of War” makeover. The new nameplate is enormous. Behind it, two workers are holding up the barrier by hand.
CROSS-02C-A.passage: You cross while the workers hold the barrier. The nameplate offers strong moral support.
CROSS-02C-A.diversion: You take the detour. The new department has secured a decisive victory over traffic.
CROSS-02C-A.permit_receipt: The permit clears you. A worker lifts the barrier with his actual defense budget: both arms. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-02C-A.permit_tag: The permit clears you. A worker lifts the barrier with his actual defense budget: both arms. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-02C-A.bribe_success: The payment gets the barrier raised. The department has discovered arms funding.
CROSS-02C-A.bribe_failure: The payment disappears into the office. The workers still have only the original two arms each.
CROSS-02C-A.terminal_failure: You cannot complete this crossing. The expedition ends beneath a nameplate large enough to hide the problem.

CROSS-02C-B.name: Merit-Based Concrete
CROSS-02C-B.desc: The crossing boss boasts that he removed DEI from the inspection checklist. He points to a crack in the concrete. “That’s a diversity of surfaces.”
CROSS-02C-B.passage: You make it across. The concrete remains unpersuaded by the personnel policy.
CROSS-02C-B.diversion: You detour. The boss has successfully excluded your van from the bridge.
CROSS-02C-B.permit_receipt: Your permit is accepted. Paperwork has passed a load-bearing test that paperwork really shouldn’t be taking. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-02C-B.permit_tag: Your permit is accepted. Paperwork has passed a load-bearing test that paperwork really shouldn’t be taking. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-02C-B.bribe_success: The payment clears the crossing. Merit has turned out to have a cash option.
CROSS-02C-B.bribe_failure: The payment is taken, but passage is refused. You have funded another investigation into the concrete’s pronouns.
CROSS-02C-B.terminal_failure: This crossing ends the expedition. The boss’s review recommends less diversity in the complaint form.

CROSS-02C-C.name: China Will Fix It
CROSS-02C-C.desc: At the crossing, workers have priced replacement steel after Trump’s tariffs. The supervisor keeps refreshing his inbox for China’s payment. A cone has been promoted to bridge repair.
CROSS-02C-C.passage: You cross. The cone remains the project’s most dependable appointment.
CROSS-02C-C.diversion: You take the detour. China has not responded to the supervisor’s fifth reminder.
CROSS-02C-C.permit_receipt: Your permit clears you. The supervisor briefly considers invoicing it for steel. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-02C-C.permit_tag: Your permit clears you. The supervisor briefly considers invoicing it for steel. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-02C-C.bribe_success: The payment clears the barrier. The supervisor puts it in the folder meant for China’s contribution.
CROSS-02C-C.bribe_failure: The payment is taken without passage. You have been mistaken for another country with spare money.
CROSS-02C-C.terminal_failure: The crossing cannot be completed. Your expedition ends; the cone receives another term.

CROSS-02D-A.name: The Privacy Camera
CROSS-02D-A.desc: The checkpoint’s Flock camera is advertised as protection. A woman ahead asks who protects her when an officer uses it to stalk her. The guard points to a second camera.
CROSS-02D-A.passage: You pass. The second camera is apparently supervising the first camera’s personal growth.
CROSS-02D-A.diversion: You take the diversion. The privacy notice promises to record your concerns, along with your number plate.
CROSS-02D-A.permit_receipt: Your permit is accepted. The guard briefly experiences identifying someone without stalking them. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-02D-A.permit_tag: Your permit is accepted. The guard briefly experiences identifying someone without stalking them. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-02D-A.bribe_success: The payment clears the barrier. Privacy remains unavailable, but passage has a price.
CROSS-02D-A.bribe_failure: The payment is taken and passage refused. The camera has preserved an excellent record of the customer experience.
CROSS-02D-A.terminal_failure: The crossing ends your expedition. The protection camera continues protecting the guard from having to remember anything.

CROSS-02D-B.name: Two Documents, One Person
CROSS-02D-B.desc: At the checkpoint, a trans traveler’s renewed federal passport conflicts with her state ID. The guard says the computer cannot reconcile them. She suggests looking up from the computer.
CROSS-02D-B.passage: You clear the crossing. The woman ahead remains one person, despite the office’s impressive ability to manufacture two problems.
CROSS-02D-B.diversion: You divert. The guard says the alternate road is less direct, a subject on which he has considerable experience.
CROSS-02D-B.permit_receipt: Your permit clears you. The guard accepts that some documents are allowed to agree with their owner. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-02D-B.permit_tag: Your permit clears you. The guard accepts that some documents are allowed to agree with their owner. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-02D-B.bribe_success: The payment opens the barrier. The computer recognizes money with touching flexibility.
CROSS-02D-B.bribe_failure: The payment is taken; passage is refused. Money has been recognized. People remain under review.
CROSS-02D-B.terminal_failure: The crossing ends your expedition. The computer displays no conflict with that outcome.

CROSS-02D-C.name: Screened for Needing Treatment
CROSS-02D-C.desc: The checkpoint advertises ICE-style medical screening. A diabetic man asks about treatment. The guard points to his intake form. “We’ve already established that you need some.”
CROSS-02D-C.passage: You pass. The clinic’s treatment plan remains a very thorough description of why it needs a treatment plan.
CROSS-02D-C.diversion: You divert. The intake desk describes your departure as reduced demand for services.
CROSS-02D-C.permit_receipt: Your permit is accepted. The crossing can process paper considerably faster than it processes people. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-02D-C.permit_tag: Your permit is accepted. The crossing can process paper considerably faster than it processes people. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-02D-C.bribe_success: The payment clears the barrier. The cash receives immediate attention from a specialist.
CROSS-02D-C.bribe_failure: The payment is taken without passage. The office has completed its financial intake.
CROSS-02D-C.terminal_failure: The crossing ends your expedition. The intake form is complete; the service it describes remains missing.

CROSS-03-A.name: Free Speech Has a Cover Charge
CROSS-03-A.desc: At the final crossing, the official calls campaign spending “speech.” He looks at your van full of actual speakers. “We meant the folding kind.”
CROSS-03-A.passage: You cross. Your voices have briefly cleared a market that prefers banknotes.
CROSS-03-A.diversion: You take the diversion. Apparently freedom of speech includes a longer walk to the microphone.
CROSS-03-A.permit_receipt: Your permit clears you. For once, paper gets heard without having a face printed on it. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-03-A.permit_tag: Your permit clears you. For once, paper gets heard without having a face printed on it. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-03-A.bribe_success: The payment opens the barrier. Your money has delivered a concise and persuasive address.
CROSS-03-A.bribe_failure: The money is taken; passage is refused. Your speech has been entered into somebody’s wallet.
CROSS-03-A.terminal_failure: The crossing ends your expedition. The official describes the silence as a healthy marketplace of ideas.

CROSS-03-B.name: Approved Version of the Journey
CROSS-03-B.desc: The crossing office follows Trump’s demand for a more flattering American history. The officer weighs your case folder. “That’s a lot of country that needs improving.”
CROSS-03-B.passage: You cross with the case. The country’s flattering biography has acquired an awkward appendix.
CROSS-03-B.diversion: You detour. The officer starts describing your absence as public satisfaction.
CROSS-03-B.permit_receipt: Your permit clears you. The folder remains inconveniently full. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-03-B.permit_tag: Your permit clears you. The folder remains inconveniently full. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-03-B.bribe_success: The payment opens the barrier. Your story has found a sponsor.
CROSS-03-B.bribe_failure: The payment is kept, but passage is refused. Sponsorship does not include editorial control.
CROSS-03-B.terminal_failure: You cannot complete this crossing. The expedition ends; the official version is already shorter.

CROSS-03-C.name: The Department of Arrivals
CROSS-03-C.desc: The crossing office is copying Trump’s plan to dismantle the Education Department: abolish the desk, announce better service. Your appointment is being held on an upturned bucket.
CROSS-03-C.passage: You cross. The bucket receives no credit for its public service.
CROSS-03-C.diversion: You detour. The bucket is now managing both arrivals and complaints.
CROSS-03-C.permit_receipt: Your permit clears you. The bucket has retained institutional knowledge. One Receipt is used.
CROSS-03-C.permit_tag: Your permit clears you. The bucket has retained institutional knowledge. Your permit tag remains available.
CROSS-03-C.bribe_success: The payment gets you through. A private contractor immediately offers to rent you a second bucket.
CROSS-03-C.bribe_failure: The payment is kept, but passage is refused. The contractor bills for bucket access.
CROSS-03-C.terminal_failure: The crossing cannot be completed. The expedition ends; the bucket has been shortlisted for promotion.

OPEN-JOURNALIST-A.name: Seattle: Added to the Chat
OPEN-JOURNALIST-A.desc: You leave Seattle with five companions and a reporter’s notebook. Trump’s team sent bombing plans to a journalist by accident. You’re hoping your government answers questions nearly as easily.
OPEN-JOURNALIST-A.log_0: The van pulls out. You check the route twice, placing it ahead of the national-security team.

OPEN-JOURNALIST-B.name: Seattle: The Unapproved Edition
OPEN-JOURNALIST-B.desc: Trump wants a more flattering version of American history. You leave Seattle to report the current version. Five companions climb into the van; nobody’s circumstances have been improved by editing.
OPEN-JOURNALIST-B.log_0: You head for D.C. The notebook opens to a blank page, still the most optimistic thing in the van.

OPEN-JOURNALIST-C.name: Seattle: Follow the Money, Slowly
OPEN-JOURNALIST-C.desc: You’re a reporter leaving Seattle with five companions to follow political money to D.C. The billionaires took planes. Your investigation begins by splitting the price of gas.
OPEN-JOURNALIST-C.log_0: The van sets off. Following the money would be easier if it occasionally used a rest stop.

OPEN-LOBBYIST-A.name: Los Angeles: Access, Economy Class
OPEN-LOBBYIST-A.desc: You know how Washington sells access. Unfortunately, your five companions know how much gas costs. You leave Los Angeles for D.C. with lobbying experience and a donor network consisting of the glove box.
OPEN-LOBBYIST-A.log_0: The van heads east. Loose change speaks, mostly when you hit a pothole.

OPEN-LOBBYIST-B.name: Los Angeles: The Unfunded Briefing
OPEN-LOBBYIST-B.desc: You’ve heard the tariff pitch: foreign countries pay. Your crew pays for the supplies. You leave Los Angeles with five companions to explain this accounting problem in D.C., preferably to someone holding the calculator.
OPEN-LOBBYIST-B.log_0: You set out. China has declined to split the gas.

OPEN-LOBBYIST-C.name: Los Angeles: Dinner Not Included
OPEN-LOBBYIST-C.desc: Washington hosts fundraisers where the chicken comes with a senator. You’re taking five companions from Los Angeles to D.C. Your lobbying budget currently covers the chicken, if everybody respects the drumsticks.
OPEN-LOBBYIST-C.log_0: You leave. For once, nobody in the van has to pretend the senator is the interesting part of dinner.

OPEN-ORGANIZER-A.name: Portland: The Public Workforce
OPEN-ORGANIZER-A.desc: DOGE keeps firing public workers and calling it efficiency. You organize five companions for a trip from Portland to D.C. Fitting everyone’s luggage into one van is your first suspiciously public service.
OPEN-ORGANIZER-A.log_0: You set out. Nobody has been fired for pointing out that the cooler needs room.

OPEN-ORGANIZER-B.name: Portland: A Very Small Super PAC
OPEN-ORGANIZER-B.desc: Billionaires get unlimited independent political spending. Your Portland crew gets a jar for gas money. You’re taking five companions to D.C. to see whether six actual mouths can compete with one very large wallet.
OPEN-ORGANIZER-B.log_0: You head east. The gas jar is your treasurer, and it has already called an emergency meeting.

OPEN-ORGANIZER-C.name: Portland: Proof of Doing Things
OPEN-ORGANIZER-C.desc: Congress wants more work paperwork from people seeking benefits. You organize five companions for D.C. Between shifts, bills and this trip, everybody is exhausted. You begin documenting the apparently hypothetical labor.
OPEN-ORGANIZER-C.log_0: You leave Portland. Organizing the receipts has become the only job that doesn’t pay even badly.

OPEN-SATIRIST-A.name: San Diego: The Ocean Kept Its Job
OPEN-SATIRIST-A.desc: Trump renamed the Gulf. You’re a satirist leaving San Diego with five companions to ask D.C. whether changing the name of broke also helps. The van votes for “temporarily presidential.”
OPEN-SATIRIST-A.log_0: You set out. The newly prestigious budget still requires cheap gas.

OPEN-SATIRIST-B.name: San Diego: Please Stop Helping
OPEN-SATIRIST-B.desc: The government accidentally sent bombing plans to a journalist. You’re a satirist heading from San Diego to D.C. with five companions. You would like to arrive before reality takes all the good lines.
OPEN-SATIRIST-B.log_0: You leave. The crew agrees to keep trip planning out of the national-security chat.

OPEN-SATIRIST-C.name: San Diego: Straight Man Needed
OPEN-SATIRIST-C.desc: Trump calls defense “war” and says it promotes peace. You’re taking five companions from San Diego to D.C. to ask what food should be renamed before you can afford it.
OPEN-SATIRIST-C.log_0: The van pulls away. Renaming breakfast “economic confidence” has left everyone hungry for details.

OPEN-STAFFER-A.name: Sacramento: The Brand Survives
OPEN-STAFFER-A.desc: Trump added “Department of War” to the government’s branding. You’re a staffer leaving Sacramento with five companions to ask D.C. for actual help. You name the van “Reliable.” Nothing mechanical happens.
OPEN-STAFFER-A.log_0: You set out. The new nameplate weighs less than a working spare and accomplishes considerably less.

OPEN-STAFFER-B.name: Sacramento: Inbox Zero, Services Zero
OPEN-STAFFER-B.desc: You’ve seen DOGE turn staffing cuts into a success announcement. You leave Sacramento with five companions to explain what disappeared with the staff. Unlike the announcement, your van has to carry its contents somewhere.
OPEN-STAFFER-B.log_0: You head for D.C. The crew declines to improve legroom by declaring two passengers redundant.

OPEN-STAFFER-C.name: Sacramento: Let Them Eat Guidance
OPEN-STAFFER-C.desc: Congress’s new benefits work rules need explaining. You’re a staffer taking five companions from Sacramento to D.C. Everyone has worked. Nobody has yet managed to eat the guidance document.
OPEN-STAFFER-C.log_0: The trip starts. You pack the forms beside the food, where they can observe the difference.

OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-A.name: San Francisco: Essential Until Deleted
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-A.desc: DOGE calls missing staff “savings.” You know what those people did. You leave San Francisco with five companions and your case for D.C. The van has fewer departments, but you’re keeping the brakes.
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-A.log_0: You set out. Nobody suggests improving fuel efficiency by removing the driver.

OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-B.name: San Francisco: The Wrong Recipient
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-B.desc: You’re a whistleblower heading from San Francisco to D.C. with five companions. Officials say government information must be handled carefully. The bombing-plan group chat apparently had a different onboarding video.
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-B.log_0: You start the trip. The case folder stays shut, an ambitious new standard for information security.

OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-C.name: San Francisco: An Inconvenient Appendix
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-C.desc: Trump wants history to emphasize American greatness. Your whistleblower case concerns the small print. Five companions join you for D.C.; the folder fits badly between everybody’s actual living expenses.
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-C.log_0: You leave San Francisco. The official story has room for improvement, which is awkward for its editors.

END-COLD-A.name: The Insulated Donor
END-COLD-A.desc: Cold exposure ends the journey. The political fundraiser’s dinner is kept warm under little silver lids. Apparently even a potato can obtain better representation.

END-COLD-B.name: Essential Door, Optional Staff
END-COLD-B.desc: Cold exposure ends the expedition. DOGE’s pitch was that fewer public workers meant savings. A locked door has no heating bill and an excellent record of refusing help.

END-COLD-C.name: Energy Dominance, Bring a Coat
END-COLD-C.desc: Cold exposure ends the journey. Trump’s energy-dominance speech continues in a heated room. The microphone is wearing better weather protection than the public.

END-COLLAPSE-BREAKDOWN-A.name: The Invoice Won
END-COLLAPSE-BREAKDOWN-A.desc: The unresolved breakdown ends the expedition. Trump said the tariffs would be paid overseas. The repair quote has spent the whole discussion looking directly at you.

END-COLLAPSE-BREAKDOWN-B.name: A Working Nameplate
END-COLLAPSE-BREAKDOWN-B.desc: The breakdown ends the journey. Washington can rename defense “war” and call the job done. Your van’s newly impressive title still needs a functioning part beneath it.

END-COLLAPSE-BREAKDOWN-C.name: Efficiency’s Roadside Office
END-COLLAPSE-BREAKDOWN-C.desc: The breakdown ends the expedition. DOGE sells the idea that a system works better with less support. The van is now conducting a very long stationary demonstration.

END-COLLAPSE-CROSSING-A.name: Money Clears Customs
END-COLLAPSE-CROSSING-A.desc: The crossing ends the expedition. In American politics, enormous sums move freely as independent speech. Your actual people have encountered a less accommodating barrier.

END-COLLAPSE-CROSSING-B.name: The Office of Not Getting Through
END-COLLAPSE-CROSSING-B.desc: The crossing ends your journey. Trump’s renaming strategy could make the barrier sound stronger. It already stops ordinary people perfectly; the problem may be who counts as the enemy.

END-COLLAPSE-CROSSING-C.name: The Improved Record
END-COLLAPSE-CROSSING-C.desc: The crossing ends the expedition. Trump wants a more flattering national story. The version in which your van never gets through will probably need a smaller font.

END-COLLAPSE-DISEASE-A.name: Illness Has No Upload Button
END-COLLAPSE-DISEASE-A.desc: Illness ends the expedition. Congress wants work documented before more people can keep benefits. Your body has been doing nothing but fight. It has neglected to create a login.

END-COLLAPSE-DISEASE-B.name: The Budget Looks Healthy
END-COLLAPSE-DISEASE-B.desc: Disease ends the journey. Washington can describe projected health-spending cuts as savings. The budget looks much healthier when none of the sick people are drawn on the chart.

END-COLLAPSE-DISEASE-C.name: A Second Opinion From the Slogan
END-COLLAPSE-DISEASE-C.desc: Illness ends the expedition. The MAHA pitch promised health through suspicion of safeguards. The disease has offered no opinion on government and an extremely detailed opinion on bodies.

END-COLLAPSE-HUNGER-A.name: Trickle-Down, Mouth Open
END-COLLAPSE-HUNGER-A.desc: Hunger ends the expedition. Congress cut projected food-aid spending and called it savings. You cannot eat the forecast, although it now contains a very impressive number.

END-COLLAPSE-HUNGER-B.name: Access to Dinner
END-COLLAPSE-HUNGER-B.desc: Hunger ends the journey. Political fundraisers still offer access to lawmakers over dinner. It is a strange country where the chicken comes with someone you must convince you need chicken.

END-COLLAPSE-HUNGER-C.name: A Well-Protected Loaf
END-COLLAPSE-HUNGER-C.desc: Hunger ends the expedition. Trump’s tariff pitch said foreign countries would pay. The food stayed on the shelf, impeccably protected from domestic consumption.

END-COLLAPSE-PANIC-A.name: Nothing to See, Too Much to Hear
END-COLLAPSE-PANIC-A.desc: Panic ends the expedition. Officials who misplaced bombing plans will continue explaining that everyone else is overreacting. You switch off the briefing; it is the first thing to stop escalating.

END-COLLAPSE-PANIC-B.name: The Reassurance Department
END-COLLAPSE-PANIC-B.desc: Panic ends the journey. The government has renamed defense “war” to make everyone feel safer. The word “relax” could probably use a less heavily armed communications team.

END-COLLAPSE-PANIC-C.name: You Have Been Invited to Worry
END-COLLAPSE-PANIC-C.desc: Panic ends the expedition. Another political bulletin declares a national emergency over classroom pronouns. A leaking roof has yet to qualify for this level of concern.

END-COLLAPSE-VEHICLE-A.name: The Vehicle Has Rebranded
END-COLLAPSE-VEHICLE-A.desc: Vehicle condition ends the expedition. Trump gave defense a fiercer name. You could try the same with the van, but “unstoppable” would now be blocking traffic.

END-COLLAPSE-VEHICLE-B.name: A Job Creator
END-COLLAPSE-VEHICLE-B.desc: The van’s condition ends the journey. Tariffs were meant to revive American manufacturing. Staring at the repair costs, you wonder how many new jobs you personally are supposed to take.

END-COLLAPSE-VEHICLE-C.name: The Maintenance Department Is Gone
END-COLLAPSE-VEHICLE-C.desc: Vehicle condition ends the expedition. The DOGE theory says less support produces better performance. Your van has submitted its rebuttal by refusing to move.

END-COLLAPSE-WEATHER-A.name: Weather, Unedited
END-COLLAPSE-WEATHER-A.desc: Weather ends the expedition. Sharpiegate demonstrated how to change a forecast with a pen. Nobody demonstrated how to drive across the correction.

END-COLLAPSE-WEATHER-B.name: The Sovereign Weather System
END-COLLAPSE-WEATHER-B.desc: Weather ends the journey. Trump renamed the Gulf; the weather has declined to update its paperwork. It continues arriving without proof of citizenship.

END-COLLAPSE-WEATHER-C.name: The Prosperity Forecast
END-COLLAPSE-WEATHER-C.desc: Weather ends the expedition. The fossil-fuel speech promises an economy without environmental obstacles. Outside the van, an obstacle has become the entire view.

END-DESTROYED-A.name: America First, Van Last
END-DESTROYED-A.desc: The van is destroyed. The journey ends with American travelers unable to travel. The tariff pitch promised to protect domestic industry; your contribution now appears to be scrap.

END-DESTROYED-B.name: The Department of Scrap
END-DESTROYED-B.desc: The van is destroyed and the expedition ends. Calling it a tank did no more than calling defense “war.” At least the scrap yard uses names that describe the contents.

END-DESTROYED-C.name: An Extremely Efficient Vehicle
END-DESTROYED-C.desc: The van is destroyed. It now uses no fuel, needs no driver and delivers no services. A DOGE presentation could make this the best-performing vehicle you ever owned.

END-FALLBACK-A.name: An Unclassified Ending
END-FALLBACK-A.desc: This account does not say how the journey ended. After the bombing-plan group chat, check the recipient list. The government may have sent the conclusion to a man who sells patio furniture.

END-FALLBACK-B.name: The Official Blank Space
END-FALLBACK-B.desc: The ending is missing from this account. Trump’s preferred, flattering history has competition: this version contains no recorded mistakes at all. An editor somewhere is delighted.

END-FALLBACK-C.name: The Most Efficient Record
END-FALLBACK-C.desc: The record does not establish how the journey ended. DOGE-style accounting could call that a reduction in bad outcomes. It certainly uses less ink than finding out.

END-HEAT-A.name: Local Control of the Thermostat
END-HEAT-A.desc: Heat exposure ends the expedition. Politicians who oppose mandatory worker heat breaks make their case indoors. The thermostat has been allowed to regulate without a public hearing.

END-HEAT-B.name: The Forecast Has Been Corrected
END-HEAT-B.desc: Heat exposure ends the journey. Sharpiegate offered a cheaper approach to bad forecasts: change the map. The sun remains infuriatingly difficult to reach with a marker.

END-HEAT-C.name: Drill, Baby, Stop
END-HEAT-C.desc: Heat exposure ends the expedition. The radio is still celebrating Trump’s energy dominance. Somewhere, the air conditioner cooling that announcement is working very hard.

END-INCOMPLETE-A.name: The Committee Is Still Somewhere Ahead
END-INCOMPLETE-A.desc: This journey is unfinished. In Washington, the donor dinner is still on the calendar. The chicken has secured an appointment; your case is still on the road.

END-INCOMPLETE-B.name: American History, Draft Saved
END-INCOMPLETE-B.desc: The journey is unfinished. Trump’s flattering version of America can wait for an ending. Your current draft still contains people who need things fixed.

END-INCOMPLETE-C.name: Delivery Pending
END-INCOMPLETE-C.desc: The expedition is unfinished. Trump’s tariff pitch promises that someone overseas will pay. Your crew is still waiting for that country to offer a useful driving shift.

END-SANITY-A.name: The Brain Declines the Briefing
END-SANITY-A.desc: You cannot keep going; your sanity is exhausted. Officials who put bombing plans in a group chat will continue lecturing everyone about judgment. Yours has at least recognized an emergency.

END-SANITY-B.name: Renaming the Problem
END-SANITY-B.desc: Your sanity gives out and the journey ends. Trump renamed defense “war.” You try calling this “strategic wellness.” It changes exactly as much.

END-SANITY-C.name: Five Things You Can No Longer Do
END-SANITY-C.desc: Your sanity is exhausted; the expedition ends. DOGE wanted five weekly accomplishments. You have reached the point where “listen to another announcement” cannot make the list.

END-VICTORY-A.name: The Quarter PAC
END-VICTORY-A.desc: You win the final vote. A lobbyist asks which super PAC backed you. You show the laundry change. He looks underneath it for the billionaire.

END-VICTORY-B.name: An Unflattering Success
END-VICTORY-B.desc: You win the hearing. The chair calls it a triumph of American greatness. He is already editing out the part where you had to argue with him.

END-VICTORY-C.name: The Government Did a Thing
END-VICTORY-C.desc: You win the final vote. For once, government responds to the people in front of it. Somewhere in the room, a DOGE enthusiast starts looking for something to unplug.

END-VOTEFAIL-A.name: The Wrong Kind of Speech
END-VOTEFAIL-A.desc: The final vote goes against you. You brought evidence, testimony and an actual journey. The donor envelope brought none of these and gets invited to dinner.

END-VOTEFAIL-B.name: A Less Divisive Ending
END-VOTEFAIL-B.desc: You lose the final vote. The chair invokes Trump’s preferred, uplifting version of America. Your case is removed from the table before the photograph.

END-VOTEFAIL-C.name: Efficiency Achieved
END-VOTEFAIL-C.desc: The final vote rejects your case. A DOGE admirer praises the savings. The government has avoided doing something, after making everybody travel here to ask.

ALLY-01-A.name: The Red Hat Referral
ALLY-01-A.desc: Your outside contact {name} quits helping and joins a MAGA merchandise drive. Their goodbye includes a discount code. Political conversion now has affiliate tracking.
ALLY-01-A.last: That was your last outside contact. The traveling crew remains; your support network is now empty.

ALLY-01-B.name: America First, Contact Last
ALLY-01-B.desc: Your contact {name} drops the trip to sell America First hats. They ask you to reimburse the tariff on the shipment. China has apparently nominated friends and family.
ALLY-01-B.last: No outside allies remain. Nobody in the van has departed because of this message.

ALLY-01-C.name: The Donor Conversion
ALLY-01-C.desc: Your contact {name} stops supporting the trip and takes a job courting super-PAC donors. They still believe in your voice. They’ve simply discovered the volume knob.
ALLY-01-C.last: Your final outside ally has withdrawn. The travelers still present will have to continue without that network.

ALLY-02-A.name: Efficiency Has Arrived
ALLY-02-A.desc: DOGE cuts cost your outside contact {name} their job. They withdraw to find work. Their last assignment was to document the value of documenting their value.
ALLY-02-A.last: That was your last outside contact. The traveling crew remains; your support network is now empty.

ALLY-02-B.name: Nobody to Answer
ALLY-02-B.desc: Your contact {name} loses a public-service job in the DOGE cuts and must stop helping. The agency’s goodbye says to call with questions. They were the person who answered.
ALLY-02-B.last: No outside allies remain. Nobody in the van has departed because of this message.

ALLY-02-C.name: The Merit Vacancy
ALLY-02-C.desc: Your contact {name} loses their job as a contractor scraps its DEI work and must withdraw. The boss announces a new era of merit. His son announces that lunch is ready.
ALLY-02-C.last: Your final outside ally has withdrawn. The travelers still present will have to continue without that network.

ALLY-03-A.name: America Pays First
ALLY-03-A.desc: Your contact {name} takes extra shifts to cover tariff-inflated repair costs and can’t keep helping. They’ve found out which foreign country pays. It’s the one printed on their address.
ALLY-03-A.last: That was your last outside contact. The traveling crew remains; your support network is now empty.

ALLY-03-B.name: Trickle-Down Overtime
ALLY-03-B.desc: Your contact {name} needs extra shifts for medical bills and withdraws. Congress is selling health-budget cuts as savings. They would like to know where the savings get deposited.
ALLY-03-B.last: No outside allies remain. Nobody in the van has departed because of this message.

ALLY-03-C.name: The Food Budget
ALLY-03-C.desc: Your contact {name} takes another shift to cover groceries and stops helping. They watched Congress sell food-aid cuts as independence. They are now independently working Saturday.
ALLY-03-C.last: Your final outside ally has withdrawn. The travelers still present will have to continue without that network.

ALLY-04-A.name: Bipartisan Checkout
ALLY-04-A.desc: Your contact {name} leaves to sell merchandise to rival political rallies. They’ve solved the two-party problem with two card readers.
ALLY-04-A.last: That was your last outside contact. The traveling crew remains; your support network is now empty.

ALLY-04-B.name: The Patriotic Returns Policy
ALLY-04-B.desc: Your contact {name} quits helping to sell Gulf of America souvenirs. They keep the old Gulf of Mexico stock underneath. The ocean has yet to request a refund.
ALLY-04-B.last: No outside allies remain. Nobody in the van has departed because of this message.

ALLY-04-C.name: Emergency Appeal
ALLY-04-C.desc: Your contact {name} leaves to write political fundraising emails. Every message says democracy ends at midnight. Their contract renews monthly.
ALLY-04-C.last: Your final outside ally has withdrawn. The travelers still present will have to continue without that network.

ALLY-05-A.name: The Deep State Group Chat
ALLY-05-A.desc: Your contact {name} sends a video claiming journalists invented the Signal scandal, then blocks the crew. The explanation is now more secure than the bombing chat.
ALLY-05-A.last: That was your last outside contact. The traveling crew remains; your support network is now empty.

ALLY-05-B.name: The Classified Stomach
ALLY-05-B.desc: Your contact {name} decides your criticism of MAHA milk proves you work for the FDA and cuts contact. Your new federal career comes with no salary and several stomach cramps.
ALLY-05-B.last: No outside allies remain. Nobody in the van has departed because of this message.

ALLY-05-C.name: The Tariff Awakening
ALLY-05-C.desc: Your contact {name} says tariffs cannot raise American prices because Trump said China pays. They block you after the crew sends a receipt. Evidence is apparently an import.
ALLY-05-C.last: Your final outside ally has withdrawn. The travelers still present will have to continue without that network.

ALLY-06-A.name: The Protest Barrier
ALLY-06-A.desc: Your contact {name} twists an ankle outside a political fundraiser and withdraws. The accessible entrance was reserved for donors. Equal access was available at the next sponsorship level.
ALLY-06-A.last: That was your last outside contact. The traveling crew remains; your support network is now empty.

ALLY-06-B.name: The Unpaid Department
ALLY-06-B.desc: Your contact {name} hurts their back volunteering after DOGE staffing cuts and must stop helping. They’ve been injured performing a job the government proved nobody needed.
ALLY-06-B.last: No outside allies remain. Nobody in the van has departed because of this message.

ALLY-06-C.name: The Stage of Free Speech
ALLY-06-C.desc: Your contact {name} strains a shoulder hauling equipment for a protest against billionaire political spending. Free speech, it turns out, is heavier when nobody delivers it for you.
ALLY-06-C.last: Your final outside ally has withdrawn. The travelers still present will have to continue without that network.

HEARING-C-A.name: The Two-Minute Citizens
HEARING-C-A.desc: At the D.C. hearing, the chair gives you two minutes. His political donors get three hours over dinner. Apparently chicken needs more representation.
HEARING-C-A.round_1: The first procedural round drains your stamina. The chair explains how valuable everyone’s time is, at length.
HEARING-C-A.round_2: Another round of procedure. The donor-dinner menu arrives before anyone has addressed your case.
HEARING-C-A.round_3: The last procedural round. The chair asks for brevity, then reads the dessert options.
HEARING-C-A.before_vote: You endured the procedure. One vote now decides the case. For a moment, the menu goes face down.
HEARING-C-A.exhausted: You cannot endure the remaining procedure. Your hearing ends before the vote; the dinner reservation survives.

HEARING-C-B.name: Competence, Selectively Required
HEARING-C-B.desc: You reach the D.C. hearing. The chair demands impeccable evidence. A clerk hands him the wrong folder. After the bombing-plan group chat, at least this one contains sandwiches.
HEARING-C-B.round_1: The opening procedural round drains stamina. The chair says the folder was never classified.
HEARING-C-B.round_2: The second round addresses procedure. A clerk removes the sandwiches from the official record.
HEARING-C-B.round_3: The final procedural round. The chair insists nobody was ever in danger of lunch.
HEARING-C-B.before_vote: The procedure is complete. One vote will decide your case, provided they have found the correct folder.
HEARING-C-B.exhausted: You run out of stamina before the vote. The chair has retained enough energy to deny knowing the sandwiches.

HEARING-C-C.name: The Approved Account
HEARING-C-C.desc: At the hearing, the chair invokes Trump’s call for a more flattering American history. Your case concerns the present. He seems annoyed that history is still being manufactured.
HEARING-C-C.round_1: The first procedural round drains stamina. Your difficulties are reclassified as discouraging presentation.
HEARING-C-C.round_2: The second round debates tone. The chair asks whether the unpaid bill could sound more grateful.
HEARING-C-C.round_3: The final procedural round. The bill remains the same size despite extensive editing.
HEARING-C-C.before_vote: You make it through procedure. One vote will decide whether the room can cope with the unflattering version.
HEARING-C-C.exhausted: You cannot finish the hearing. No vote follows. The chair’s preferred account is now conveniently shorter.

HEARING-D-A.name: The Appendix Exception
HEARING-D-A.desc: At the abortion-ban hearing, a nurse explains why hospital lawyers keep getting called during emergencies. The chair announces a study. She asks whether his appendix also waits for peer review.
HEARING-D-A.round_1: The first round drains stamina. The chair asks the nurse to define urgent. She points to the clock. He requests a second opinion.
HEARING-D-A.round_2: The second round establishes that time is critical. The committee takes a recess to decide which time.
HEARING-D-A.round_3: The last procedural round. The study receives an extension. Nobody has worked out how to give one to a patient.
HEARING-D-A.before_vote: You finish the procedure. One vote decides your case. The study will get considerably longer to make up its mind.
HEARING-D-A.exhausted: You cannot finish the rounds, so there is no vote. The chair schedules a study of why people keep running out of time.

HEARING-D-B.name: Nothing to Hide
HEARING-D-B.desc: At the hearing on Flock misuse, the chair says innocent people have nothing to hide. A clerk starts describing his own camera records. The chair discovers executive privacy before the first sandwich shop.
HEARING-D-B.round_1: The first procedural round drains stamina. The chair distinguishes public safety from information about his lunch.
HEARING-D-B.round_2: The next round discusses oversight. He demands oversight of whoever overlooked his right to have no oversight.
HEARING-D-B.round_3: The last procedural round. His sandwich has been sealed from the public record.
HEARING-D-B.before_vote: You endure the procedure. One vote will decide the case. The chair’s lunch has already received full protection.
HEARING-D-B.exhausted: You cannot finish the rounds. The hearing ends before a vote; the chair calls this a useful reduction in surveillance.

HEARING-D-C.name: Prior Authorization to Be Heard
HEARING-D-C.desc: The hearing concerns Medicare Advantage denials of qualifying care. The chair asks whether the patients appealed. A nurse holds up the appeal form. “Yes. It made a full recovery.”
HEARING-D-C.round_1: The opening round drains stamina. The chair asks whether the appeal form needs another appeal form.
HEARING-D-C.round_2: The second round reviews the review. The nurse adds a chair for the paperwork; it has been here longest.
HEARING-D-C.round_3: The final procedural round. The paperwork is declared fit to return to work.
HEARING-D-C.before_vote: You finish the rounds. One vote now decides the case. The form is excused from further examination.
HEARING-D-C.exhausted: You cannot finish the rounds, so no vote follows. The chair asks the paperwork whether it can continue without you.

COND-CLEAR-A.name: Unregulated Sunshine
COND-CLEAR-A.desc: Clear skies. The radio credits Trump’s energy agenda. The sun declines the cabinet appointment.
COND-CLEAR-A.continuing: The clear weather continues. The sun has not returned the communications team’s calls.
COND-CLEAR-A.relief: The clear spell ends. Apparently the sun serves at its own pleasure.

COND-CLEAR-B.name: Forecast Approved
COND-CLEAR-B.desc: Clear weather gives the crew a break. Nobody has needed to improve the forecast with a Sharpie.
COND-CLEAR-B.continuing: The sky remains clear without editorial assistance.
COND-CLEAR-B.relief: The weather changes. The marker is referred to the complaints department.

COND-CLEAR-C.name: The Public Option
COND-CLEAR-C.desc: Clear skies. DOGE fired forecasters; the remaining staff called this one. The sunshine has been given until Monday to explain what it accomplished.
COND-CLEAR-C.continuing: The forecast continues to match the sky. An unfashionable government outcome.
COND-CLEAR-C.relief: The clear spell ends; check the actual new forecast, not the applause.

COND-COLD-A.name: A Private Climate
COND-COLD-A.desc: Cold grips the route. The fossil-fuel lobby calls its dinner an energy-security event. You’d like to attend the room-temperature portion.
COND-COLD-A.continuing: The cold continues. Energy security still appears to be indoors.
COND-COLD-A.relief: The cold eases. Your fingers regain the ability to disagree with a press release.

COND-COLD-B.name: Frozen Federal Assets
COND-COLD-B.desc: The cold settles in beside a reduced-hours public visitor center. DOGE saved on heating the office by removing the people who opened it.
COND-COLD-B.continuing: Cold persists. The locked visitor center is achieving excellent energy savings.
COND-COLD-B.relief: Conditions improve. The door remains a separate policy problem.

COND-COLD-C.name: Personal Responsibility, Insulated
COND-COLD-C.desc: The temperature drops. A donor’s billboard praises personal responsibility. Your blanket would like to know whether that comes in fleece.
COND-COLD-C.continuing: The cold continues. You add another layer without forming a super PAC.
COND-COLD-C.relief: The cold eases. Warmth arrives without requesting your billing address.

COND-COLDEXPOSURE-A.name: The Private Warmth Sector
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-A.desc: Cold exposure is now causing harm. The political donor’s promise of opportunity offers several square feet of cardboard. You investigate its insulation policy.
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-A.continuing: The cold remains harmful. Seek protection; donor enthusiasm has no measurable heat output.
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-A.relief: Exposure is relieved. Your hands regain the ability to put the leaflet down.

COND-COLDEXPOSURE-B.name: Essential Services, Optional Hours
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-B.desc: Cold exposure is harming the crew near a closed public rest facility. The staffing cuts saved a salary. The door is still costing everybody else.
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-B.continuing: The cold remains dangerous. Find protection; the locked door will not reconsider its staffing level.
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-B.relief: Exposure eases after protection. The closed facility retains its perfect attendance record.

COND-COLDEXPOSURE-C.name: Heating the Debate
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-C.desc: Prolonged cold is now harming the crew. A politician on the radio promises to heat up the energy debate. You hold a hand over the speaker. Nothing.
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-C.continuing: The cold is still causing harm. Get actual protection; the speech has reached its third insulated anecdote.
COND-COLDEXPOSURE-C.relief: Exposure is relieved. The radio can return to being merely irritating.

COND-HEAT-A.name: The Freedom to Sweat
COND-HEAT-A.desc: A heat wave settles over the route. Politicians call mandatory water breaks overreach. Your sweat appears to be a grassroots protest.
COND-HEAT-A.continuing: The heat persists. The protest has spread to every seat.
COND-HEAT-A.relief: The heat eases. The seats begin negotiating a return to normal relations.

COND-HEAT-B.name: Drill, Baby, Swelter
COND-HEAT-B.desc: The radio plays “Drill, baby, drill” over another heat warning. The dashboard has begun producing its own plastic reserves.
COND-HEAT-B.continuing: The heat continues. The steering wheel remains too patriotic to touch.
COND-HEAT-B.relief: Temperatures ease. The dashboard declines further energy development.

COND-HEAT-C.name: Executive Air Conditioning
COND-HEAT-C.desc: A heat wave arrives. On the radio, an official opposes worker heat rules from a room you can hear being air-conditioned.
COND-HEAT-C.continuing: The heat persists. The studio thermostat remains outside the debate.
COND-HEAT-C.relief: The heat breaks. The official’s jacket has survived without comment.

COND-HEATEXPOSURE-A.name: The Cost of Local Control
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-A.desc: Prolonged heat is now harming the crew. Opponents of mandatory heat breaks promised freedom. Your body has mistaken it for permission to shut down.
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-A.continuing: Heat is still causing harm. Get protection and attend to the crew; the slogan has no cooling setting.
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-A.relief: Heat exposure is relieved. Your body accepts the change without a constitutional challenge.

COND-HEATEXPOSURE-B.name: Policy-Proof Temperature
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-B.desc: Heat exposure is causing damage. The Sharpiegate approach has failed: you can change a line on a map, but the steering wheel still burns.
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-B.continuing: The heat remains harmful. The marker stays comfortably cool in the glove box.
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-B.relief: Exposure is relieved. You return the marker to a job within its qualifications.

COND-HEATEXPOSURE-C.name: An Energy Success Story
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-C.desc: The heat has become dangerous. A roadside “energy dominance” banner flaps above the van. It is providing the most useful part of the policy: shade.
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-C.continuing: Heat is still harming the crew. Stay protected; the banner is not medical care.
COND-HEATEXPOSURE-C.relief: Exposure eases. The banner’s brief public-service career ends.

COND-HUNGER-A.name: Trickle-Down Lunch
COND-HUNGER-A.desc: Food is running short. Congress has cut projected food-aid spending. Someone holds an empty bowl under the radio, just in case the savings trickle down.
COND-HUNGER-A.continuing: Hunger continues. You turn the bowl around to improve reception.
COND-HUNGER-A.relief: Food relieves the hunger. It arrives through an actual person, a supply the radio had overlooked.

COND-HUNGER-B.name: The Protected Pantry
COND-HUNGER-B.desc: Food runs low while Trump’s tariff pitch plays on the radio. The crew has been successfully protected from the contents of several shops.
COND-HUNGER-B.continuing: Hunger persists. China has not sent sandwiches.
COND-HUNGER-B.relief: You eat. International trade briefly becomes a matter of chewing.

COND-HUNGER-C.name: Donor-Class Calories
COND-HUNGER-C.desc: Supplies are low. A political fundraiser advertises dinner with a senator. The crew would settle for dinner without one.
COND-HUNGER-C.continuing: Hunger continues. Access to the senator appears to be the expensive part of the chicken.
COND-HUNGER-C.relief: You get enough food. The absence of a senator improves the meal.

COND-ILLNESS-A.name: An Unfunded Body
COND-ILLNESS-A.desc: Illness hits the journey. Congress calls health-budget cuts a saving. Your body would like to see the return address for whatever it caught.
COND-ILLNESS-A.continuing: The illness continues. Your body remains inconveniently outside the budget’s success metrics.
COND-ILLNESS-A.relief: The illness clears. Recovery has happened despite the running commentary.

COND-ILLNESS-B.name: Natural Selection of a Chair
COND-ILLNESS-B.desc: Illness interrupts the trip. A MAHA advertisement offers to help your body heal itself. The crew starts with a chair that makes fewer promises.
COND-ILLNESS-B.continuing: The illness persists. The miracle advertisement remains in excellent health.
COND-ILLNESS-B.relief: The illness clears. The chair asks for no testimonial.

COND-ILLNESS-C.name: The Medical Work Requirement
COND-ILLNESS-C.desc: Illness slows the crew. The radio explains Congress’s new Medicaid work requirements. Your immune system would like its overtime recorded.
COND-ILLNESS-C.continuing: You remain unwell. The immune system has not taken a lunch break or received a supervisor’s signature.
COND-ILLNESS-C.relief: The illness clears. Your body submits its completed assignment by getting out of the chair.

COND-SMOKE-A.name: Now With More Freedom
COND-SMOKE-A.desc: Smoke hangs over the road. The radio celebrates rolling back environmental rules. You close the windows on the celebration.
COND-SMOKE-A.continuing: The smoke persists. Freedom has developed a taste you can’t get out of your mouth.
COND-SMOKE-A.relief: The smoke clears. Breathing briefly returns to being a background activity.

COND-SMOKE-B.name: Visible Deregulation
COND-SMOKE-B.desc: Smoke reduces visibility. Officials say environmental rules hold business back. The horizon appears to have been released from its obligations.
COND-SMOKE-B.continuing: Smoke continues. Your next landmark has exercised its freedom to disappear.
COND-SMOKE-B.relief: The air clears enough to see farther. The horizon resumes public service.

COND-SMOKE-C.name: The Museum of Clean Air
COND-SMOKE-C.desc: Smoke settles over the route. A museum follows Trump’s flattering-history directive with an exhibit celebrating American industry. You are inhaling the deleted scenes.
COND-SMOKE-C.continuing: The smoke persists. The souvenir has entered through a gap in the window seal.
COND-SMOKE-C.relief: The air clears. You decline the gift shop’s take-home edition.

COND-STORM-A.name: The Map Is Dry
COND-STORM-A.desc: A storm lashes the van. You consider the Sharpiegate approach, but there isn’t enough marker to cross out the sky.
COND-STORM-A.continuing: Rain continues. The forecast map is the only dry territory you control.
COND-STORM-A.relief: The storm passes. The sky has corrected itself without a press conference.

COND-STORM-B.name: The Energy Announcement
COND-STORM-B.desc: Heavy rain hits as the radio celebrates climate-policy rollbacks. The announcement is waterproof. The passenger-side window isn’t.
COND-STORM-B.continuing: The storm continues. You move the radio away from the leak so optimism can remain operational.
COND-STORM-B.relief: The rain eases. The leak remains available for the next victory speech.

COND-STORM-C.name: Patriotically Wet
COND-STORM-C.desc: The storm does not care what Trump calls the Gulf. Water arrives under both names and immediately ignores your towel.
COND-STORM-C.continuing: Rain keeps coming. You have recognized its sovereignty over the seat cushion.
COND-STORM-C.relief: The storm ends. The towel requests disaster assistance.

play.travel_help: Set your pace and information diet, then travel. The road runs briefly before stopping at your next decision. Watch the gauges; choices and repairs report their actual costs.
play.outfit_help: Your starting funds pay for the selected cart. There are no free supplies underneath it. Add or remove food, water, parts and protection; you may leave empty. Purchases are charged when you depart. A spare is consumed only when fitted.
play.resupply_help: Choose supplies, parts and protection, then review the total. Buying charges your cash immediately and returns you to town. Leaving the store does not charge you. A spare is consumed only when fitted.
play.review_help: Check what you are carrying and what you will have left. These purchases happen when you start the journey.
play.capacity: Supplies are capped at 20. Extra provisions above that limit do not carry over.
play.pack_empty: A starter load is selected. Every item comes out of your funds—change or remove anything.
play.fuel_food_help: Food and water add shared supply units. Water jugs also reduce heat exposure.
play.vehicle_help: One matching spare is consumed when fitted. Without one, repairs may cost cash, time, or vehicle condition.
play.ppe_help: Protective gear softens specific weather penalties. Select an item to see what it protects against.
play.docs_help: A press pass can help at permit checks. A legal fund adds credibility.
play.pace_help: Steady adds no pace fatigue. Heated costs 1 Sanity and Blitz costs 2 per 5 hours of driving; unfinished fatigue carries into later drives. Weather and vehicle condition affect distance, and activities use available driving time.
play.diet_help: Your information diet is your news intake. Its Sanity effect applies once per day. Quieter coverage supports Sanity; doomscrolling improves your chances of finding receipts but costs Sanity.
play.locked: Today’s settings are locked until the next day.
play.weather_help: These modifiers describe the current weather. Conditions can change as the next day begins. Protective gear can replace some penalties.
play.cred_help: Credibility rises by listening to locals, documenting events and useful encounter choices. Misleading claims and some shortcuts reduce it. It affects the final hearing.
play.morale_help: Morale is the crew’s shared spirit. Care, rest, cooperation and successful encounters raise it. Losses, departures, hunger and difficult choices lower it.
play.sanity_help: News intake, rushed travel, illness and stressful choices can lower sanity. Quiet news, camp recovery and helpful encounters restore it. A warning appears at 2 or less.
play.health_help: Health falls through injury, hunger and hard physical work. Care, recovery days and some encounters restore it. At zero the journey ends.
play.supplies_help: Food and water share a 20-unit capacity. Travel, weather, care and barter use supplies. Buy provisions, gather outside town, trade or work for food to replenish them.
play.allies_help: Allies are outside supporters, separate from the people in your van. Helpful encounter choices build support; choices that spend or alienate support reduce it. Allies contribute to the final hearing.
play.travel_wait: Watch the road. Your next decision is approaching.
play.travel_done: You made it through this stretch.
play.journal_empty: The journal fills as your journey unfolds.
play.repair_help: Choose a repair and review its cost before fitting a part or calling for help.
play.danger: Sanity is in the danger zone
play.danger_help: Your sanity is 2 or lower. Consider rest or a quieter information diet before pushing on.
play.unknown_log: Trail conditions changed. Check the latest resource receipt.
play.seed_hint: Use a run code to replay a journey. Leave the generated code as-is for this trip.
play.receipts_help: Receipts are evidence for your D.C. hearing. Earn them from encounter choices showing Receipts +1. Each receipt you keep adds 8 points to your journey score. They decrease only when a choice explicitly spends one. Your character and news diet affect the displayed chance of finding an extra receipt.

journey.forecast_caveat: Weather, care and choices can change this estimate.
journey.forecast_stable: Recent completed travel days did not reduce supply stock. Keep a reserve for weather, care and delays.
journey.camp_forecast: These are the recovery effects at your current levels. One stationary day passes; weather and hunger can also affect the crew. Rest helps every present crew member.
journey.capacity: The van holds 20 supply units. Remove surplus packs before checkout; you will not be charged for goods you cannot carry.
journey.shop_help: Restock for the next leg. Your current supplies and spares are already in the van.
journey.rolling: On the road. Travel continues until a decision, arrival or danger needs you.
journey.arrival_help: The road can wait. Restock, exchange goods or hear what the locals know before departing.
journey.town_heartland: The grain elevator has been renamed the Center for Agricultural Innovation. It still buys grain. Neighbors recommend a spare tire for the rural stretch ahead; volunteers run the aid table. Your notes add credibility.
journey.town_rustbelt: The old mill is an Innovation District now. The library still has working outlets. Locals recommend a spare battery; the exchange board lists today’s offer. You record their account.
journey.town_beltway: The community center is accepting feedback about the feedback process. Neighbors point out the actual aid desk around the back. Gather your evidence and rest before the D.C. hearing.
journey.care_body: The medic offers {name} treatment before asking about payment. You briefly suspect an elaborate sting.
journey.care_critical: {name} is critically unwell. Pressing on without care now will kill them. If this is your character, the journey will end.
journey.shelter_action: Leave a companion with the medics · Crew member leaves · {effects}
journey.defer_action: Keep driving without care · {effects} · Illness may worsen
journey.care_hint: Each choice takes one hour. Care costs two supplies. Only companions can leave with the medics. A full recovery day clears illness.
journey.care_helped: {name} is fit to travel. Two supplies: the least insulting medical bill in America.
journey.care_sheltered: {name} stays in shelter and leaves the traveling crew alive. The incident is cleared.
journey.care_deferred: You continue without care. {name} remains unwell, and the incident can worsen.
journey.care_lost: {name} has died after the crew continued without care. Their place in the van is empty.
journey.mission: Bring the crew and evidence of institutional nonsense to a public hearing in D.C. Gather receipts, build credibility and find allies along the way. Arriving is only part of it: the crew needs enough sanity to be heard.
journey.multiplier: Affects final scoring, not your travel speed or starting cash.
journey.vote_exhausted: The crew cannot withstand the full hearing at these levels. Recover before proceeding.
journey.vote_chance: Estimated chance of passing the final vote: {chance}%.
journey.vote_basis: Evidence, credibility, allies, health, morale and supplies contribute to the journey score. Days and resolved encounters add experience; breakdowns subtract from it. The crew needs enough sanity to complete the hearing. The final vote is uncertain.
journey.vote_won: The hearing passed. Your crew’s account is on the record in D.C.
journey.vote_lost: The hearing ended without a win. The journey and the people who helped still count.
journey.forecast: Recent supply use: about {days} days of stock. Conditions and choices can change this.
journey.forecast_wait: Supply outlook appears after the first travel day. Carry a reserve for weather, care and delays.
journey.abandon_explanation: This ends the current journey and saves its story. You can start a new trip or load a separate manual save.
journey.abandoned_story: {name} chose to end the trail here with {crew}. Your journey and everyone who traveled with you remain in the journal.
journey.player_lost: You have died after continuing without care. Your journey ends here.
journey.trade_help: Choose an exchange. The community can make one trade with your crew at this stop.

trail.shop_help: Supply shop. Buy food, water, spare parts and protective gear with cash at this stop.
trail.trade_help: Community trading. Exchange goods or work for supplies; local offers are available once per stop.
trail.repair_context: The van cannot continue. Parts and local contacts near {town} offer these routes back onto the road.
trail.repair_radio: Call local radio; work in exchange for repairs
trail.repair_help: A fitted spare is consumed. Buying outside town includes $10 delivery. Barter consumes four supplies. Radio contacts arrange a used part in exchange for four hours of work, costing sanity and morale. The radio option remains available without cash or spares.
trail.repaired: The {part} is fitted. The crew checks the van before continuing.
trail.gather_help: Outside town, gather once every three completed days. Choose a short forage or harder work with more food. In towns, choose one paid or food-for-work offer per stop. Supplies cannot exceed 20; unavailable choices show their costs before you commit.
trail.work_supplies: Sort donations for a food parcel
trail.forage_done: Your guide identifies what can be gathered safely. The crew returns with food and a clearer head.
trail.glean_done: The farmer shares the harvest. Lifting and carrying have taken a physical toll.
trail.work_supplies_done: The donation shelves are stocked and the crew receives an agreed food parcel.
trail.work_cash_done: The unloading shift is complete. Payment goes directly into the crew’s cash reserve.
trail.gather_wait: Gathering available again in {days} travel days.
trail.work_done: You have completed this stop’s work offer. More offers await in the next town.
trail.fact_note: Local facts are sourced. The resident and their commentary are fictional.
trail.care_reason_0: {name} feels sick after a MAHA raw-milk sample. The vendor blames the deep state inside their stomach.
trail.care_reason_1: {name} is dehydrated. The unloading boss crossed out the heat warning with a Sharpie. Apparently the sun doesn’t take corrections.
trail.care_reason_2: {name} stayed up listing five accomplishments for a DOGE-inspired boss. Exhausted, they submit a sixth: unpaid overtime.
trail.care_reason_3: {name} vomits after a MAHA wellness sample. The vendor cites ‘unpublished research.’ They publish a rebuttal into his sample bucket.
trail.care_reason_4: {name} lost sleep navigating a road with three patriotic names. None of them was the exit you needed.
trail.care_reason_5: {name} spent the night disputing a repair tariff. They’re exhausted. The trade war has secured a decisive victory over bedtime.
trail.care_reason_6: {name} is exhausted from a temp-job Signal chat. The boss added strangers, leaked the door code, and took inspiration from the cabinet.
trail.care_reason_7: {name} strains their back hauling donated food after USDA delivery cuts. Washington has replaced a delivery budget with their spine.
trail.satire_note: The roadside scene, dialogue and resource prices are fictional satire inspired by this documented episode.

ally_loss.title: Word from your allies
ally_loss.reason_0: {name} quits for MAGA. Their goodbye text includes a discount code for red hats. Even the betrayal has a checkout page.
ally_loss.reason_1: {name} is laid off in a DOGE-style cut. They leave to job-hunt. Efficiency has created forty hours of unpaid work.
ally_loss.reason_2: A repair tariff forces {name} to quit helping and take evening shifts. “They said China would pay. China can cover my fucking shift.”
ally_loss.reason_3: {name} quits to sell Trump merch. They promise to keep fighting fascism after they’ve cleared the inventory.
ally_loss.reason_4: {name} sends a Truth Social rant, says “do your own research,” then blocks you. Peer review completed.
ally_loss.reason_5: {name} sprains their ankle protesting and heads home. “Tell Washington I’ve filed a motion to sit the fuck down.”

hearing.arrival_body: Now make them listen. Your crew gathers its folders outside the hearing room.
hearing.preparation_body: The clerk eyes your folders. “State your case. If the committee needs more, it will ask.”
hearing.rest_warning: Your crew looks worn thin. “A breather first?” someone whispers. The committee has never mistaken exhaustion for a reason to stop talking.
hearing.guarantee: The votes are promised. Your crew still has to stay on its feet long enough to claim them.
hearing.opening_question: The chair asks you to summarize the evidence. Preferably without referring to any of it.
hearing.followup_question: The committee requests clarification on the parts that were already clear.
hearing.challenge_question: One final question: can you prove this matters to someone in this room?
hearing.opening_positive: Your receipts survive the first attempt to misfile them.
hearing.opening_neutral: Your evidence enters the record. The record promises to get back to you.
hearing.opening_negative: The chair calls your evidence anecdotal. There are binders of anecdotes.
hearing.followup_positive: An ally confirms your account. The committee briefly mistakes this for consensus.
hearing.followup_neutral: Your answer is accepted as an answer. Its contents remain under review.
hearing.followup_negative: The chair objects: those facts were not in the briefing.
hearing.challenge_positive: A receipt is entered into the record. Accidentally.
hearing.challenge_neutral: The committee acknowledges your point without specifying which one.
hearing.challenge_negative: The chair asks whether the problem has considered solving itself.
hearing.committee_wait: The chair checks whether there is time for another question.
hearing.called: The committee calls another round. Your crew returns to the microphone.
hearing.no_questions: The chair looks around. The committee is satisfied. “No further questions. Clerk, call the vote.”
hearing.closed_body: Your case is complete. The clerk is ready to announce the vote.
hearing.vote_wait: The clerk opens the decision. Your crew waits.
hearing.passed_body: Your evidence is heard. The crew takes a breath; this time, the record requires a response.
hearing.failed_body: The committee thanks you for participating in its decision not to act.
hearing.secured_body: The chair looks around for an objection. None comes. “The ayes have it.” Your crew finally lets go of the folders.
hearing.exhausted_body: The next answer never comes. Companions gather the folders and help each other out. The clerk closes the record without a vote.
hearing.preparation_ready: Your crew trades a last look. The folders are in order. The committee is less promising.
hearing.preparation_supplies: Before you go in, the crew will break into the supplies for a bite and a steadier grip on the folders.
hearing.preparation_cash: Before you go in, the crew will buy a bite to eat. Apparently testimony is hungry work.

jobs.headline: JOBS ARE COMING
jobs.copy: The sign has a permanent position.

ORDER-DEREGULATE-A.title: Peace, Now With More War
ORDER-DEREGULATE-A.activation: The government promotes “Department of War” branding. The spokesperson calls it peace through strength. Your van would settle for peace through a working alternator.
ORDER-DEREGULATE-A.expiration: The reorganization event ends. The van has retained its original, less threatening name.

ORDER-DEREGULATE-B.title: Two Names, One Purchase Order
ORDER-DEREGULATE-B.activation: Trump’s War Department branding brings another reorganization. Officials order new signs before checking the equipment. Your van has nominated its rattle for a leadership position.
ORDER-DEREGULATE-B.expiration: The event expires. The rattle is demoted to a maintenance issue.

ORDER-DEREGULATE-C.title: The Branding Campaign
ORDER-DEREGULATE-C.activation: Officials explain that calling defense “war” will project strength. The crew tries calling the van “a tank.” The suspension files an immediate objection.
ORDER-DEREGULATE-C.expiration: The branding event ends. The van accepts a return to civilian duties.

ORDER-GAG-A.title: A Very Dangerous Index
ORDER-GAG-A.activation: Book-panic bulletin: officials copy Trump’s ban on classroom “indoctrination.” The approved reading list arrives pre-approved, with instructions on how freely to discuss it.
ORDER-GAG-A.expiration: The panic recedes. A librarian quietly moves the books back where people can accidentally learn things.

ORDER-GAG-B.title: The classical refund
ORDER-GAG-B.activation: Trump’s architecture order prefers classical designs for covered federal buildings. A rest-stop owner copies it with cardboard columns around the snack machine. One blocks the coin return. It now serves the grandeur of Western civilization. It no longer serves coins.
ORDER-GAG-B.expiration: The bulletin ends. The owner moves a column and gets their test coin back. The machine manages this without consulting an architect.

ORDER-GAG-C.title: The Pronoun Emergency
ORDER-GAG-C.activation: Officials announce another emergency about gender in schools. The roof still leaks. Nobody has established the puddle’s biological sex.
ORDER-GAG-C.expiration: The bulletin expires. The puddle has acquired a second bucket and no political affiliation.

ORDER-MILITARIZE-A.title: Freedom of Movement, Subject to Movement
ORDER-MILITARIZE-A.activation: Checkpoint bulletin: officials invoke Trump’s border-security rhetoric to add another road inspection. The officer asks why free citizens are always trying to go somewhere.
ORDER-MILITARIZE-A.expiration: The extra inspections end. Your destination is once again a place rather than an explanation.

ORDER-MILITARIZE-B.title: America, Please Hold
ORDER-MILITARIZE-B.activation: Trump-style extreme vetting demands proof you belong here. The van’s registration, your accent and your patience are called forward separately.
ORDER-MILITARIZE-B.expiration: The restriction expires. Your patience is still waiting to have its documents returned.

ORDER-MILITARIZE-C.title: The Domestic Border
ORDER-MILITARIZE-C.activation: Officials bring “extreme vetting” to another stretch of road. Your crew explains you’re already in America. The guard says that’s what everyone says.
ORDER-MILITARIZE-C.expiration: The order ends. The road stops interviewing its users.

ORDER-SHUTDOWN-A.title: Essential, Unpaid
ORDER-SHUTDOWN-A.activation: Shutdown bulletin: Congress has run out of agreement. Federal workers are asked to keep being essential on an optional-salary basis.
ORDER-SHUTDOWN-A.expiration: The shutdown ends. Paychecks may resume pretending this was a scheduling problem.

ORDER-SHUTDOWN-B.title: Open for Contributions
ORDER-SHUTDOWN-B.activation: The government shuts down. Services close; political fundraising emails continue arriving. Apparently the donation button is essential infrastructure.
ORDER-SHUTDOWN-B.expiration: Services reopen. Nobody has needed to reboot the donation button.

ORDER-SHUTDOWN-C.title: Hostage Negotiations
ORDER-SHUTDOWN-C.activation: Congress fails to keep the government open. Your next meal has been invited to participate in the negotiations. It wasn’t given a chair.
ORDER-SHUTDOWN-C.expiration: The shutdown ends. The food budget is released without a thank-you note.

ORDER-TARIFFS-A.title: Foreign Aid, Domestic Wallet
ORDER-TARIFFS-A.activation: Trump’s tariff message says foreign countries will pay. Your grocery bill has volunteered to be a foreign country.
ORDER-TARIFFS-A.expiration: The tariff event ends. Your wallet would like its citizenship restored.

ORDER-TARIFFS-B.title: The Importer Is You
ORDER-TARIFFS-B.activation: Another tariff bulletin promises to punish overseas producers. At the shop, the punishment is itemized beneath your bread.
ORDER-TARIFFS-B.expiration: The event expires. The bread is released into your custody.

ORDER-TARIFFS-C.title: Protected From Purchasing
ORDER-TARIFFS-C.activation: Officials announce protection for American consumers through higher import taxes. The food remains safely on the shelf, beyond the reach of American consumers.
ORDER-TARIFFS-C.expiration: The tariff event passes. You and the shelf resume diplomatic relations.

ORDER-TAXCUTS-A.title: Education Has Left the Building
ORDER-TAXCUTS-A.activation: The education department is eliminated. Officials promise to preserve learning. The exit sign has been assigned the remaining teaching hours.
ORDER-TAXCUTS-A.expiration: The order ends. The exit sign returns to its specialist subject.

ORDER-TAXCUTS-B.title: School of Hard Cuts
ORDER-TAXCUTS-B.activation: The education department closes. Students are directed to the school of hard knocks. It is already charging for the door.
ORDER-TAXCUTS-B.expiration: The order expires. The school of hard knocks keeps your application fee.

ORDER-TAXCUTS-C.title: Discover It Yourself
ORDER-TAXCUTS-C.activation: Officials eliminate the education department. The announcement calls it empowerment. The teacher begins explaining long division with the remaining half of a pencil.
ORDER-TAXCUTS-C.expiration: The order ends. The pencil requests a colleague.
